questions.explanation: Passar a means to start doing, voltar a means to do again and estar a marks an action in progress.

questions.prompt: Complete with the verb that builds the expression for spending all your time on something: 'Ele ___ a vida a comentar publicações.'
questions.explanation: Passar a vida a plus an infinitive is a fixed expression criticising excess.

questions.prompt: Complete with the verb meaning to delete something from a phone: 'Acabei por ___ duas aplicações que só me roubavam tempo.'
questions.explanation: Apagar is the everyday verb for deleting a file or an application, and after acabar por the verb stays in the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Build the European Portuguese for: 'I decided to stop using that app.'
questions.explanation: Deixar de keeps its preposition even when it follows another verb such as decidir.

questions.prompt: Listen and fill in the word you hear: 'Passo a vida a olhar para o ___ sem razão nenhuma.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Passo a vida a olhar para o telemóvel sem razão nenhuma.', which means 'I spend all my time looking at my phone for no reason at all.'
questions.audioText: Passo a vida a olhar para o telemóvel sem razão nenhuma.

questions.prompt: Say it in Portuguese, in writing: 'I catch myself losing hours without realising.'
questions.answer: Dou por mim a perder horas sem dar conta.
questions.explanation: 'I catch myself losing hours without realising.' is 'Dou por mim a perder horas sem dar conta.'

activities.title: Too much screen time
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend complains about screen time and you answer using the lesson's periphrases.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Viste o relatório do tempo de ecrã desta semana? O meu foi assustador.
lines.en: Did you see this week's screen time report? Mine was frightening.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: O meu também. Passo a vida a olhar para o telemóvel sem motivo.
lines.en: Mine too. I spend all my time looking at my phone for no reason.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E fazes alguma coisa para mudar isso?
lines.en: And are you doing anything to change that?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Deixei de levar o telemóvel para o quarto à noite.
lines.en: I stopped taking my phone into the bedroom at night.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Isso resulta mesmo?
lines.en: Does that really work?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Resulta, mas às vezes dou por mim a ver vídeos até tarde na mesma.
lines.en: It does, but sometimes I still catch myself watching videos until late.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E as aplicações? Ainda tens todas?
lines.en: And the apps? Do you still have them all?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não, acabei por apagar duas. Nem tudo o que lá se lê vale o tempo.
lines.en: No, I ended up deleting two. Not everything you read there is worth the time.

days.title: Free time and culture
days.objective: Suggest and react to cultural plans, using vale a pena, estar a dar, apetecer and dar um salto a.
days.paretoFocus: Making and answering suggestions is what free time conversation actually consists of, and apetecer is the verb Portuguese uses instead of 'feel like'.
drills: Write three suggestions with vale a pena plus an infinitive and a reason for each.
Answer three invitations, one accepting and two refusing politely with apetecer.
Describe your last cultural outing in four sentences.

items: How does apetecer work grammatically compared with the English 'feel like'?
Which expression says a film is currently showing?
How do you say it is worth going early?

activities.title: Tempos livres e programas culturais
activities.intro: Apetecer works like gostar in reverse: the thing you fancy is the subject and you appear as an indirect pronoun, apetece-me. Dar um salto a means to pop over somewhere briefly, vale a pena plus an infinitive recommends something, and estar a dar says a film or show is on.

items.hr: Vale a pena ver a exposição, está lá até ao fim do mês.
items.en: The exhibition is worth seeing, it is there until the end of the month.
items.note: valer a pena + infinitivo

items.hr: Está a dar um filme português no cinema aqui ao pé.
items.en: There is a Portuguese film on at the cinema nearby.
items.note: estar a dar = to be showing

items.hr: Apetece-me sair, mas não me apetece nada gastar muito.
items.en: I feel like going out, but I really don't feel like spending much.
items.note: apetecer a alguém; negation moves the pronoun forward

items.hr: Ao sábado, damos sempre um salto à feira do livro.
items.en: On Saturdays we always pop over to the book fair.
items.note: dar um salto a = to pop over to

items.hr: Se calhar marcamos para as nove, assim dá tempo de jantar antes.
items.en: Maybe we set it for nine, that way there is time to have dinner first.
items.note: se calhar = maybe, followed by the indicative

activities.title: Making and declining invitations
activities.intro: Practise suggesting plans and reacting to them.

questions.prompt: 'Apetece-me um café' means:
questions.explanation: With apetecer the thing wanted is the subject and the person appears as an indirect pronoun, so the literal structure is 'a coffee appeals to me'.

questions.prompt: Which expression says a film is currently showing?
questions.explanation: Dar is used impersonally for what is on at the cinema or on television: o que está a dar hoje?

questions.prompt: Complete with the noun in the expression meaning that something is worth doing: 'Vale a ___ ir cedo para apanhar lugar.'
questions.explanation: Valer a pena is a fixed expression and the noun never changes, whatever the tense of valer.

questions.prompt: Complete with the verb in the expression meaning to pop over somewhere: 'Vamos ___ um salto ao museu depois do almoço.'
questions.explanation: Dar um salto a plus a place means to go there briefly, and the preposition a contracts with the article: ao museu.

questions.prompt: Build the European Portuguese for: 'It is worth booking the tickets in advance.'
questions.explanation: Valer a pena is followed directly by the infinitive, and com antecedência is the fixed phrase for doing something in advance.

questions.prompt: Play the audio and complete: 'Está a dar um filme ___ no cinema aqui ao pé.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Está a dar um filme português no cinema aqui ao pé.', which means 'There is a Portuguese film on at the cinema nearby.'
questions.audioText: Está a dar um filme português no cinema aqui ao pé.

activities.title: Weekend plans
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend proposes plans and you accept, refuse and counter-suggest using the lesson's expressions.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Estás livre no sábado? Podíamos fazer alguma coisa.
lines.en: Are you free on Saturday? We could do something.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Estou. Apetece-me sair, mas não me apetece nada uma noite longa.
lines.en: I am. I feel like going out, but I really don't feel like a long night.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então vamos ao cinema. Está a dar um filme novo.
lines.en: Then let's go to the cinema. There is a new film on.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Boa ideia. Vale a pena reservar os bilhetes com antecedência.
lines.en: Good idea. It is worth booking the tickets in advance.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E antes? Jantamos ou comemos qualquer coisa rápida?
lines.en: And before? Shall we have dinner or grab something quick?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Se calhar damos um salto àquela tasca ao pé do teatro.
lines.en: Maybe we pop over to that little place next to the theatre.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Combinado. A que horas te dá jeito?
lines.en: Agreed. What time suits you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Às sete e meia, assim dá tempo de jantar antes da sessão.
lines.en: At half past seven, that way there is time to eat before the showing.

days.title: O voluntariado e a solidariedade
days.objective: Talk about volunteering and helping others, using the present subjunctive after impersonal expressions and after para que.
days.paretoFocus: É importante que and para que force the subjunctive, and these two frames alone let you express purpose and social values in any discussion.
drills: Write three sentences beginning with É importante que about your community.
Write three purpose clauses with para que plus the present subjunctive.
Conjugate dar, ser and estar in the present subjunctive out loud, then use each in a sentence.

items: Which mood follows para que and why?
Give the present subjunctive of dar for eu, tu and eles.
How do you say you do volunteer work at a local association?

activities.title: Volunteering and helping others
activities.intro: Impersonal expressions of value such as é importante, é preciso and basta are followed by que plus the present subjunctive. The same mood follows para que, which introduces a purpose when the two clauses have different subjects. If the subject is the same, use para plus the infinitive instead.

items.hr: É importante que as pessoas deem um pouco do seu tempo.
items.en: It is important that people give a little of their time.
items.note: dar in the present subjunctive: que eles deem

items.hr: Faço voluntariado numa associação de bairro aos sábados de manhã.
items.en: I do volunteer work at a neighbourhood association on Saturday mornings.
items.note: fazer voluntariado; associação de bairro

items.hr: Ajudamos para que ninguém fique sozinho no Natal.
items.en: We help so that nobody is left alone at Christmas.
items.note: para que + presente do conjuntivo: fique

items.hr: Basta que cada um dê uma ajuda de vez em quando.
items.en: It is enough for each person to lend a hand every now and then.
items.note: dar uma ajuda = to lend a hand

items.hr: Recolhemos roupa e bens alimentares para famílias carenciadas.
items.en: We collect clothes and food for families in need.
items.note: carenciado = in need, deprived

activities.title: Ajudar e participar
activities.intro: Practise the present subjunctive in value and purpose clauses.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: 'É preciso que tu ___ mais atenção aos outros.'
questions.explanation: É preciso que requires the present subjunctive, and the tu form of dar in that mood is dês, written with a circumflex.

questions.prompt: Which conjunction expresses purpose and requires the subjunctive?
questions.explanation: The other three introduce a cause and are followed by the indicative, since a cause is presented as a fact.

questions.prompt: Complete with the verb meaning to gather donated items: 'A associação ___ roupa usada todos os meses.'
questions.explanation: Recolher is the verb used for collecting donations, distinct from apanhar, which is about picking things up physically.

questions.prompt: Complete with the present subjunctive of ficar: 'Trabalhamos para que ninguém ___ sem apoio este inverno.'
questions.explanation: After para que the verb goes into the present subjunctive, and ficar changes its c to qu before e: fique.

questions.prompt: Build the European Portuguese for: 'I do volunteer work twice a month.'
questions.explanation: Fazer voluntariado takes no article, and frequency is given with duas vezes por mês.

questions.prompt: Listen closely and fill the gap: 'É ___ que as pessoas deem um pouco do seu tempo.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'É importante que as pessoas deem um pouco do seu tempo.', which means 'It is important that people give a little of their time.'
questions.audioText: É importante que as pessoas deem um pouco do seu tempo.

questions.prompt: Type the Portuguese for: 'We collect clothes and food for families in need.'
questions.answer: Recolhemos roupa e bens alimentares para famílias carenciadas.
questions.explanation: 'We collect clothes and food for families in need.' is 'Recolhemos roupa e bens alimentares para famílias carenciadas.'

activities.title: Signing up as a volunteer
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You offer to volunteer at a local association, using impersonal expressions and purpose clauses.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa tarde. Soube que quer dar uma ajuda por cá.
lines.en: Good afternoon. I hear you want to lend a hand here.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Quero, sim. Acho importante que cada um dê algum tempo.
lines.en: Yes, I do. I think it is important that everyone gives some time.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Que dias é que lhe dão jeito?
lines.en: Which days suit you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Aos sábados de manhã, para que não choque com o trabalho.
lines.en: Saturday mornings, so that it does not clash with work.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Temos a recolha de bens alimentares e o apoio a idosos.
lines.en: We have the food collection and support for elderly people.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Prefiro o apoio a idosos, basta que me expliquem o que fazer.
lines.en: I prefer support for elderly people, as long as someone explains what to do.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Damos formação no primeiro dia. Traga um documento de identificação.
lines.en: We give training on the first day. Bring an identification document.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Combinado. Espero que a equipa precise de mais mãos.
lines.en: Agreed. I hope the team needs more hands.

days.title: The modern family and relationships
days.objective: Describe family relationships and how people get on, using dar-se bem com, reciprocal verbs and voltar a plus infinitive.
days.paretoFocus: Reciprocal verbs and dar-se bem com are how Portuguese actually describes relationships, and the vemo-nos spelling rule shows up constantly in speech.
drills: Write five sentences with dar-se bem or dar-se mal about people you know.
Write three reciprocal sentences in the nós form and check the dropped s.
Describe two changes in your family over the last ten years using cada vez mais.

items: Why is it vemo-nos and not vemos-nos?
How do you say 'they started talking to each other again'?
Give two ways to say you get on badly with someone.

activities.title: Family and relationships
activities.intro: Dar-se bem com is the standard way to say you get on with someone. Reciprocal actions use the nós form with the pronoun nos, and the verb drops its final s before that pronoun: vemos plus nos becomes vemo-nos. Voltar a plus an infinitive says an action started again.

items.hr: Dou-me muito bem com a minha cunhada.
items.en: I get on very well with my sister-in-law.
items.note: dar-se bem / mal com alguém

items.hr: Os meus pais divorciaram-se, mas continuam a dar-se bem.
items.en: My parents got divorced, but they still get on well.
items.note: continuar a + infinitivo = to keep on doing

items.hr: Hoje em dia, cada vez mais casais vivem juntos sem casar.
items.en: Nowadays more and more couples live together without marrying.
items.note: cada vez mais = increasingly

items.hr: Vemo-nos uma vez por mês, nem que seja para um café.
items.en: We see each other once a month, even if it is only for a coffee.
items.note: vemos + nos gives vemo-nos; nem que + conjuntivo

items.hr: A minha irmã voltou a viver com os meus pais por causa das rendas.
items.en: My sister went back to living with my parents because of the rents.
items.note: voltar a + infinitivo = to do again

activities.title: Family relationships
activities.intro: Practise reciprocal verbs and relationship expressions.

questions.prompt: Which form is correct in European Portuguese?
questions.explanation: The nós ending loses its final s before the pronoun nos, giving encontramo-nos; fronting the pronoun with no trigger word is not European usage.

questions.prompt: 'Dou-me bem com ele' means:
options: I get on well with him.
questions.answer: I get on well with him.
questions.explanation: Dar-se bem com is a fixed reflexive expression about relationships and has nothing to do with giving.

questions.prompt: Complete with the verb that builds the structure meaning to do something again: 'Eles ___ a falar-se depois de dois anos.'
questions.explanation: Voltar a plus the infinitive expresses repetition, and in the preterite the eles form is voltaram.

questions.prompt: Complete with the reflexive verb meaning to end a marriage legally: 'Os meus tios ___ o ano passado.'
questions.explanation: Divorciar-se is reflexive, and in an affirmative clause the pronoun attaches to the end of the verb with a hyphen.

questions.prompt: Build the European Portuguese for: 'We see each other once a month.'
questions.explanation: The reciprocal nós form drops the final s of the verb before nos, giving vemo-nos.

questions.prompt: Type the word you hear: 'Dou-me muito bem com a minha ___.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Dou-me muito bem com a minha cunhada.', which means 'I get on very well with my sister-in-law.'
questions.audioText: Dou-me muito bem com a minha cunhada.

activities.title: Talking about family
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend asks about your family and you answer with reciprocal verbs and dar-se bem com.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: A tua família é grande?
lines.en: Is your family big?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Nem por isso. Somos quatro, mas damo-nos todos muito bem.
lines.en: Not really. There are four of us, but we all get on very well.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E vês os teus pais muitas vezes?
lines.en: And do you see your parents often?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vemo-nos uma vez por mês, nem que seja para um almoço rápido.
lines.en: We see each other once a month, even if it is only for a quick lunch.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: A minha irmã voltou a viver com os meus pais.
lines.en: My sister went back to living with my parents.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Hoje em dia acontece cada vez mais, com as rendas como estão.
lines.en: That happens more and more nowadays, with rents as they are.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E dão-se bem, os três?
lines.en: And do the three of them get on?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ao início discutiam, mas agora entendem-se bem melhor.
lines.en: At first they used to argue, but now they understand each other much better.

days.title: Formalities and documents
days.objective: Handle documents and their requirements, using ter de, bastar, caducar and the vocabulary of official paperwork in Portugal.
days.paretoFocus: Renewals, proofs and deadlines follow the same three verbs, so one set of sentences covers every document you will ever need.
drills: List four documents you own and write when each one expires.
Write three sentences with basta plus an infinitive about what is enough to bring.
Write the requirements for one renewal as a numbered list in Portuguese.

items: What does caducar mean and what nouns go with it?
Which verb do you use for picking up a document that is ready?
How do you say 'five working days'?

activities.title: Dealing with documents
activities.intro: Obligation about paperwork is expressed with ter de plus an infinitive, and bastar says what is sufficient. Documents caducam rather than expiram in everyday Portuguese, and you levantar a document once it is ready. Deadlines are counted in dias úteis, working days.

items.hr: Tem de renovar o cartão de cidadão antes de este caducar.
items.en: You have to renew your citizen card before it expires.
items.note: caducar = to expire

items.hr: Basta levar um comprovativo de morada e uma fotografia.
items.en: It is enough to bring proof of address and a photograph.
items.note: bastar = to be enough; comprovativo = proof document

items.hr: É preciso marcar atendimento com bastante antecedência.
items.en: You need to book an appointment well in advance.
items.note: marcar atendimento = to book a service appointment

items.hr: O certificado demora cerca de dez dias úteis a ser emitido.
items.en: The certificate takes about ten working days to be issued.
items.note: dias úteis = working days; emitir = to issue

items.hr: Já levantei a carta de condução nova ao balcão.
items.en: I have already picked up my new driving licence at the counter.
items.note: levantar = to collect something that is ready

activities.title: Documentos e prazos
activities.intro: Practise the verbs and nouns of official paperwork.

questions.prompt: 'O passaporte caduca em março' means:
options: The passport is issued in March.
The passport is renewed in March.
The passport is cancelled in March.
questions.explanation: Caducar is the standard verb for a document reaching the end of its validity in Portugal.

questions.prompt: Which verb means to collect a document that is ready for you?
questions.explanation: Levantar um documento means to pick it up at a counter; tirar means to obtain a document for the first time and apanhar is for catching things or transport.

questions.prompt: Complete with the verb meaning that something is sufficient: '___ apresentar um documento de identificação.'
questions.explanation: Bastar is used impersonally in the third person singular before an infinitive to say what is enough.

questions.prompt: Complete with the adjective used for days on which offices are open: 'A resposta chega em cinco dias ___.'
questions.explanation: Dias úteis are working days; the plural of útil is úteis, keeping the accent.

questions.prompt: Build the European Portuguese for: 'You have to renew your identity card.'
questions.explanation: Obligation uses ter de plus an infinitive, and the Portuguese identity document is o cartão de cidadão.

questions.prompt: Listen and complete the sentence: 'Tem de ___ o cartão de cidadão antes de este caducar.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Tem de renovar o cartão de cidadão antes de este caducar.', which means 'You have to renew your citizen card before it expires.'
questions.audioText: Tem de renovar o cartão de cidadão antes de este caducar.

questions.prompt: Say it in Portuguese, in writing: 'I have already picked up my new driving licence at the counter.'
questions.answer: Já levantei a carta de condução nova ao balcão.
questions.explanation: 'I have already picked up my new driving licence at the counter.' is 'Já levantei a carta de condução nova ao balcão.'

activities.title: At the service counter
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You renew a document and ask about requirements and deadlines.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bom dia. Diga, faz favor.
lines.en: Good morning. How can I help?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bom dia. O meu cartão caduca no mês que vem e queria renová-lo.
lines.en: Good morning. My card expires next month and I would like to renew it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Trouxe algum comprovativo de morada?
lines.en: Did you bring any proof of address?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Trouxe uma fatura da água. Basta isso ou é preciso mais?
lines.en: I brought a water bill. Is that enough or is more needed?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Chega. A fotografia é tirada aqui mesmo.
lines.en: That is fine. The photograph is taken right here.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: E quanto tempo demora até estar pronto?
lines.en: And how long does it take until it is ready?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Cerca de dez dias úteis. Depois vem levantá-lo ao balcão.
lines.en: About ten working days. Then you come and pick it up at the counter.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Muito obrigado. Então tenho de voltar cá no fim do mês.
lines.en: Thank you very much. So I have to come back here at the end of the month.

days.title: A publicidade e o consumo
days.objective: Discuss advertising and consumer habits, using fazer com que plus the subjunctive, levar alguém a plus infinitive and deixar-se levar por.
days.paretoFocus: Fazer com que and levar a are the two structures Portuguese uses to talk about causes and influence, which is the heart of any opinion discussion.
drills: Write three sentences with fazer com que about the effects of advertising.
Write two sentences about your own purchases: what led you to buy them? Use levar alguém a.
Describe a purchase you regret in four sentences.

items: Which mood follows fazer com que and why?
How do you say an advert made you buy on impulse?
What does deixar-se levar por mean?

activities.title: Publicidade e consumo
activities.intro: Fazer com que expresses causing something and always takes the present subjunctive. Levar alguém a followed by an infinitive says that something pushes a person into an action. Deixar-se levar por means to be swayed by something, and the pronoun moves in front of the verb after não.

items.hr: A publicidade faz com que a gente compre coisas de que não precisa.
items.en: Advertising makes people buy things they do not need.
items.note: fazer com que + presente do conjuntivo: compre

items.hr: Os descontos levam-nos a gastar mais do que queríamos.
items.en: Discounts lead us to spend more than we wanted to.
items.note: levar alguém a + infinitivo

items.hr: Não me deixo levar por promoções agressivas.
items.en: I do not let myself be swayed by aggressive offers.
items.note: deixar-se levar por; não moves the pronoun forward

items.hr: Antes de comprar, comparo sempre preços e leio comentários.
items.en: Before buying, I always compare prices and read reviews.
items.note: antes de + infinitivo

items.hr: Aquilo é publicidade enganosa: prometem coisas que não cumprem.
items.en: That is misleading advertising: they promise things they do not deliver.
items.note: enganoso = misleading; cumprir = to deliver on

activities.title: Adverts and shopping
activities.intro: Practise causative structures and consumer vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: 'A campanha faz com que muita gente ___ produtos inúteis.'
questions.explanation: Fazer com que always introduces a subordinate clause in the present subjunctive, so comprar becomes compre.

questions.prompt: 'Deixei-me levar pela promoção' means:
options: I let myself be swayed by the offer.
questions.answer: I let myself be swayed by the offer.
questions.explanation: Deixar-se levar por is a fixed reflexive expression meaning to be carried along by something, here an offer.

questions.prompt: Complete with the adjective describing advertising that misleads the public: 'A associação de consumidores queixou-se de publicidade ___.'
questions.explanation: Enganoso comes from enganar, to deceive, and agrees with the feminine noun publicidade.

questions.prompt: Complete with the verb that means to push someone into doing something: 'Os anúncios ___-nos a comprar por impulso.'
questions.explanation: Levar alguém a plus an infinitive expresses influence, and here the eles form levam agrees with os anúncios.

questions.prompt: Build the European Portuguese for: 'I always compare prices before buying.'
questions.explanation: Sempre normally sits right after the verb, and antes de is followed by the infinitive when the subject stays the same.

questions.prompt: Listen, then type the missing word: 'Os ___ levam-nos a gastar mais do que queríamos.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Os descontos levam-nos a gastar mais do que queríamos.', which means 'Discounts lead us to spend more than we wanted to.'
questions.audioText: Os descontos levam-nos a gastar mais do que queríamos.

questions.prompt: Put this into Portuguese: 'That is misleading advertising: they promise things they do not deliver.'
questions.answer: Aquilo é publicidade enganosa: prometem coisas que não cumprem.
questions.explanation: 'That is misleading advertising: they promise things they do not deliver.' is 'Aquilo é publicidade enganosa: prometem coisas que não cumprem.'

activities.title: An impulse buy
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend shows off a purchase and you discuss the influence of advertising.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Olha o que comprei ontem. Estava com cinquenta por cento de desconto.
lines.en: Look what I bought yesterday. It was fifty per cent off.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Precisavas mesmo disso ou deixaste-te levar pela promoção?
lines.en: Did you really need it or did you let yourself be swayed by the offer?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Confesso que foi o anúncio que me convenceu.
lines.en: I admit it was the advert that convinced me.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É isso: a publicidade faz com que compremos o que não nos faz falta.
lines.en: That is it: advertising makes us buy what we do not need.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E tu nunca cais nessa?
lines.en: And you never fall for that?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Caio, mas antes de comprar comparo sempre preços noutro sítio.
lines.en: I do, but before buying I always compare prices somewhere else.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Se calhar tinha encontrado mais barato.
lines.en: Maybe I would have found it cheaper.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Provavelmente. Os descontos levam-nos a decidir depressa de mais.
lines.en: Probably. Discounts lead us to decide far too quickly.

days.title: The news: understanding a short article
days.objective: Understand and summarise a short news item, recognising the passive with ser, source phrases such as segundo, and the future perfect used for unconfirmed information.
days.paretoFocus: Portuguese news writing recycles the same few structures, so learning them unlocks almost any short article or bulletin.
drills: Rewrite three active sentences of your own in the passive with ser.
Write two sentences with terá plus a participle about something not yet confirmed.
Summarise a short news story you know in five Portuguese sentences, naming the source.

items: What does terá começado mean in a news report?
Which preposition introduces the agent in a passive sentence?
Give two phrases that introduce the source of information.

activities.title: Reading a news story
activities.intro: News Portuguese leans on the passive with ser plus a past participle, with the agent introduced by por and its contractions. Sources are marked with segundo or de acordo com. When information is not confirmed, journalists use the future perfect, terá acontecido, which means it apparently happened.

items.hr: Segundo o jornal, a greve foi adiada para a próxima semana.
items.en: According to the newspaper, the strike was postponed to next week.
items.note: segundo = according to, with no preposition after it

items.hr: De acordo com a autarquia, as obras estarão concluídas em junho.
items.en: According to the local council, the works will be finished in June.
items.note: autarquia = local council

items.hr: O acordo foi assinado esta manhã pelos dois governos.
items.en: The agreement was signed this morning by the two governments.
items.note: passiva: ser + particípio + por, contracted to pelos

items.hr: O incêndio terá começado por volta das três da madrugada.
items.en: The fire apparently started at around three in the morning.
items.note: futuro composto for unconfirmed facts: terá começado

items.hr: A notícia refere ainda que os prejuízos ascendem a milhares de euros.
items.en: The report also states that the damage amounts to thousands of euros.
items.note: prejuízos = damage, losses; ascender a = to amount to

activities.title: The language of the news
activities.intro: Practise the passive, source phrases and unconfirmed information.

questions.prompt: 'O suspeito terá fugido a pé' in a news report means:
options: The suspect apparently fled on foot.
The suspect will flee on foot.
The suspect had to flee on foot.
The suspect wanted to flee on foot.
questions.answer: The suspect apparently fled on foot.
questions.explanation: In journalism the future perfect signals information that is likely but not confirmed, not a future action.

questions.prompt: Which phrase introduces the source of a piece of news?
questions.explanation: De acordo com and segundo attribute information to a source; the others express contrast, concession and cause.

questions.prompt: Complete with the past participle of anunciar in the passive: 'A decisão foi ___ ontem à noite.'
questions.explanation: In the passive with ser the participle agrees with the subject, and a decisão is feminine singular.

questions.prompt: Complete with the contracted preposition that introduces the agent: 'O relatório foi divulgado ___ ministério.'
questions.explanation: The agent of a passive sentence is introduced by por, which contracts with o to give pelo.

questions.prompt: Build the European Portuguese for: 'According to the newspaper, the meeting was postponed.'
questions.explanation: Segundo takes no preposition before the source, and the passive foi adiada agrees with a reunião.

questions.prompt: Listen and fill in the word you hear: 'Segundo o jornal, a greve foi adiada para a ___ semana.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Segundo o jornal, a greve foi adiada para a próxima semana.', which means 'According to the newspaper, the strike was postponed to next week.'
questions.audioText: Segundo o jornal, a greve foi adiada para a próxima semana.

questions.prompt: Type the Portuguese for: 'The agreement was signed this morning by the two governments.'
questions.answer: O acordo foi assinado esta manhã pelos dois governos.
questions.explanation: 'The agreement was signed this morning by the two governments.' is 'O acordo foi assinado esta manhã pelos dois governos.'

activities.title: Commenting on a news story
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A colleague asks what a short article said and you report it using passives and source phrases.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Leste a notícia sobre a ponte? O que é que dizia?
lines.en: Did you read the news about the bridge? What did it say?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Segundo o jornal, as obras foram adiadas outra vez.
lines.en: According to the newspaper, the works have been postponed again.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Outra vez? E dão alguma razão?
lines.en: Again? And do they give any reason?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: O atraso terá sido causado por um problema no financiamento.
lines.en: The delay was apparently caused by a funding problem.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E quem é que anunciou isso?
lines.en: And who announced that?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: De acordo com o artigo, foi anunciado pela autarquia na sexta-feira.
lines.en: According to the article, it was announced by the local council on Friday.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Dizem quando é que aquilo fica pronto?
lines.en: Do they say when it will be ready?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A notícia refere ainda que estará concluída no próximo verão.
lines.en: The report also states that it will be finished next summer.

days.title: A lusofonia: o português no mundo
days.objective: Talk about where Portuguese is spoken and compare its varieties using connectors of addition and contrast.
days.paretoFocus: Portuguese is spread over four continents, so learners meet several accents daily and need language to compare them without sounding confused.
drills: List the nine countries where Portuguese is official, saying each name out loud in Portuguese.
Write three sentences using 'tanto ... como', 'além de' and 'ao passo que' about the language.
Say aloud two words you know that differ between European and other varieties, and use each in a sentence.

items: How do you say 'besides Portugal' in Portuguese?
Which connector means 'whereas' and introduces a contrast?
Which mood follows 'embora'?

activities.title: Portuguese around the world
activities.intro: Portuguese is an official language on four continents, and each region has its own accent and some of its own words. To describe this you need connectors that add ('além de', 'tanto ... como') and connectors that contrast ('ao passo que', 'embora'). Note that 'embora' is always followed by the subjunctive.

items.hr: O português é língua oficial em nove países, tanto na Europa como em África.
items.en: Portuguese is an official language in nine countries, both in Europe and in Africa.
items.note: tanto ... como = both ... and

items.hr: Além de Portugal e do Brasil, fala-se português em Angola, Moçambique e Timor-Leste.
items.en: Besides Portugal and Brazil, Portuguese is spoken in Angola, Mozambique and East Timor.
items.note: além de + noun = besides, in addition to

items.hr: Em Portugal diz-se 'comboio', ao passo que noutras variedades se usa outra palavra.
items.en: In Portugal people say 'comboio', whereas in other varieties another word is used.
items.note: ao passo que = whereas

items.hr: Embora a ortografia seja quase igual, a pronúncia varia bastante de país para país.
items.en: Although the spelling is almost the same, the pronunciation varies a lot from country to country.
items.note: embora + conjuntivo: ser becomes seja

items.hr: Cada variedade tem o seu sotaque próprio, o que não impede que nos entendamos.
items.en: Each variety has its own accent, which does not stop us from understanding each other.
items.note: impedir que + conjuntivo

items.hr: O sotaque muda de país para país.
items.en: The accent changes from country to country.

items.hr: Entendemo-nos sem dificuldade.
items.en: We understand each other without difficulty.
items.note: Reciprocal se, with the pronoun attached: entendemo-nos loses the -s of entendemos.

activities.title: Comparar variedades
activities.intro: Practise the connectors used to add and to contrast information about the language.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'O português é falado ___ na Europa como em África.'
questions.explanation: The pair is 'tanto ... como', the Portuguese equivalent of 'both ... and'.

questions.prompt: Which connector introduces a contrast between two varieties of the language?
questions.explanation: 'Ao passo que' means 'whereas'. 'Por isso' gives a consequence, 'visto que' a cause and 'assim que' a time relation.

questions.prompt: Complete so that the sentence means 'Besides Portugal, Portuguese is spoken in Angola': '___ Portugal, fala-se português em Angola.'
questions.explanation: 'Além de' is followed directly by a noun and adds a further element to the list.

questions.prompt: Give the correct form of 'ser' after 'embora': 'Embora a ortografia ___ quase igual, a pronúncia muda.'
questions.explanation: 'Embora' always takes the present subjunctive, so 'ser' becomes 'seja'.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'Portuguese is an official language in nine countries.'
questions.explanation: In this fixed expression 'língua oficial' takes no article: 'é língua oficial em'.

activities.title: Quantos portugueses existem?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A colleague asks you about the varieties of Portuguese, and you answer, linking your points and marking the differences.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ouvi dizer que o português se fala em muitos países. É mesmo assim?
lines.en: I heard that Portuguese is spoken in many countries. Is that really so?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É, sim. Além de Portugal e do Brasil, é língua oficial em Angola, em Moçambique e em Timor-Leste.
lines.en: Yes, it is. Besides Portugal and Brazil, it is an official language in Angola, in Mozambique and in East Timor.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E as pessoas percebem-se umas às outras?
lines.en: And do people understand each other?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Percebem. Embora o sotaque seja muito diferente, a gramática é praticamente a mesma.
lines.en: They do. Although the accent is very different, the grammar is practically the same.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E o vocabulário? Dá-me um exemplo.
lines.en: And the vocabulary? Give me an example.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Aqui apanhamos o comboio, ao passo que noutros sítios usam outra palavra para o mesmo transporte.
lines.en: Here we take the train, whereas in other places they use another word for the same transport.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então tenho de habituar o ouvido a tudo isso.
lines.en: So I have to get my ear used to all of that.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tanto na rádio como nas séries ouves vários sotaques, e ao fim de umas semanas já distingues.
lines.en: Both on the radio and in series you hear several accents, and after a few weeks you can already tell them apart.

days.title: Living abroad: settling in and adapting
days.objective: Describe settling into a new country using reflexive verbs of adaptation and the prepositions they require.
days.paretoFocus: Almost every conversation with a new neighbour or colleague abroad starts with how long you have been there and how you are adapting.
drills: Say three things you are still getting used to, each with 'habituar-se a'.
Describe two people you get on well with using 'dar-se bem com'.
Name three things from home that you miss, using 'fazer falta'.

items: Which preposition follows 'habituar-se'?
How do you say 'I find it hard to understand the accent'?
How do you say 'I miss the sea' in Portuguese?

activities.title: Settling into a new country
activities.intro: Portuguese describes adaptation with reflexive verbs that each take a fixed preposition: 'habituar-se a', 'dar-se bem com', 'adaptar-se a'. Two other patterns are very frequent here: 'custar a + infinitive' for something you find hard, and 'fazer falta a alguém' for missing something.

items.hr: Mudei-me para Lisboa há seis meses e ainda me estou a habituar ao ritmo.
items.en: I moved to Lisbon six months ago and I am still getting used to the pace.
items.note: habituar-se a; estar a + infinitivo is the European Portuguese progressive

items.hr: No início, custou-me a perceber o sotaque das pessoas na rua.
items.en: At the start, I found it hard to understand people's accent in the street.
items.note: custar a + infinitivo = to find something hard

items.hr: Já me dou bem com os vizinhos, sobretudo com a senhora do quarto andar.
items.en: I already get on well with the neighbours, especially with the lady on the fourth floor.
items.note: dar-se bem com alguém

items.hr: Aos poucos, fui-me adaptando à maneira de viver daqui.
items.en: Little by little, I gradually adapted to the way of living here.
items.note: ir + gerúndio expresses a gradual process

items.hr: O que mais me faz falta é a comida da minha mãe.
items.en: What I miss most is my mother's cooking.
items.note: fazer falta a alguém: the thing missed is the subject

activities.title: Adapting to a new life
activities.intro: Practise the reflexive verbs and prepositions used to talk about settling in.

questions.prompt: Which verb means 'to get used to' and is followed by 'a'?
questions.explanation: 'Habituar-se a' means to get used to. 'Despedir-se de' is to say goodbye, 'queixar-se de' to complain and 'aproximar-se de' to come closer.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Dou-me muito ___ com os meus colegas de trabalho.'
questions.explanation: 'Dar-se bem com' uses the adverb 'bem', which never agrees with the subject.

questions.prompt: Supply the missing preposition plus article: 'Ainda me estou a habituar ___ horário das lojas.'
questions.explanation: 'Habituar-se a' plus the masculine article 'o' contracts to 'ao'.

questions.prompt: Supply the verb so the sentence means 'What I miss most is the sea': 'O que mais me ___ falta é o mar.'
questions.explanation: In 'fazer falta' the verb agrees with the thing missed, here 'o mar', so it is third person singular.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I moved to Lisbon six months ago.'
questions.explanation: 'Mudar-se para' takes 'para' for the destination, and elapsed time uses 'há'.

questions.prompt: Listen closely and fill the gap: 'No início, custou-me a ___ o sotaque das pessoas na rua.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'No início, custou-me a perceber o sotaque das pessoas na rua.', which means 'At the start, I found it hard to understand people's accent in the street.'
questions.audioText: No início, custou-me a perceber o sotaque das pessoas na rua.

activities.title: Do you feel at home yet?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A neighbour asks how you are settling in and you answer with reflexive verbs of adaptation.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então, já te sentes em casa cá no bairro?
lines.en: So, do you feel at home here in the neighbourhood yet?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Aos poucos. Ainda me estou a habituar aos horários, mas já não me perco.
lines.en: Little by little. I am still getting used to the timetables, but I no longer get lost.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E o que foi mais difícil no início?
lines.en: And what was hardest at the beginning?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Custou-me a perceber as pessoas ao telefone. Ao vivo é muito mais fácil.
lines.en: I found it hard to understand people on the phone. In person it is much easier.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E com os vizinhos, tens-te dado bem?
lines.en: And with the neighbours, have you been getting on well?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Dou-me bem com toda a gente, sobretudo com o senhor do rés do chão.
lines.en: I get on well with everybody, especially with the gentleman on the ground floor.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Nunca tens saudades de nada?
lines.en: Don't you ever miss anything?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tenho. O que mais me faz falta são os jantares longos com a família.
lines.en: I do. What I miss most are the long dinners with my family.

days.title: Responsible tourism
days.objective: Give impersonal recommendations about travelling responsibly using 'deve-se', 'convém que' and 'valer a pena'.
days.paretoFocus: Impersonal recommendation structures let you give advice about any topic without pointing at the person you are speaking to.
drills: Write three rules for visitors to your town, each starting with 'Deve-se'.
Turn two of those rules into 'Convém que os visitantes ...' with the subjunctive.
Say three things that are worth doing off season, using 'vale a pena'.

items: How do you say 'one should respect the silence'?
Which mood follows 'convém que'?
What is the European Portuguese word for 'train'?

activities.title: Travelling respectfully
activities.intro: To recommend something without naming who must do it, Portuguese uses impersonal structures. 'Deve-se + infinitive' and 'evita-se' use the impersonal 'se'; 'convém que' and 'é preferível que' are followed by the subjunctive. 'Valer a pena + infinitive' says something is worth doing.

items.hr: Deve-se respeitar o silêncio nas ruas dos bairros antigos.
items.en: One should respect the silence in the streets of the old neighbourhoods.
items.note: deve-se + infinitivo = impersonal 'one should'

items.hr: Convém que os visitantes comprem produtos locais em vez de recordações importadas.
items.en: It is advisable for visitors to buy local products instead of imported souvenirs.
items.note: convém que + conjuntivo: comprar becomes comprem

items.hr: É preferível andar de comboio do que ir de avião em distâncias curtas.
items.en: It is preferable to travel by train rather than to fly over short distances.
items.note: comboio is the European Portuguese word for train

items.hr: Evita-se assim o excesso de pessoas nos mesmos sítios e à mesma hora.
items.en: That way you avoid the excess of people in the same places at the same time.
items.note: evita-se: impersonal se with a plural or singular object

items.hr: Vale a pena visitar aldeias pequenas fora da época alta.
items.en: It is worth visiting small villages outside the high season.
items.note: valer a pena + infinitivo

activities.title: Advice for visitors
activities.intro: Deve-se or convém que? Give travel advice without naming anyone in particular.

questions.prompt: Which form gives an impersonal recommendation rather than a personal one?
questions.explanation: The clitic 'se' removes the subject, so the advice applies to anyone. The other options all name a specific speaker.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Convém que os turistas ___ os horários dos locais de culto.'
questions.explanation: 'Convém que' triggers the present subjunctive, so 'respeitar' becomes 'respeitem'.

questions.prompt: Supply the verb so the sentence means 'It is worth visiting the villages in autumn': '___ a pena visitar as aldeias no outono.'
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'valer a pena', used impersonally in the third person singular.

questions.prompt: Supply the European Portuguese noun for the transport that runs on rails: 'Em vez de ir de avião, fui de ___.'
questions.explanation: European Portuguese uses 'comboio' for train; other varieties use a different word.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'It is preferable to travel outside the high season.'
questions.explanation: With no named subject, 'é preferível' is followed straight by the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Type the word you hear: 'Deve-se ___ o silêncio nas ruas dos bairros antigos.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Deve-se respeitar o silêncio nas ruas dos bairros antigos.', which means 'One should respect the silence in the streets of the old neighbourhoods.'
questions.audioText: Deve-se respeitar o silêncio nas ruas dos bairros antigos.

activities.title: Planning a trip sensibly
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend is planning a trip and you suggest a more responsible way of doing it, using impersonal recommendations.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Estou a pensar ir três dias ao sul em agosto. O que achas?
lines.en: I am thinking of going south for three days in August. What do you think?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale mais a pena ir em setembro. Fora da época alta, está tudo mais calmo e mais barato.
lines.en: It is more worth going in September. Outside the high season, everything is calmer and cheaper.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Faz sentido. E vou de avião ou de carro?
lines.en: That makes sense. And should I fly or drive?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Em distâncias curtas, é preferível ir de comboio. Gasta-se menos e chega-se ao centro da cidade.
lines.en: Over short distances, it is preferable to go by train. You spend less and you arrive in the city centre.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E onde é que devo ficar?
lines.en: And where should I stay?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Convém que escolhas um sítio fora do centro histórico, para não ocupar casas de quem lá vive.
lines.en: It is advisable that you choose a place outside the historic centre, so as not to take up homes from the people who live there.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E à noite, há alguma regra?
lines.en: And at night, is there any rule?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Deve-se respeitar o silêncio depois das dez. As casas são antigas e ouve-se tudo.
lines.en: One should respect the silence after ten. The houses are old and you hear everything.

days.title: Climate and everyday habits
days.objective: Link everyday habits to their causes and consequences using 'devido a', 'graças a', 'por isso', 'como' and 'de modo que'.
days.paretoFocus: Cause and consequence connectors are the backbone of any explanation, from why you changed a habit to why a plan failed.
drills: Write three sentences about your habits, each with a different cause connector.
Turn one cause sentence around so the consequence comes second with 'por isso'.
Say aloud one change you made and what it saved, using 'graças a'.

items: Which expression introduces a positive cause?
Which connector opens a sentence and means 'since'?
How do you contract 'devido a' with a feminine plural noun?

activities.title: Pequenos gestos, grande efeito
activities.intro: Portuguese separates connectors that introduce a cause from those that introduce a consequence. 'Devido a', 'graças a' and 'por causa de' take a noun; 'como' opens the sentence with the cause. 'Por isso' and 'de modo que' introduce the result.

items.hr: Devido às ondas de calor, muita gente mudou os horários das compras.
items.en: Because of the heatwaves, many people changed their shopping times.
items.note: devido a + noun; a + as contracts to às

items.hr: Como o verão está cada vez mais seco, poupamos água em casa.
items.en: Since the summer is getting drier and drier, we save water at home.
items.note: como at the start of a sentence means 'since', never 'how'

items.hr: Uso menos o carro, por isso gasto muito menos combustível.
items.en: I use the car less, so I spend much less on fuel.
items.note: por isso introduces the consequence

items.hr: Graças à reciclagem do prédio, produzimos metade do lixo do ano passado.
items.en: Thanks to the building's recycling, we produce half the rubbish of last year.
items.note: graças a is only used for a cause with a good result

items.hr: Desliguei os aparelhos à noite, de modo que a conta desceu quase um terço.
items.en: I switched off the appliances at night, so that the bill went down almost a third.
items.note: de modo que + indicativo when the result really happened

activities.title: Causes and consequences
activities.intro: Practise choosing between cause connectors and consequence connectors.

questions.prompt: Which expression introduces a cause with a good result?
questions.explanation: 'Graças a' means 'thanks to' and is only used when the outcome is positive. The others express concession or contrast.

questions.prompt: Complete: '___ o verão está mais seco, poupamos água em casa.'
questions.explanation: At the start of a sentence 'como' introduces the cause. 'Por isso' and 'portanto' introduce results and cannot open this clause.

questions.prompt: Supply the two words that introduce the result: 'Uso menos o carro, ___ ___ gasto menos combustível.'
questions.explanation: 'Por isso' links a fact to the consequence that follows from it.

questions.prompt: Supply the contraction of 'a' with the feminine plural article: 'Devido ___ ondas de calor, mudámos os horários.'
questions.explanation: 'Devido a' plus 'as' contracts to 'às', with the grave accent marking the contraction.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I separate the rubbish every day.'
questions.explanation: 'Todos os dias' is the fixed adverbial for 'every day' and goes after the object.

questions.prompt: Listen and complete the sentence: 'Devido às ondas de calor, muita gente mudou os ___ das compras.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Devido às ondas de calor, muita gente mudou os horários das compras.', which means 'Because of the heatwaves, many people changed their shopping times.'
questions.audioText: Devido às ondas de calor, muita gente mudou os horários das compras.

activities.title: The electricity bill went down
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend notices your bills went down and you explain the causes and the consequences of your new habits.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Disseste que a tua conta da luz desceu. Como é que conseguiste?
lines.en: You said your electricity bill went down. How did you manage that?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Comecei a desligar tudo à noite, de modo que a conta desceu quase um terço.
lines.en: I started switching everything off at night, so the bill went down almost a third.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Só isso? Parece pouco para tanta diferença.
lines.en: Just that? It seems little for such a difference.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Também uso menos o carro, por isso gasto bastante menos ao fim do mês.
lines.en: I also use the car less, so I spend considerably less at the end of the month.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E a água? Aqui em casa é o que mais pesa.
lines.en: And water? Here at home that is what weighs most.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Como o verão está cada vez mais seco, passei a apanhar a água fria do duche num balde.
lines.en: Since the summer is getting drier and drier, I started collecting the cold shower water in a bucket.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Nunca me tinha lembrado disso. E funciona mesmo?
lines.en: I had never thought of that. And does it really work?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Funciona. Graças a esses gestos pequenos, este ano quase não notei o aumento dos preços.
lines.en: It does. Thanks to those small gestures, this year I hardly noticed the price increase.

days.title: The press and sources of information
days.objective: Attribute information to a source and mark what is unconfirmed using 'segundo', 'de acordo com', 'ao que parece' and 'diz-se que'.
days.paretoFocus: Marking where information came from is what separates repeating a rumour from reporting a fact, in speech and in writing alike.
drills: Report three headlines you saw this week, each starting with 'Segundo'.
Rewrite one of them with 'De acordo com' and one with 'Ao que parece'.
Say one thing you heard but cannot confirm, using 'diz-se que'.

items: Which one-word expression means 'according to'?
How do you say 'apparently' at the start of a sentence?
How do you build the impersonal 'it is said that'?

activities.title: Citing a source
activities.intro: When you report something you did not witness, Portuguese asks you to name the source or to flag the doubt. 'Segundo' and 'de acordo com' introduce the source; 'diz-se que' and 'ao que parece' signal that the information is not confirmed.

items.hr: Segundo o jornal de hoje, o tempo vai mudar no fim de semana.
items.en: According to today's newspaper, the weather is going to change at the weekend.
items.note: segundo takes no preposition after it

items.hr: De acordo com os dados divulgados ontem, o número de leitores subiu.
items.en: According to the data released yesterday, the number of readers went up.
items.note: de acordo com is the slightly more formal equivalent

items.hr: Ao que parece, a notícia ainda não foi confirmada por ninguém.
items.en: Apparently, the news has not been confirmed by anyone yet.
items.note: ao que parece = apparently, from what it seems

items.hr: Diz-se que a decisão será anunciada amanhã de manhã.
items.en: It is said that the decision will be announced tomorrow morning.
items.note: diz-se que: impersonal se, no named source

items.hr: Antes de partilhar uma notícia, verifico sempre quem a escreveu e quando.
items.en: Before sharing a piece of news, I always check who wrote it and when.
items.note: notícia is countable: uma notícia = one news item

activities.title: Where does the information come from?
activities.intro: Practise attributing information and flagging what is still unconfirmed.

questions.prompt: Which expression tells the listener that the information is unconfirmed?
questions.explanation: 'Ao que parece' means apparently. 'Por acaso' means by chance, 'de vez em quando' occasionally and 'ainda por cima' on top of that.

questions.prompt: Complete: '___ com o relatório publicado ontem, os preços vão descer.'
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'de acordo com'. 'Segundo' is used alone, without 'com'.

questions.prompt: Supply the single word that attributes the statement to a named source: '___ o jornal de ontem, a greve foi adiada.'
questions.explanation: 'Segundo' is followed directly by the source, with no preposition in between.

questions.prompt: Supply the missing verb form in this impersonal report: '___-se que a notícia é falsa.'
questions.explanation: The impersonal 'se' attaches to the third person singular 'diz', giving 'diz-se que'.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'The news has not been confirmed yet.'
questions.explanation: In the passive the participle agrees with the subject, so 'confirmada' is feminine singular, and 'ainda' comes before 'não'.

questions.prompt: Listen, then type the missing word: 'De acordo com os dados ___ ontem, o número de leitores subiu.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'De acordo com os dados divulgados ontem, o número de leitores subiu.', which means 'According to the data released yesterday, the number of readers went up.'
questions.audioText: De acordo com os dados divulgados ontem, o número de leitores subiu.

activities.title: Is that true?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A colleague repeats something they read and you push them to say where it came from.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ouvi dizer que vão fechar a biblioteca do bairro.
lines.en: I heard they are going to close the neighbourhood library.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ouviste onde? Ao que parece, ainda não há nada decidido.
lines.en: Where did you hear that? Apparently, nothing has been decided yet.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Estava numa mensagem que me enviaram esta manhã.
lines.en: It was in a message someone sent me this morning.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Segundo o jornal local, a obra é só para arranjar o telhado.
lines.en: According to the local paper, the work is only to fix the roof.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então a mensagem estava errada?
lines.en: So the message was wrong?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: De acordo com os dados que li, sim. E a mensagem não dizia quem a tinha escrito.
lines.en: According to the data I read, yes. And the message did not say who had written it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tens razão, eu nem olhei para isso.
lines.en: You are right, I did not even look at that.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Antes de reenviar, vejo sempre quem escreveu e em que dia. Poupa muitos sustos.
lines.en: Before forwarding, I always check who wrote it and on what day. It saves a lot of scares.

days.title: Sport and competition: commenting on an event
days.objective: Comment on a sports event by combining the pretérito perfeito and imperfeito and the near-miss expressions 'por pouco não' and 'estar quase a'.
days.paretoFocus: The same tense contrast and near-miss expressions are used to narrate any event, from a match to an accident or a job interview.
drills: Describe a match or race in five sentences, using the imperfect for the background and the perfect for the events.
Write two sentences with 'por pouco não' about things that almost happened to you.
Say aloud three Portuguese words for people in a match: player, goalkeeper, referee.

items: Which tense sets the scene and which reports the events?
How do you say 'we almost scored'?
What is the Portuguese word for goalkeeper?

activities.title: Commenting on a match
activities.intro: To tell someone about a match you need two past tenses at once: the imperfeito for what was going on, and the pretérito perfeito for what happened. Two near-miss patterns are essential in commentary: 'por pouco não' plus the perfect, and 'estar quase a' plus the infinitive.

items.hr: O jogo estava equilibrado até que o guarda-redes falhou uma bola fácil.
items.en: The match was balanced until the goalkeeper missed an easy ball.
items.note: estava sets the scene, falhou reports the event

items.hr: Por pouco não marcámos nos últimos minutos.
items.en: We almost scored in the last minutes.
items.note: por pouco não: the negative is not translated into English

items.hr: Enquanto a equipa da casa atacava, a outra defendia-se muito bem.
items.en: While the home team was attacking, the other one was defending itself very well.
items.note: two simultaneous backgrounds, both imperfeito

items.hr: Estivemos quase a empatar, mas o árbitro apitou o fim.
items.en: We were about to draw, but the referee blew for the end.
items.note: estar quase a + infinitivo

items.hr: Foi um jogo renhido, ganharam por um golo de diferença.
items.en: It was a closely fought match, they won by one goal.
items.note: renhido = closely fought, hard-fought

activities.title: Saying what happened
activities.intro: Perfeito or imperfeito, and how do you say something almost happened? Commentary practice.

questions.prompt: Which word is European Portuguese for the player who defends the goal?
questions.explanation: 'Guarda-redes' is the European Portuguese term. 'Porteiro' is a caretaker and 'avançado' is a forward.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Por pouco não ___ o golo do empate no último minuto.'
questions.explanation: 'Por pouco não' refers to a completed near miss, so it takes the pretérito perfeito.

questions.prompt: Supply the imperfeito of 'estar': 'O resultado ___ empatado quando saí do café.'
questions.explanation: The score is background information that was ongoing, so the imperfeito is required.

questions.prompt: Supply the adjective that describes a match decided by the smallest of margins: 'Foi um jogo muito ___, decidido nos descontos.'
questions.explanation: 'Renhido' describes a hard-fought, very close contest and is the usual word in sports commentary.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'We were about to draw the match.'
questions.explanation: 'Estar quase a' keeps 'quase' between the verb and 'a', and the infinitive follows.

questions.prompt: Listen and fill in the word you hear: 'Por pouco não ___ nos últimos minutos.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Por pouco não marcámos nos últimos minutos.', which means 'We almost scored in the last minutes.'
questions.audioText: Por pouco não marcámos nos últimos minutos.

activities.title: Did you see yesterday's match?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend missed the match and you narrate it, mixing the imperfeito for the scene and the perfeito for the events.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perdi o jogo de ontem. Valeu a pena?
lines.en: I missed yesterday's match. Was it worth it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Foi um jogo renhido. Estava tudo empatado até aos oitenta minutos.
lines.en: It was a closely fought match. Everything was level until the eightieth minute.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E depois? Quem é que marcou?
lines.en: And then? Who scored?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Enquanto nós atacávamos, eles saíram num contra-ataque e marcaram.
lines.en: While we were attacking, they broke away on a counter-attack and scored.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Que azar. Não houve resposta?
lines.en: What bad luck. Was there no reply?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Por pouco não empatámos. A bola bateu no poste aos noventa.
lines.en: We almost drew. The ball hit the post in the ninetieth minute.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E o guarda-redes deles esteve bem?
lines.en: And was their goalkeeper good?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Esteve enorme. Estivemos quase a marcar três vezes e ele defendeu tudo.
lines.en: He was huge. We were about to score three times and he saved everything.

days.title: Portuguese music: understanding lyrics
days.objective: Understand sung Portuguese by recognising reduced forms, figurative images and inverted word order in lyrics.
days.paretoFocus: The reductions singers use are exactly the ones fast speakers use, so decoding lyrics trains you for real conversation speed.
drills: Say aloud five full forms and their sung reductions, for example 'está' and 'tá'.
Choose a Portuguese song you like and write down three words you catch without help.
Write two sentences about feelings using an image rather than a plain adjective.

items: What full word is hidden behind the sung form 'tá'?
Which noun names the feeling of longing so common in Portuguese songs?
What can you use to guess a word you cannot hear at the end of a line?

activities.title: Making sense of lyrics
activities.intro: Sung Portuguese drops unstressed sounds and reorders words to fit the melody, which is why a familiar sentence can sound unrecognisable. Learning the common reductions and listening for the rhyme lets you reconstruct what you did not catch. Lyrics also lean heavily on images rather than plain description.

items.hr: Nas canções, 'está' aparece muitas vezes como 'tá' e 'para' como 'pra'.
items.en: In songs, 'está' often appears as 'tá' and 'para' as 'pra'.
items.note: unstressed first syllables drop in fast or sung speech

items.hr: O fado fala muitas vezes de saudade, de mar e de despedidas.
items.en: Fado often speaks of longing, of the sea and of farewells.
items.note: saudade: the feeling of missing someone or something

items.hr: A letra diz que o coração dela ficou preso ao cais.
items.en: The lyrics say that her heart stayed tied to the quay.
items.note: images replace plain adjectives: preso ao cais = unable to move on

items.hr: Quando não percebo uma palavra, uso a rima para adivinhar o som.
items.en: When I do not catch a word, I use the rhyme to guess the sound.
items.note: a rima = the rhyme; adivinhar = to guess

items.hr: Muitas letras trocam a ordem das palavras: 'ao mar voltei' em vez de 'voltei ao mar'.
items.en: Many lyrics swap the word order: 'ao mar voltei' instead of 'voltei ao mar'.
items.note: the complement can move in front of the verb for rhythm

activities.title: From the lyrics to the meaning
activities.intro: Practise recognising sung reductions, images and inverted order in lyrics.

questions.prompt: In sung Portuguese, the form 'tá' is a reduction of which full word?
questions.explanation: The unstressed first syllable of 'está' disappears, leaving 'tá'. The other words keep their first syllable.

questions.prompt: Which noun names the feeling of longing that so many Portuguese songs describe?
questions.explanation: 'Saudade' is missing someone or something absent. 'Vontade' is a wish, 'novidade' news and 'liberdade' freedom.

questions.prompt: Supply the sung reduction of 'para a' that you would hear in a song: 'Vou ___ beira-mar contigo.'
questions.explanation: 'Para a' collapses to 'pra' in sung and informal speech, keeping only one syllable.

questions.prompt: Supply the noun for the sound match at the end of two lines: 'Quando não apanho a palavra, sigo a ___ do verso anterior.'
questions.explanation: 'A rima' is the rhyme, and it narrows down the possible endings of the missing word.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'The lyrics speak of the sea and of farewells.'
questions.explanation: 'Falar de' contracts with the article: de + o gives 'do', de + as gives 'das'.

questions.prompt: Play the audio and complete: 'Nas ___, 'está' aparece muitas vezes como 'tá' e 'para' como 'pra'.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Nas canções, 'está' aparece muitas vezes como 'tá' e 'para' como 'pra'.', which means 'In songs, 'está' often appears as 'tá' and 'para' as 'pra'.'
questions.audioText: Nas canções, 'está' aparece muitas vezes como 'tá' e 'para' como 'pra'.

activities.title: What does that song say?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend cannot follow a song in Portuguese and you explain the reductions and the images in the lyrics.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Gosto da música, mas não apanho metade das palavras. É normal?
lines.en: I like the song, but I do not catch half the words. Is that normal?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É normalíssimo. Quando ela canta 'tá', está a dizer 'está'. Come a primeira sílaba.
lines.en: It is completely normal. When she sings 'tá', she is saying 'está'. She swallows the first syllable.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E aquele 'pra' que aparece a toda a hora?
lines.en: And that 'pra' that comes up all the time?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É 'para a'. Na fala rápida também dizemos assim, não é só nas canções.
lines.en: It is 'para a'. In fast speech we say it like that too, it is not only in songs.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E o refrão fala de um coração preso ao cais. Isso é literal?
lines.en: And the chorus speaks of a heart tied to the quay. Is that literal?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não, é uma imagem. Quer dizer que ela ficou à espera de alguém que partiu.
lines.en: No, it is an image. It means she stayed waiting for someone who left.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Há um verso que soa todo ao contrário.
lines.en: There is a line that sounds all back to front.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pois é, 'ao mar voltei'. Trocam a ordem para a frase caber na melodia.
lines.en: That is right, 'ao mar voltei'. They swap the order so the phrase fits the melody.

days.title: O cinema: contar e criticar um filme
days.objective: Summarise a film's plot in the present tense and judge it using the vocabulary of directing, script, cast and soundtrack.
days.paretoFocus: Retelling a story in the present and giving a balanced judgement is exactly what conversations about books, series and news events also require.
drills: Summarise a film you know in three present-tense sentences without revealing the ending.
Write one sentence praising one aspect and criticising another with 'mas'.
List the Portuguese words for script, directing, cast and soundtrack.

items: Which tense do you use to summarise a plot?
What is the Portuguese word for the script of a film?
How do you say 'the soundtrack'?

activities.title: Recounting and reviewing a film
activities.intro: A plot summary in Portuguese is told in the present tense, however old the film is. To judge it you separate the parts: 'a realização' is the directing, 'o argumento' the script, 'o elenco' the cast and 'a banda sonora' the soundtrack. A balanced review praises one part and criticises another.

items.hr: O filme conta a história de uma médica que volta à aldeia onde nasceu.
items.en: The film tells the story of a doctor who returns to the village where she was born.
items.note: contar a história de: standard opening for a summary

items.hr: A meio da história, ela descobre um segredo de família.
items.en: Halfway through the story, she discovers a family secret.
items.note: a meio de = halfway through

items.hr: A realização é excelente, mas o argumento é fraco na segunda parte.
items.en: The directing is excellent, but the script is weak in the second half.
items.note: realização = directing; argumento = script

items.hr: O que mais me agradou foi a banda sonora e o trabalho do elenco.
items.en: What pleased me most was the soundtrack and the work of the cast.
items.note: agradar a alguém = to please someone

items.hr: No fim, fica tudo em aberto, o que me deixou algo frustrado.
items.en: At the end, everything is left open, which left me somewhat frustrated.
items.note: ficar em aberto = to be left unresolved

activities.title: Talking about a film
activities.intro: Practise the vocabulary of film criticism and the present tense used for plot summaries.

questions.prompt: Which Portuguese word names the written script of a film?
questions.explanation: 'O argumento' is the screenplay. 'A realização' is the directing, 'o elenco' the cast and 'a estreia' the premiere.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'A ___ sonora deste filme é inesquecível.'
questions.explanation: The fixed term is 'banda sonora'. 'Faixa' is an individual track and the other two do not combine with 'sonora'.

questions.prompt: Supply the present-tense verb used to open a plot summary: 'O filme ___ a história de dois irmãos.'
questions.explanation: Plot summaries stay in the present, so 'contar' appears as 'conta' in the third person singular.

questions.prompt: Supply the noun for the work done by the director: 'A ___ é cuidada, cada plano parece um quadro.'
questions.explanation: In Portuguese the director's craft is 'a realização', from 'realizador'.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'What pleased me most was the ending.'
questions.explanation: The cleft structure 'O que ... foi ...' highlights one element, and 'agradar' takes an indirect object pronoun.

questions.prompt: Listen closely and fill the gap: 'A meio da ___, ela descobre um segredo de família.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'A meio da história, ela descobre um segredo de família.', which means 'Halfway through the story, she discovers a family secret.'
questions.audioText: A meio da história, ela descobre um segredo de família.

activities.title: Vale a pena ver?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend asks about a film you saw and you summarise it in the present and give a balanced judgement.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Viste aquele filme português de que toda a gente fala. É bom?
lines.en: You saw that Portuguese film everybody is talking about. Is it good?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Conta a história de uma médica que volta à aldeia onde nasceu.
lines.en: It tells the story of a doctor who returns to the village where she was born.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E acontece alguma coisa ou é só paisagem?
lines.en: And does anything happen or is it just scenery?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A meio da história, ela descobre um segredo de família. Não digo mais nada.
lines.en: Halfway through the story, she discovers a family secret. I will not say anything else.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E tecnicamente, está bem feito?
lines.en: And technically, is it well made?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A realização é excelente, mas o argumento perde força na segunda parte.
lines.en: The directing is excellent, but the script loses strength in the second half.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então saíste desiludido?
lines.en: So you came out disappointed?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Nem por isso. O que mais me agradou foi a banda sonora, e por isso vale a ida ao cinema.
lines.en: Not really. What pleased me most was the soundtrack, and for that reason the trip to the cinema is worth it.

days.title: Reading a short story: reading strategies
days.objective: Read a short story efficiently by guessing words from context and by recognising the pluperfect that signals an earlier past.
days.paretoFocus: Reading without stopping at every new word is the single habit that turns slow decoding into real reading speed.
drills: Read one page of any Portuguese text without a dictionary and underline unknown words instead of stopping.
Write two sentences with 'tinha' plus a past participle about things that had happened before another event.
Guess the meaning of three underlined words from context, then check them.

items: Which form places an action before another past action?
What do you do with a new word on a first reading?
What two things do you look for on a second reading?

activities.title: Reading a short story
activities.intro: Short stories jump backwards in time, and Portuguese marks that jump with 'tinha' plus a past participle, the compound pluperfect. Reading strategy matters as much as grammar: on a first pass you underline and keep going, and only on a second pass do you check words and identify the narrator and the setting.

items.hr: Antes de ler, olho para o título e imagino de que trata o conto.
items.en: Before reading, I look at the title and imagine what the story is about.
items.note: tratar de = to be about

items.hr: Quando o narrador diz que ela tinha partido, percebo que isso aconteceu antes.
items.en: When the narrator says that she had left, I understand that this happened earlier.
items.note: tinha + particípio = the earlier of two past events

items.hr: Não paro em cada palavra nova, sublinho e continuo até ao fim do parágrafo.
items.en: I do not stop at every new word, I underline it and carry on to the end of the paragraph.
items.note: sublinhar = to underline

items.hr: Pelo contexto, percebi que 'trémulo' queria dizer que ele tremia.
items.en: From the context, I understood that 'trémulo' meant that he was trembling.
items.note: pelo contexto = from the context; querer dizer = to mean

items.hr: Na segunda leitura, procuro quem conta a história e onde se passa.
items.en: On the second reading, I look for who tells the story and where it takes place.
items.note: passar-se = to take place

activities.title: Strategies and the tenses of a story
activities.intro: Practise the pluperfect and the vocabulary of reading strategies.

questions.prompt: Which form places one action before another action already in the past?
questions.explanation: 'Tinha' plus a past participle is the compound pluperfect, used for the earlier of two past events.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Quando cheguei ao café, ele já ___ saído.'
questions.explanation: The auxiliary of the compound pluperfect is 'ter' in the imperfeito, so 'tinha saído'.

questions.prompt: Supply the noun for the surrounding words that help you guess a meaning: 'Percebi a palavra nova pelo ___ da frase.'
questions.explanation: 'Pelo contexto' is the standard way to say you worked the meaning out from the surrounding text.

questions.prompt: Supply the past participle of 'escrever': 'O conto tinha sido ___ há mais de cinquenta anos.'
questions.explanation: 'Escrever' has the irregular participle 'escrito', with no ending in 'ido'.
