questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'Before reading, I look at the title.'
questions.explanation: 'Antes de' is followed by the infinitive, and 'olhar' requires 'para' before its object.

questions.prompt: Type the word you hear: 'Pelo ___, percebi que 'trémulo' queria dizer que ele tremia.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Pelo contexto, percebi que 'trémulo' queria dizer que ele tremia.', which means 'From the context, I understood that 'trémulo' meant that he was trembling.'
questions.audioText: Pelo contexto, percebi que 'trémulo' queria dizer que ele tremia.

activities.title: Is that story difficult?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend is stuck on a short story and you share your reading strategy, using the pluperfect to explain the time jumps.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Comecei o conto e desisti na primeira página. Havia palavras a mais.
lines.en: I started the story and gave up on the first page. There were too many words I did not know.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não pares em cada palavra. Sublinha e continua até ao fim do parágrafo.
lines.en: Do not stop at every word. Underline it and carry on to the end of the paragraph.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Mas assim não percebo nada.
lines.en: But that way I do not understand anything.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Percebes mais do que pensas. Pelo contexto, quase sempre se adivinha o sentido.
lines.en: You understand more than you think. From the context, you can almost always guess the meaning.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Há uma parte em que ele fala do passado e eu perco-me.
lines.en: There is a part where he talks about the past and I get lost.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Repara nos verbos. Quando diz que ela tinha partido, é porque isso aconteceu antes do resto.
lines.en: Look at the verbs. When it says that she had left, it is because that happened before the rest.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E vale a pena ler outra vez do início?
lines.en: And is it worth reading again from the start?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale. Na segunda leitura procura só quem conta a história e onde se passa.
lines.en: It is. On the second reading just look for who tells the story and where it takes place.

days.title: Wishes, regrets and intentions
days.objective: Express wishes, regrets and intentions with 'quem me dera que', 'arrepender-se de ter', 'devia ter' and 'tencionar'.
days.paretoFocus: Wishes and regrets carry most of the emotional weight in personal conversation, and 'devia ter' is the standard way to apologise properly.
drills: Write two regrets about the past with 'devia ter' plus a participle.
Write two wishes using 'quem me dera que' followed by the imperfect subjunctive.
State three intentions for the next twelve months using 'tenciono'.

items: How do you say 'I should have warned you'?
Which mood follows 'quem me dera que'?
Which verb means 'to intend' in a slightly formal register?

activities.title: If only...
activities.intro: Portuguese has one pattern for each of these three ideas. A wish about an unreal present uses 'quem me dera que' plus the imperfect subjunctive; a regret uses 'arrepender-se de ter' or 'devia ter' plus the past participle; an intention uses 'tencionar' plus the infinitive.

items.hr: Gostaria de ter estudado português muito mais cedo.
items.en: I would like to have studied Portuguese much earlier.
items.note: gostaria de ter + particípio = a wish about the past

items.hr: Quem me dera que os dias tivessem mais duas horas.
items.en: I wish the days had two more hours.
items.note: quem me dera que + imperfeito do conjuntivo: ter becomes tivessem

items.hr: Arrependo-me de não ter aceitado aquele convite.
items.en: I regret not having accepted that invitation.
items.note: arrepender-se de + infinitivo composto

items.hr: Devia ter avisado, peço imensa desculpa.
items.en: I should have warned you, I am terribly sorry.
items.note: devia ter + particípio = should have done

items.hr: Tenciono mudar de cidade no próximo ano.
items.en: I intend to move to another city next year.
items.note: tencionar + infinitivo, slightly more formal than 'pensar em'

activities.title: What I would do differently
activities.intro: Practise the structures for wishes, regrets and intentions.

questions.prompt: Which structure expresses regret about something you failed to do?
questions.explanation: 'Devia ter' plus a participle looks back at an unfulfilled obligation. The others refer to the present or the future.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Quem me dera que ele ___ aqui connosco agora.'
questions.explanation: 'Quem me dera que' presents the wish as unreal, so it takes the imperfect subjunctive 'estivesse'.

questions.prompt: Supply the verb that states a plan in a formal register: '___ mudar de emprego no verão.'
questions.explanation: 'Tencionar' plus the infinitive announces an intention and is common in careful speech and writing.

questions.prompt: Supply the reflexive verb of regret in the first person: '___-me de não ter ido à festa dela.'
questions.explanation: 'Arrepender-se de' is reflexive, so the first person singular is 'arrependo-me de'.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I would like to have studied more.'
questions.explanation: The conditional of 'gostar' takes 'de' plus the compound infinitive 'ter estudado' for a wish about the past.

questions.prompt: Listen and complete the sentence: 'Gostaria de ter estudado ___ muito mais cedo.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Gostaria de ter estudado português muito mais cedo.', which means 'I would like to have studied Portuguese much earlier.'
questions.audioText: Gostaria de ter estudado português muito mais cedo.

questions.prompt: Say it in Portuguese, in writing: 'I intend to move to another city next year.'
questions.answer: Tenciono mudar de cidade no próximo ano.
questions.explanation: 'I intend to move to another city next year.' is 'Tenciono mudar de cidade no próximo ano.'

activities.title: If I could go back
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend asks what you would change and you answer with wishes, regrets and intentions.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Se pudesses voltar atrás dez anos, o que farias de diferente?
lines.en: If you could go back ten years, what would you do differently?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Gostaria de ter estudado línguas mais cedo. Agora custa-me muito mais.
lines.en: I would like to have studied languages earlier. Now it is much harder for me.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Mais alguma coisa te ficou atravessada?
lines.en: Is there anything else that still bothers you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Arrependo-me de não ter aceitado um trabalho no estrangeiro em 2018.
lines.en: I regret not having accepted a job abroad in 2018.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ainda vais a tempo, não vais?
lines.en: You are still in time, are you not?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Talvez. Tenciono candidatar-me outra vez no início do ano.
lines.en: Perhaps. I intend to apply again at the start of the year.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E o que te falta para decidires?
lines.en: And what do you need in order to decide?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tempo. Quem me dera que os dias tivessem mais duas horas.
lines.en: Time. I wish the days had two more hours.

days.title: Shading an opinion: softening and insisting
days.objective: Soften or reinforce an opinion using 'se calhar', 'talvez' with the subjunctive, 'de certo modo', 'sem dúvida' and 'fazer questão de'.
days.paretoFocus: Knowing how strongly to state an opinion decides whether you sound rude, vague or convincing, and it costs only a handful of set phrases.
drills: State one opinion three times: hedged, neutral and emphatic.
Write two sentences with 'talvez' plus the present subjunctive.
Say aloud one point you would insist on, using 'faço questão de'.

items: Which two-word phrase softens a statement at the start of a sentence?
Which mood follows 'talvez'?
How do you say 'I insist on saying' in Portuguese?

activities.title: Atenuar e insistir
activities.intro: Portuguese speakers rarely state a strong opinion flat. To soften they use 'se calhar', 'talvez' plus the subjunctive, and 'de certo modo'; to reinforce they use 'fazer questão de' and 'sem dúvida'. Note that 'talvez' before the verb requires the subjunctive.

items.hr: Se calhar estou enganado, mas parece-me que a ideia não resulta.
items.en: Maybe I am wrong, but it seems to me that the idea does not work.
items.note: se calhar = maybe; resultar = to work out

items.hr: Talvez seja melhor esperar mais uns dias antes de decidir.
items.en: Perhaps it is better to wait a few more days before deciding.
items.note: talvez before the verb takes the conjuntivo: seja, not é

items.hr: De certo modo, tens razão, embora eu veja as coisas de outra maneira.
items.en: In a way, you are right, although I see things differently.
items.note: de certo modo = in a way, up to a point

items.hr: Sem dúvida que este é o caminho certo, e insisto nisso.
items.en: This is without doubt the right path, and I insist on that.
items.note: insistir em: em + isso gives nisso

items.hr: Faço questão de dizer que não estou contra a proposta.
items.en: I make a point of saying that I am not against the proposal.
items.note: fazer questão de + infinitivo = to insist on doing

activities.title: Stronger or softer?
activities.intro: Practise choosing between hedging phrases and emphatic ones.

questions.prompt: Which expression signals that the speaker is certain rather than hesitant?
questions.explanation: 'Sem dúvida' asserts certainty; the other three all weaken the claim to different degrees.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Talvez ___ melhor falarmos disto amanhã.'
questions.explanation: 'Talvez' placed before the verb requires the present subjunctive, so 'ser' becomes 'seja'.

questions.prompt: Supply the missing noun: 'De certo ___, concordo contigo, mas tenho algumas reservas.'
questions.explanation: 'De certo modo' means 'in a way' and softens an agreement that is only partial.

questions.prompt: Supply the two words that hedge the opening of this claim: '___ ___ estou enganado, mas os números não batem certo.'
questions.explanation: 'Se calhar' is the everyday European Portuguese hedge and, unlike 'talvez', takes the indicative.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'Perhaps it is better to wait.'
questions.explanation: 'Talvez' comes first, the subjunctive 'seja' follows, and the infinitive closes the phrase.

questions.prompt: Listen, then type the missing word: 'Se calhar estou ___, mas parece-me que a ideia não resulta.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Se calhar estou enganado, mas parece-me que a ideia não resulta.', which means 'Maybe I am wrong, but it seems to me that the idea does not work.'
questions.audioText: Se calhar estou enganado, mas parece-me que a ideia não resulta.

activities.title: Disagreeing, tactfully
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A colleague defends a plan and you disagree, first softening your objection and then insisting on one point.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Acho que devíamos avançar já com o projeto esta semana.
lines.en: I think we should go ahead with the project this week.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Se calhar estou enganado, mas parece-me cedo de mais.
lines.en: Maybe I am wrong, but it seems too early to me.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Cedo? Já estamos a discutir isto há um mês.
lines.en: Too early? We have been discussing this for a month already.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: De certo modo, tens razão. Ainda assim, talvez seja melhor ouvir a equipa toda.
lines.en: In a way, you are right. Even so, perhaps it is better to hear the whole team.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Isso atrasa-nos mais duas semanas.
lines.en: That delays us another two weeks.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Faço questão de ouvir quem vai executar o trabalho. Nisso não abro mão.
lines.en: I make a point of hearing the people who will do the work. On that I will not give way.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Está bem. E depois disso avançamos?
lines.en: All right. And after that we go ahead?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sem dúvida. Com a equipa de acordo, o projeto anda muito mais depressa.
lines.en: Without doubt. With the team in agreement, the project moves much faster.

days.title: Structuring a three-minute talk
days.objective: Structure a short spoken presentation with signposting phrases that announce, connect and close each part.
days.paretoFocus: Signposting makes a listener follow you even when your grammar slips, and the same phrases work in meetings, classes and interviews.
drills: Plan a three minute talk in three points and write the opening sentence for each.
Say the whole talk out loud once, timing yourself with a clock.
Rewrite your closing line so it ends with a question to the audience.

items: Which phrase announces that you are moving to the next point?
How do you say 'as I already mentioned'?
Which pronoun form attaches to 'deixo' when addressing a group?

activities.title: Structuring a talk
activities.intro: A short talk in Portuguese lives or dies by its signposts: they tell the listener where you are. 'Em primeiro lugar' opens, 'passo agora a' moves on, 'como já referi' refers back and 'para concluir' closes. Note the enclitic pronoun in 'deixo-vos', normal in careful spoken Portuguese.

items.hr: Em primeiro lugar, gostava de explicar porque escolhi este tema.
items.en: First of all, I would like to explain why I chose this topic.
items.note: gostava de is the everyday equivalent of gostaria de

items.hr: Vou dividir a minha apresentação em três partes muito curtas.
items.en: I am going to divide my presentation into three very short parts.
items.note: dividir em, never dividir a

items.hr: Passo agora ao segundo ponto, que tem a ver com os custos.
items.en: I now move on to the second point, which has to do with the costs.
items.note: passar a + noun; ter a ver com = to have to do with

items.hr: Como já referi, os dados que uso são deste ano.
items.en: As I already mentioned, the data I am using are from this year.
items.note: de + este contracts to deste

items.hr: Para concluir, deixo-vos uma pergunta para pensarem.
items.en: To conclude, I leave you a question to think about.
items.note: enclisis: the pronoun follows the verb in an affirmative main clause

activities.title: Signposting a talk
activities.intro: Practise the phrases that signpost the parts of a spoken presentation.

questions.prompt: Which phrase announces that the speaker is moving to the next section?
questions.explanation: 'Passar a' plus the next point is the standard transition. The other options express chance, frequency and concession.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Para ___, queria deixar uma ideia final.'
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'para' Portuguese uses the infinitive, so 'concluir'.

questions.prompt: Supply the ordinal that opens the first section of a talk: 'Em ___ lugar, vou apresentar-me.'
questions.explanation: 'Em primeiro lugar' is the fixed opening formula, and the ordinal agrees with the masculine 'lugar'.

questions.prompt: Supply the enclitic pronoun for addressing the whole audience: 'Para terminar, deixo-___ uma pergunta.'
questions.explanation: 'Vos' is the second person plural object pronoun and attaches to the verb with a hyphen after an affirmative verb.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I am going to divide my presentation into three parts.'
questions.explanation: The possessive takes the article in European Portuguese, and 'dividir' requires 'em'.

questions.prompt: Listen and fill in the word you hear: 'Em ___ lugar, gostava de explicar porque escolhi este tema.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Em primeiro lugar, gostava de explicar porque escolhi este tema.', which means 'First of all, I would like to explain why I chose this topic.'
questions.audioText: Em primeiro lugar, gostava de explicar porque escolhi este tema.

questions.prompt: Type the Portuguese for: 'To conclude, I leave you a question to think about.'
questions.answer: Para concluir, deixo-vos uma pergunta para pensarem.
questions.explanation: 'To conclude, I leave you a question to think about.' is 'Para concluir, deixo-vos uma pergunta para pensarem.'

activities.title: Rehearsing before you present
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A colleague helps you rehearse and you answer using the signposting phrases of a short talk.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tens três minutos. Como é que pensas organizar isso?
lines.en: You have three minutes. How are you planning to organise that?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vou dividir a apresentação em três partes: o problema, os custos e a proposta.
lines.en: I am going to divide the presentation into three parts: the problem, the costs and the proposal.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E como começas?
lines.en: And how do you begin?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Em primeiro lugar, explico porque escolhi este tema, em duas frases apenas.
lines.en: First of all, I explain why I chose this topic, in two sentences only.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Cuidado com a passagem para os números, é aí que as pessoas se perdem.
lines.en: Be careful with the transition to the figures, that is where people get lost.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Por isso digo em voz alta: passo agora ao segundo ponto, que tem a ver com os custos.
lines.en: That is why I say out loud: I now move on to the second point, which has to do with the costs.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E o fim? Não acabes a pedir desculpa.
lines.en: And the end? Do not finish by apologising.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Para concluir, deixo-vos uma pergunta. Assim a discussão começa logo ali.
lines.en: To conclude, I leave you a question. That way the discussion starts right there.

days.title: Listening: picking out the essential information
days.objective: Apply a listening routine that captures the essential information of a recording before, during and after it plays.
days.paretoFocus: In any listening test the marks are lost between recordings, not during them, so the routine matters more than raw comprehension.
drills: Take any short Portuguese recording, read the questions first and underline the key words.
Listen once for topic and speakers only, writing nothing but two words.
Listen a second time and complete your answers, noting every number you hear.

items: What do you do before the recording starts?
What are you listening for on the first play?
What should you do if you miss one answer?

activities.title: Listening for the gist
activities.intro: Listening tasks are won with a routine, not with speed. Before the audio you read the questions and underline the key words; on the first play you catch only the topic and the speakers; on the second you confirm and fill the gaps. Numbers and times are said fast, so write them the moment you hear them.

items.hr: Antes de ouvir, leio as perguntas e sublinho as palavras-chave.
items.en: Before listening, I read the questions and underline the key words.
items.note: palavras-chave: the plural falls on the first element

items.hr: Na primeira audição, procuro apenas o tema geral e quem está a falar.
items.en: On the first play, I look only for the general topic and who is speaking.
items.note: a audição = the listening, the play of a recording

items.hr: Os números e as horas são ditos depressa, por isso escrevo-os logo.
items.en: Numbers and times are said fast, so I write them down straight away.
items.note: escrevo-os: enclitic o becomes os agreeing with the plural

items.hr: Se perder uma resposta, não paro, continuo para não perder as seguintes.
items.en: If I miss an answer, I do not stop, I carry on so as not to miss the following ones.
items.note: se perder: future subjunctive after se

items.hr: Na segunda audição, confirmo o que escrevi e completo o que faltava.
items.en: On the second play, I confirm what I wrote and complete what was missing.
items.note: faltava: imperfeito for what was still missing at that moment

activities.title: A listening routine
activities.intro: Practise the vocabulary and the sequence of an effective listening routine.

questions.prompt: What should you do in the seconds before a recording starts?
options: Ler as perguntas e sublinhar as palavras-chave
Traduzir tudo para a sua língua
questions.answer: Ler as perguntas e sublinhar as palavras-chave
questions.explanation: Reading the questions first tells you what to listen for, which is the only preparation that changes your score.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Na primeira ___, procuro só o tema geral.'
questions.explanation: 'Audição' is the act of listening to a recording; 'leitura' is reading and 'escrita' writing.

questions.prompt: Supply the second element of the compound noun for the important words in a question: 'Sublinho as palavras-___ antes de ouvir.'
questions.explanation: In 'palavras-chave' only the first element takes the plural, so the second stays 'chave'.

questions.prompt: Supply the future subjunctive of a verb meaning to lose or to miss something: 'Se ___ uma resposta, sigo em frente.'
questions.explanation: After 'se' referring to the future Portuguese uses the future subjunctive, which for this verb looks like the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I write the numbers down immediately on the paper.'
questions.explanation: The adverb sits after the object, and 'em' plus 'o' contracts to 'no'.

questions.prompt: Play the audio and complete: 'Antes de ouvir, leio as ___ e sublinho as palavras-chave.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Antes de ouvir, leio as perguntas e sublinho as palavras-chave.', which means 'Before listening, I read the questions and underline the key words.'
questions.audioText: Antes de ouvir, leio as perguntas e sublinho as palavras-chave.

activities.title: I missed half the recording
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A study partner panics about listening tasks and you explain your routine step by step.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Na parte de audição perco-me sempre. Ouço tudo e não fico com nada.
lines.en: In the listening part I always get lost. I hear everything and I end up with nothing.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Antes de a gravação começar, lê as perguntas e sublinha as palavras-chave.
lines.en: Before the recording starts, read the questions and underline the key words.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Mas há pouco tempo para isso.
lines.en: But there is little time for that.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Chega. Na primeira audição procura só o tema e quem fala, não escrevas frases.
lines.en: It is enough. On the first play look only for the topic and who is speaking, do not write sentences.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E as datas e os preços? Passam a correr.
lines.en: And the dates and the prices? They go by in a flash.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Escreve-os no momento em que os ouves, mesmo que ainda não saibas a pergunta.
lines.en: Write them down the moment you hear them, even if you do not yet know the question.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E se falhar uma resposta, volto atrás mentalmente?
lines.en: And if I miss an answer, do I go back over it in my head?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Nunca. Se perderes uma, segue em frente e recupera-a na segunda audição.
lines.en: Never. If you miss one, carry on and pick it up on the second play.

days.title: Writing: the argued email
days.objective: Write a formal argued email that opens properly, balances two arguments and closes with a request and a formal sign-off.
days.paretoFocus: The same four moves, formal opening, one argument each side, request, sign-off, cover complaints, applications and requests to any institution.
drills: Write a five line email disagreeing with a rule, using one 'por um lado' and one 'por outro lado'.
Rewrite your request sentence with 'peço que' plus the subjunctive.
Practise the formal opening and closing formulas from memory, without looking.

items: How do you open a formal written complaint?
Which mood follows 'peço que'?
What is the standard formal sign-off in Portuguese?

activities.title: Writing an argued email
activities.intro: A formal argued email in Portuguese follows a fixed shape. It opens with 'Venho por este meio', develops two sides with 'por um lado' and 'por outro lado', makes its request with 'peço que' plus the subjunctive, and closes with a set formula. The register stays impersonal throughout.

items.hr: Venho por este meio manifestar o meu desacordo com a nova regra.
items.en: I am writing to express my disagreement with the new rule.
items.note: venho por este meio + infinitivo: standard formal opening

items.hr: Por um lado, a medida prejudica quem trabalha por turnos.
items.en: On the one hand, the measure harms those who work shifts.
items.note: prejudicar = to harm; por turnos = on shifts

items.hr: Por outro lado, existem alternativas mais simples e menos dispendiosas.
items.en: On the other hand, there are simpler and less costly alternatives.
items.note: dispendioso is the formal word for expensive

items.hr: Por tudo isto, peço que a decisão seja revista com brevidade.
items.en: For all these reasons, I ask that the decision be reviewed shortly.
items.note: pedir que + conjuntivo; passive with ser plus participle

items.hr: Fico a aguardar uma resposta. Com os melhores cumprimentos,
items.en: I look forward to a reply. Kind regards,
items.note: ficar a aguardar; the sign-off ends with a comma before the name

activities.title: The parts of a formal email
activities.intro: Practise the openings, connectors and closings of a formal argued email.

questions.prompt: Which opening suits a formal written complaint to an institution?
options: Aqui vai o que eu penso
questions.explanation: Only this option keeps the impersonal formal register; the others address the reader informally.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Peço que a decisão ___ revista o mais depressa possível.'
questions.explanation: 'Pedir que' requires the subjunctive, and the passive is built with 'ser' plus the participle, giving 'seja revista'.

questions.prompt: Supply the missing word so the pair of arguments is balanced: 'Por um lado, é caro; por ___ lado, resolve o problema.'
questions.explanation: The fixed pair is 'por um lado ... por outro lado', used to present two sides of the same question.

questions.prompt: Supply the noun that completes the standard formal sign-off: 'Com os melhores ___,'
questions.explanation: 'Com os melhores cumprimentos' is the usual formal closing in European Portuguese correspondence.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I look forward to your reply.'
questions.explanation: 'Ficar a aguardar' uses the European Portuguese progressive with 'a', and 'vossa' addresses an institution.

questions.prompt: Listen closely and fill the gap: 'Venho por este meio ___ o meu desacordo com a nova regra.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Venho por este meio manifestar o meu desacordo com a nova regra.', which means 'I am writing to express my disagreement with the new rule.'
questions.audioText: Venho por este meio manifestar o meu desacordo com a nova regra.

questions.prompt: Say it in Portuguese, in writing: 'I look forward to a reply. Kind regards,'
questions.answer: Fico a aguardar uma resposta. Com os melhores cumprimentos,
questions.explanation: 'I look forward to a reply. Kind regards,' is 'Fico a aguardar uma resposta. Com os melhores cumprimentos,'

activities.title: Checking the email before you send it
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A study partner has drafted a formal email and you correct its structure and register.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Escrevi o e-mail. Comecei com 'Olá, queria só dizer que não concordo'.
lines.en: I wrote the email. I started with 'Hi, I just wanted to say that I disagree'.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Isso é demasiado informal. Escreve antes: venho por este meio manifestar o meu desacordo.
lines.en: That is too informal. Write instead: I am writing to express my disagreement.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Depois pus três razões todas seguidas.
lines.en: Then I put three reasons one after the other.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Fica melhor com dois lados: por um lado, o problema; por outro lado, a alternativa.
lines.en: It works better with two sides: on the one hand the problem, on the other hand the alternative.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E no fim escrevi 'mudem isso, por favor'.
lines.en: And at the end I wrote 'change that, please'.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Um pedido formal fica assim: peço que a decisão seja revista.
lines.en: A formal request goes like this: I ask that the decision be reviewed.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E assino como? Pus só o meu nome.
lines.en: And how do I sign off? I just put my name.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Acrescenta uma linha antes: fico a aguardar uma resposta, com os melhores cumprimentos.
lines.en: Add a line before it: I look forward to a reply, kind regards.

days.title: Treinar o oral: simulação guiada
days.objective: Keep a spoken interaction going by paraphrasing unknown words, buying time politely, asking for repetition and justifying every opinion.
days.paretoFocus: In speaking tasks and in real life, fluency is judged on whether you keep going, not on whether you know every word.
drills: Describe five objects without naming them, using 'é uma coisa que serve para'.
Answer three opinion questions out loud, adding a concrete example each time.
Practise three ways of buying time before answering a difficult question.

items: How do you politely ask someone to repeat a question?
What do you say to buy a few seconds before answering?
What should follow every opinion you give?

activities.title: Keeping talking
activities.intro: Speaking well under pressure is mostly a set of repair strategies. When a word escapes you, describe it instead; when you need a second, use a filler; when you did not catch the question, ask politely for a repetition. Every opinion should be followed by a concrete example.

items.hr: Se não me lembro de uma palavra, explico-a por outras palavras.
items.en: If I do not remember a word, I explain it in other words.
items.note: lembrar-se de; explico-a: enclitic pronoun for a feminine noun

items.hr: Ganho tempo com expressões como 'deixe-me pensar' ou 'é uma boa pergunta'.
items.en: I buy time with expressions such as 'let me think' or 'that is a good question'.
items.note: deixe-me pensar: formal you; deixa-me pensar with tu

items.hr: Quando não percebo a pergunta, digo: importa-se de repetir?
items.en: When I do not understand the question, I say: would you mind repeating?
items.note: importar-se de + infinitivo: polite request

items.hr: Justifico sempre a minha opinião com um exemplo concreto.
items.en: I always back up my opinion with a concrete example.
items.note: justificar com = to back up with

items.hr: No fim, faço um resumo curto do que disse em duas frases.
items.en: At the end, I make a short summary of what I said in two sentences.
items.note: fazer um resumo de = to summarise

activities.title: Strategies for not drying up
activities.intro: Practise the repair and time-buying strategies of a guided speaking simulation.

questions.prompt: Which phrase politely asks the other person to say the question again?
questions.explanation: 'Importar-se de' plus the infinitive is the polite way to ask a favour of someone you address formally.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Deixe-me ___ um momento antes de responder.'
questions.explanation: 'Deixar' plus another verb takes the infinitive, so 'deixe-me pensar'.

questions.prompt: Supply the first person verb of the paraphrase strategy: 'Se não sei a palavra exata, ___ a ideia por outras palavras.'
questions.explanation: 'Explicar por outras palavras' is the standard way to describe paraphrasing, here in the first person singular.

questions.prompt: Supply the noun for the piece of evidence that should follow an opinion: 'Justifico sempre a minha opinião com um ___ concreto.'
questions.explanation: An opinion in a speaking task counts for much more when it is supported by 'um exemplo concreto'.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'At the end, I summarise what I said.'
questions.explanation: 'Resumir' takes a direct object, and 'o que' introduces the free relative clause with no preposition.

questions.prompt: Type the word you hear: 'Se não me lembro de uma palavra, explico-a por outras ___.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Se não me lembro de uma palavra, explico-a por outras palavras.', which means 'If I do not remember a word, I explain it in other words.'
questions.audioText: Se não me lembro de uma palavra, explico-a por outras palavras.

questions.prompt: Put this into Portuguese: 'I always back up my opinion with a concrete example.'
questions.answer: Justifico sempre a minha opinião com um exemplo concreto.
questions.explanation: 'I always back up my opinion with a concrete example.' is 'Justifico sempre a minha opinião com um exemplo concreto.'

activities.title: Simulation: two minutes of talking
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. An examiner-style partner runs a short speaking simulation and you use repair strategies to keep going.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa tarde. Fale-me de um objeto de que não conseguiria prescindir.
lines.en: Good afternoon. Tell me about an object you could not do without.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Deixe-me pensar um momento. É uma coisa pequena que serve para ver as horas e as mensagens.
lines.en: Let me think for a moment. It is a small thing that is used to see the time and messages.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Está a falar do telemóvel?
lines.en: Are you talking about the mobile phone?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Exatamente, o telemóvel. Não vivo sem ele porque trabalho fora todos os dias.
lines.en: Exactly, the mobile phone. I cannot live without it because I work away every day.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E acha que dependemos de mais no dia a dia?
lines.en: And do you think we depend on it too much day to day?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Importa-se de repetir a pergunta? Não apanhei a parte do fim.
lines.en: Would you mind repeating the question? I did not catch the last part.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Claro. Acha que dependemos demasiado desse objeto?
lines.en: Of course. Do you think we depend too much on that object?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Acho que sim. Por exemplo, ao jantar em casa ninguém fala, estão todos a olhar para o ecrã.
lines.en: I think so. For example, at dinner at home nobody speaks, everyone is looking at the screen.

days.title: Indicative or subjunctive?
days.objective: Switch correctly between the indicative after verbs of certainty like achar que and saber que, and the present subjunctive after verbs of doubt like duvidar que and não achar que.
days.paretoFocus: This certainty-versus-doubt switch controls the mood of almost every opinion a learner gives in Portuguese, so making it automatic unlocks natural conversation.
drills: Say three things you are sure of, starting each with 'Acho que...' or 'Sei que...' and the indicative.
Say three things you doubt, starting each with 'Duvido que...', flipping the following verb to its subjunctive form.
Take a positive opinion in the indicative and negate it so the verb switches to the subjunctive.

items: Recall two verbs that trigger the indicative and two that trigger the subjunctive.
Explain in your own words why negating 'achar que' changes the mood of the verb that follows.
Translate: 'I doubt that he knows the truth.'

activities.title: Certainty and doubt
activities.intro: In Portuguese, verbs of certainty (achar que, saber que, ter a certeza de que) take the indicative, but verbs of doubt or a negated opinion (duvidar que, não achar que, não acreditar que) switch the next verb into the present subjunctive. If the speaker presents something as fact, use the indicative; if it is uncertain or denied, use the subjunctive.

items.hr: Acho que o Pedro tem razão.
items.en: I think Pedro is right.
items.note: achar que + indicative: presented as fact

items.hr: Sei que a reunião começa às nove.
items.en: I know the meeting starts at nine.
items.note: saber que + indicative

items.hr: Duvido que o Pedro tenha razão desta vez.
items.en: I doubt Pedro is right this time.
items.note: duvidar que + present subjunctive (tenha)

items.hr: Não acho que a reunião comece a tempo.
items.en: I don't think the meeting will start on time.
items.note: não achar que + subjunctive (comece)

items.hr: Não acredito que isso seja verdade.
items.en: I don't believe that's true.
items.note: não acreditar que + subjunctive (seja)

activities.title: Praticar o modo certo
activities.intro: Choose the indicative or the present subjunctive depending on certainty or doubt.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'Acho que ele ___ razão.'
questions.explanation: 'Achar que' expresses certainty and takes the indicative, so 'tem' is correct, not the subjunctive 'tenha'.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'Duvido que ela ___ a verdade.'
questions.explanation: 'Duvidar que' expresses doubt, so the verb switches to the present subjunctive 'saiba', not the indicative 'sabe'.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'chegar': 'Não acho que eles ___ a tempo.'
questions.explanation: 'Não achar que' negates an opinion, triggering the present subjunctive 'cheguem'.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'ser': 'Tenho a certeza de que isto ___ um erro.'
questions.explanation: 'Ter a certeza de que' expresses certainty, so the indicative 'é' is used, not a subjunctive form.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I don't think he is right.'
questions.explanation: 'Não achar que' negates the opinion, so 'ter' appears in the present subjunctive: tenha.

questions.prompt: Listen and complete the sentence: 'Acho que o Pedro tem ___.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Acho que o Pedro tem razão.', which means 'I think Pedro is right.'
questions.audioText: Acho que o Pedro tem razão.

questions.answer: Não acredito que isso seja verdade.
questions.explanation: 'I don't believe that's true.' is 'Não acredito que isso seja verdade.'

activities.title: Do you think he is coming?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend asks about weekend plans; practise choosing indicative for certainty and subjunctive for doubt.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Achas que o Rui vem à festa no sábado?
lines.en: Do you think Rui is coming to the party on Saturday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Acho que sim, ele disse que não tem outros planos.
lines.en: I think so, he said he doesn't have other plans.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Eu duvido que ele venha, ele cancela sempre à última hora.
lines.en: I doubt he'll come, he always cancels at the last minute.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pois é, mas desta vez tenho a certeza de que ele quer vir.
lines.en: That's true, but this time I'm sure he wants to come.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Não acredito que isso mude, ele é sempre igual.
lines.en: I don't believe that will change, he's always the same.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sei que ele gosta muito de ti, por isso talvez venha por essa razão.
lines.en: I know he likes you a lot, so maybe he'll come for that reason.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Não acho que seja só por isso, mas vamos ver.
lines.en: I don't think it's only because of that, but we'll see.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Concordo. De qualquer forma, tenho a certeza de que vai ser uma boa festa.
lines.en: I agree. Either way, I'm sure it'll be a good party.

days.title: Degrees of certainty
days.objective: Place a statement on the certainty scale from com certeza through se calhar to talvez, choosing indicative or present subjunctive accordingly.
days.paretoFocus: Hedging degrees of certainty is essential for natural Portuguese small talk and negotiation, and the mood choice trips up learners at every level.
drills: Make three predictions with 'com certeza' or 'se calhar' and the indicative.
Make three guesses with 'talvez' and the present subjunctive.
Rank the same statement three ways, from most to least certain.

items: Recall which two expressions on the certainty scale take the indicative.
Recall which expression usually takes the present subjunctive when it comes first.
Translate: 'Maybe she already knows the address.'

activities.title: From certain to maybe
activities.intro: Com certeza (definitely) and se calhar (probably/maybe) both take the indicative, since the speaker still commits to a version of events. Talvez (maybe), when placed before the verb, switches it to the present subjunctive, marking a more open guess.

items.hr: Com certeza vou à reunião amanhã.
items.en: I'll definitely go to the meeting tomorrow.
items.note: com certeza = definitely, takes the indicative

items.hr: Se calhar chove esta tarde.
items.en: It'll probably rain this afternoon.
items.note: se calhar = probably, takes the indicative

items.hr: Talvez chova esta tarde.
items.en: Maybe it'll rain this afternoon.
items.note: talvez + present subjunctive (chova) when talvez comes first

items.hr: Se calhar ele já sabe a notícia.
items.en: He probably already knows the news.
items.note: se calhar + indicative (sabe)

items.hr: Talvez ele já saiba a notícia.
items.en: Maybe he already knows the news.
items.note: talvez + subjunctive (saiba), more uncertain than se calhar

activities.title: Practising degrees of certainty
activities.intro: Choose the right mood for com certeza, se calhar and talvez.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'Com certeza ele ___ a verdade.'
questions.explanation: 'Com certeza' expresses strong certainty and takes the indicative 'diz'.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'Talvez ela ___ cedo hoje.'
questions.explanation: 'Talvez' before the verb triggers the present subjunctive 'saia', not the indicative 'sai'.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'poder': 'Se calhar ele ___ vir mais tarde.'
questions.explanation: 'Se calhar' takes the indicative, so 'pode' is correct.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'poder': 'Talvez ele ___ vir mais tarde.'
questions.explanation: 'Talvez' before the verb takes the present subjunctive of 'poder', 'possa'.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'Maybe she already knows the address.'
questions.explanation: 'Talvez' before the verb requires the present subjunctive 'saiba'.

questions.prompt: Listen, then type the missing word: 'Com ___ vou à reunião amanhã.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Com certeza vou à reunião amanhã.', which means 'I'll definitely go to the meeting tomorrow.'
questions.audioText: Com certeza vou à reunião amanhã.

questions.prompt: Write it in Portuguese: 'Maybe he already knows the news.'
questions.answer: Talvez ele já saiba a notícia.
questions.explanation: 'Maybe he already knows the news.' is 'Talvez ele já saiba a notícia.'

activities.title: Vai chover?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends debate the weather and weekend plans, moving up and down the certainty scale.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Achas que vai chover no sábado?
lines.en: Do you think it'll rain on Saturday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Se calhar chove de manhã, mas à tarde deve estar bom.
lines.en: It'll probably rain in the morning, but the afternoon should be fine.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Talvez seja melhor que levemos guarda-chuva, só por precaução.
lines.en: Maybe it's better if we bring an umbrella, just in case.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Com certeza, é sempre melhor prevenir.
lines.en: Definitely, it's always better to be safe.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Se calhar o Miguel também vem, ele adora andar ao ar livre.
lines.en: Miguel will probably come too, he loves being outdoors.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Talvez ele traga a irmã dele também.
lines.en: Maybe he'll bring his sister too.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Com certeza vai ser um dia divertido.
lines.en: It'll definitely be a fun day.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sem dúvida. Vou já avisar os outros.
lines.en: No doubt. I'll let the others know right away.

days.title: Exprimir probabilidade
days.objective: Make guesses about the present using dever + infinitive and the distinctly European é capaz de + infinitive.
days.paretoFocus: Dever and é capaz de are the two most natural ways Portuguese speakers hedge a guess in daily conversation, and é capaz de rarely appears in Brazilian materials, so learners need explicit exposure.
drills: Guess what a friend is doing right now using 'deve estar a...'.
Make three predictions about the weather or traffic using 'é capaz de'.
Explain a likely fact about someone using 'dever' plus infinitive.

items: Recall the two structures used to make a guess about the present.
Explain the word order of 'é capaz de + infinitive'.
Translate: 'She must be at work now.'

activities.title: Making guesses
activities.intro: Dever + infinitive expresses a confident guess (he must be tired). É capaz de + infinitive is the typical European way to say something is likely (it might rain), and never takes a conjugated verb after 'de'.

items.hr: Ele deve estar cansado, trabalhou o dia todo.
items.en: He must be tired, he worked all day.
items.note: dever + infinitive = must be / probably is

items.hr: Deve ser meio-dia, tenho fome.
items.en: It must be noon, I'm hungry.
items.note: dever + ser for guessing the time

items.hr: É capaz de chover à tarde.
items.en: It might rain in the afternoon.
items.note: é capaz de + infinitive = it's likely that

items.hr: Ela é capaz de já ter chegado a casa.
items.en: She's probably already got home.
items.note: é capaz de + ter chegado (compound infinitive)

items.hr: O Rui deve saber a resposta, é muito estudioso.
items.en: Rui probably knows the answer, he's very studious.
items.note: dever + infinitive expressing a likely fact

activities.title: Praticar a probabilidade
activities.intro: Practise dever and é capaz de for guesses about the present.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'Ele ___ estar em casa a esta hora.'
questions.explanation: 'Dever + infinitive' in the present indicative expresses a guess about now.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a frase correta.
options: É capaz de chover à tarde.
É capaz de chove à tarde.
questions.answer: É capaz de chover à tarde.
questions.explanation: 'É capaz de' must be followed by 'de' plus the infinitive, never a conjugated verb.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'ser': 'Deve ___ tarde, o céu já está escuro.'
questions.explanation: 'Dever + infinitive' (ser) is used to guess about a fact, here the time.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'ser': 'Ele ___ capaz de já ter saído.'
questions.explanation: 'É capaz de' is the fixed frame for a likely event; 'capaz' needs 'é' before it.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'She must be at work now.'
questions.explanation: 'Dever + infinitive' (estar) is used to guess about the present.

questions.prompt: Listen and fill in the word you hear: 'Ele deve estar cansado, ___ o dia todo.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Ele deve estar cansado, trabalhou o dia todo.', which means 'He must be tired, he worked all day.'
questions.audioText: Ele deve estar cansado, trabalhou o dia todo.

questions.prompt: Say it in Portuguese, in writing: 'Rui probably knows the answer, he's very studious.'
questions.answer: O Rui deve saber a resposta, é muito estudioso.
questions.explanation: 'Rui probably knows the answer, he's very studious.' is 'O Rui deve saber a resposta, é muito estudioso.'

activities.title: Where is Rui?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend hasn't shown up and you guess where he might be using dever and é capaz de.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Já são oito horas e o Rui ainda não chegou.
lines.en: It's eight o'clock already and Rui still hasn't arrived.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Deve estar preso no trânsito, ele mora longe.
lines.en: He must be stuck in traffic, he lives far away.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ou é capaz de ter-se esquecido, ele é muito distraído.
lines.en: Or he might have forgotten, he's very absent-minded.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pode ser. Vou ligar-lhe para perguntar.
lines.en: Could be. I'll call him to ask.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa ideia. Ele deve ter o telemóvel sempre à mão.
lines.en: Good idea. He probably always has his phone at hand.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não atende. É capaz de estar a conduzir.
lines.en: He's not answering. He might be driving.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Faz sentido. Deve chegar daqui a pouco.
lines.en: Makes sense. He'll probably arrive soon.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vamos esperar mais uns minutos, então.
lines.en: Let's wait a few more minutes, then.

days.title: Politeness in a request
days.objective: Soften requests using the imperfect of politeness (podia, queria, importava-se de) and the será que frame.
days.paretoFocus: Polite request forms are used constantly in shops, offices and with strangers, and the imperfect-for-politeness pattern is distinctly different from English.
drills: Ask for help in a shop three different ways using 'podia' and 'queria'.
Make a request to a stranger using 'importava-se de + infinitive'.
Soften a request even further by adding 'será que' in front of it.

items: Recall which imperfect forms are used to soften requests.
Explain how 'será que' changes the tone of a question.
Translate: 'Would you mind closing the window?'

activities.title: Asking tactfully
activities.intro: In European Portuguese, the imperfect of poder and querer (podia, queria) softens a request into something closer to English 'could/would'. Importar-se de + infinitive means 'to mind doing something', and será que in front of a question makes it even more indirect and polite.

items.hr: Podia ajudar-me com uma coisa, se faz favor?
items.en: Could you help me with something, please?
items.note: podia softens the request instead of 'pode'

items.hr: Queria uma informação sobre os horários dos comboios.
items.en: I'd like some information about the train times.
items.note: queria softens 'quero' into 'I'd like'

items.hr: Importava-se de fechar a janela?
items.en: Would you mind closing the window?
items.note: importar-se de + infinitive = to mind doing something

items.hr: Será que me pode emprestar uma caneta?
items.en: Could you possibly lend me a pen?
items.note: será que softens a question, often paired with poder

items.hr: Não se importava de repetir a pergunta?
items.en: Would you mind repeating the question?
items.note: the negative framing makes the request even more polite

activities.title: Praticar pedidos educados
activities.intro: Choose the politest form for each request.

questions.prompt: Qual é a forma mais educada de pedir ajuda?
questions.explanation: The imperfect 'podia' softens the request; the others are direct commands or blunt statements.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: '___ de fechar a porta?'
questions.explanation: European Portuguese places the clitic after the verb with a hyphen in this frame: importava-se.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma educada de 'querer': '___ um café, se faz favor.'
questions.explanation: The imperfect 'queria' is used instead of 'quero' to soften a request in a café or shop.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma educada de 'poder': '___ dizer-me as horas, por favor?'
questions.explanation: 'Podia' (imperfect) is softer than 'pode' for asking a stranger a favour.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'Could you possibly lend me your phone?'
questions.explanation: 'Será que' plus the polite imperfect 'podia' makes the request extra soft.

questions.prompt: Play the audio and complete: 'Podia ___-me com uma coisa, se faz favor?'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Podia ajudar-me com uma coisa, se faz favor?', which means 'Could you help me with something, please?'
questions.audioText: Podia ajudar-me com uma coisa, se faz favor?

questions.prompt: Put this into Portuguese: 'Would you mind repeating the question?'
questions.answer: Não se importava de repetir a pergunta?
questions.explanation: 'Would you mind repeating the question?' is 'Não se importava de repetir a pergunta?'

activities.title: A request in a shop
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You need help finding something in a shop, so you use several polite request forms.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bom dia, em que posso ajudar?
lines.en: Good morning, how can I help you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bom dia. Queria uma informação sobre este casaco.
lines.en: Good morning. I'd like some information about this coat.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Com certeza. O que gostaria de saber?
lines.en: Of course. What would you like to know?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Será que tem este casaco num tamanho mais pequeno?
lines.en: Could you possibly have this coat in a smaller size?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vou verificar. Importava-se de esperar um momento?
lines.en: I'll check. Would you mind waiting a moment?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, sem problema.
lines.en: Sure, no problem.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Encontrei um tamanho mais pequeno. Podia experimentá-lo ali.
lines.en: I found a smaller size. You could try it on over there.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Obrigado. Podia também mostrar-me umas botas parecidas?
lines.en: Thank you. Could you also show me some similar boots?

days.title: Indefinites: qualquer, ambos, cada um
days.objective: Use B1 indefinites and quantifiers qualquer, ambos, cada um, todo o and tudo o que correctly.
days.paretoFocus: These indefinites appear constantly in instructions, comparisons and generalisations, and each has its own agreement pattern that trips learners up.
drills: List three things 'qualquer pessoa' can do, using qualquer plus a singular noun.
Compare two people or things using ambos/ambas correctly.
Say what 'cada um' of your family members prefers for dinner.

items: Recall how 'ambos' changes for feminine nouns.
Explain why 'cada' never changes form.
Translate: 'She read everything that was on the table.'

activities.title: Any, both, each one
activities.intro: Qualquer precedes a singular noun with no article and means 'any'. Ambos/ambas agrees in gender with a plural noun and means 'both'. Cada is invariable and always precedes a singular noun, while cada um/uma is a pronoun. Tudo o que means 'everything that'.

items.hr: Qualquer pessoa pode aprender uma língua nova.
items.en: Anyone can learn a new language.
items.note: qualquer + singular noun = any

items.hr: Podes escolher qualquer um dos dois.
items.en: You can choose either of the two.
items.note: qualquer um as a pronoun

items.hr: Ambos os irmãos moram em Lisboa.
items.en: Both brothers live in Lisbon.
items.note: ambos + os + noun, agrees in gender: ambas as irmãs

items.hr: Cada um tem a sua opinião sobre o assunto.
items.en: Each one has their own opinion on the matter.
items.note: cada um is invariable in form

items.hr: Ela leu tudo o que encontrou sobre o tema.
items.en: She read everything she found on the topic.
items.note: tudo o que = everything that

activities.title: Practising the indefinites
activities.intro: Practise agreement with qualquer, ambos and cada.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'As duas soluções são boas, podes escolher ___.'
questions.explanation: 'Soluções' is feminine plural, so the pronoun agrees as 'qualquer uma'.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: '___ as equipas jogaram muito bem.'
questions.explanation: 'Equipas' is feminine plural, so 'ambas' agrees, unlike the masculine 'ambos'.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'cada': '___ aluno tem de entregar o trabalho até sexta-feira.'
questions.explanation: 'Cada' is invariable and always precedes a singular noun.

questions.prompt: Completa: 'Ele guardou ___ o que lhe disseram, palavra por palavra.'
questions.explanation: 'Tudo o que' means 'everything that'; 'tudo' is invariable here.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'Any student can ask a question.'
questions.explanation: 'Qualquer' precedes the singular noun directly, with no article.

questions.prompt: Listen closely and fill the gap: 'Qualquer pessoa pode ___ uma língua nova.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Qualquer pessoa pode aprender uma língua nova.', which means 'Anyone can learn a new language.'
questions.audioText: Qualquer pessoa pode aprender uma língua nova.

questions.prompt: Type the Portuguese for: 'She read everything she found on the topic.'
questions.answer: Ela leu tudo o que encontrou sobre o tema.
questions.explanation: 'She read everything she found on the topic.' is 'Ela leu tudo o que encontrou sobre o tema.'

activities.title: Choosing between two
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You and a friend are deciding between two restaurants, using indefinites to talk about options.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Não sei se vamos ao restaurante italiano ou ao japonês. Tu tens preferência?
lines.en: I don't know if we should go to the Italian or the Japanese place. Do you have a preference?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Para mim tanto faz, qualquer um serve.
lines.en: It's all the same to me, either one works.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ambos são bons, mas o italiano fica mais perto.
lines.en: Both are good, but the Italian one is closer.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Então vamos a esse. Cada um pede o que quiser.
lines.en: Let's go to that one then. Everyone can order whatever they want.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa ideia. Eu como quase tudo o que tem massa.
lines.en: Good idea. I eat almost everything that has pasta.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Eu também, qualquer prato de massa me agrada.
lines.en: Me too, any pasta dish pleases me.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então está decidido, vamos ambos ficar contentes.
lines.en: Then it's decided, we'll both be happy.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: De certeza que sim.
lines.en: I'm sure we will.

days.title: Discourse adverbs
days.objective: Steer a conversation with discourse adverbs: afinal for a revised conclusion, aliás for adding a correction or extra point, and entretanto for meanwhile.
days.paretoFocus: These three connectors are everywhere in spoken and written Portuguese to manage the flow of ideas, and mixing them up creates real confusion for the listener.
drills: Tell a short story where the ending surprises you, using 'afinal' for the twist.
Add an extra point to an opinion using 'aliás'.
Describe two things happening at the same time using 'entretanto'.

items: Recall which adverb marks a corrected expectation.
Recall which adverb marks simultaneous actions.
Translate: 'I thought it was closed, but it turns out it was open.'

activities.title: After all, indeed, meanwhile
activities.intro: Afinal marks a correction to a previous belief ('it turns out'). Aliás adds a clarifying or reinforcing point, often a small correction ('actually'). Entretanto marks two things happening at the same time ('meanwhile').

items.hr: Pensava que ele estava zangado, mas afinal estava só cansado.
items.en: I thought he was angry, but it turns out he was just tired.
items.note: afinal = it turns out, marking a correction to a previous belief

items.hr: O restaurante está fechado; afinal, hoje é feriado.
items.en: The restaurant is closed; it turns out today is a holiday.
items.note: afinal introducing the real reason

items.hr: Não gosto muito de peixe, aliás, prefiro nem pensar nisso.
items.en: I don't like fish much, actually, I'd rather not even think about it.
items.note: aliás = actually, reinforcing or correcting a statement

items.hr: Ele fala três línguas, aliás, talvez quatro.
items.en: He speaks three languages, or rather, maybe four.
items.note: aliás adding a precision or correction

items.hr: Vou preparar o jantar; entretanto, podes pôr a mesa.
items.en: I'll get dinner ready; meanwhile, you can set the table.
items.note: entretanto = meanwhile, two things at the same time

activities.title: Practising discourse adverbs
activities.intro: Choose the right discourse adverb for each context.

questions.prompt: Escolhe o advérbio correto: 'Achava que tinha perdido as chaves, mas ___ estavam no bolso.'
questions.explanation: 'Afinal' marks the correction of a mistaken belief, the classic 'it turns out' moment.

questions.prompt: Escolhe o advérbio correto: 'Vou tratar da papelada; ___, podes começar a arrumar a sala.'
questions.explanation: 'Entretanto' introduces a simultaneous action, meanwhile.

questions.prompt: Completa: 'Ele disse que não vinha à festa; ___, apareceu logo à primeira hora.'
questions.explanation: 'Afinal' signals that reality contradicted the earlier expectation.

questions.prompt: Completa: 'Não tenho muito tempo livre; ___, prefiro assim, gosto de estar ocupado.'
questions.explanation: 'Aliás' here adds a clarifying, reinforcing remark to the previous statement.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I'll cook and you can meanwhile set the table.'
questions.explanation: 'Entretanto' (meanwhile) slots naturally after the subject and verb to show simultaneity.

questions.prompt: Type the word you hear: 'Pensava que ele estava ___, mas afinal estava só cansado.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Pensava que ele estava zangado, mas afinal estava só cansado.', which means 'I thought he was angry, but it turns out he was just tired.'
questions.audioText: Pensava que ele estava zangado, mas afinal estava só cansado.

questions.prompt: Write it in Portuguese: 'I'll get dinner ready; meanwhile, you can set the table.'
questions.answer: Vou preparar o jantar; entretanto, podes pôr a mesa.
questions.explanation: 'I'll get dinner ready; meanwhile, you can set the table.' is 'Vou preparar o jantar; entretanto, podes pôr a mesa.'

activities.title: A misunderstanding
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You clear up a misunderstanding with a friend using afinal, aliás and entretanto.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Pensei que tinhas ficado zangado comigo ontem.
lines.en: I thought you'd gotten angry with me yesterday.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não, afinal só estava cansado do trabalho.
lines.en: No, it turns out I was just tired from work.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ainda bem, fiquei preocupada. Aliás, ia perguntar-te uma coisa.
lines.en: Good, I was worried. Actually, I was going to ask you something.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Diz lá, estou a ouvir.
lines.en: Go ahead, I'm listening.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vou tratar de uns papéis no banco esta tarde.
lines.en: I'm going to sort out some papers at the bank this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Entretanto eu posso ir buscar as compras, assim aproveitamos o tempo.
lines.en: Meanwhile I can go get the shopping, that way we make good use of the time.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa ideia. Afinal, hoje até correu tudo bem.
lines.en: Good idea. It turns out today ended up going well after all.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sim, aliás, foi um dia bastante produtivo.
lines.en: Yes, actually, it was quite a productive day.

days.title: Expressing a trend
days.objective: Describe growing and correlated change using cada vez mais/menos and quanto mais... mais.
days.paretoFocus: These progression structures let learners talk about trends and cause-effect relationships, a core B1 speaking and writing skill for opinions and essays.
drills: Give one example of something that's cada vez mais caro (increasingly expensive) and one that's cada vez menos comum (increasingly rare) in your city.
Build three 'quanto mais... mais...' sentences about your own habits.
Say one thing that is getting better and one that is getting worse in your life.

items: Recall the irregular comparative forms used after 'cada vez'.
Explain the word order of 'quanto mais... mais...'.
Translate: 'The more you sleep, the better you feel.'

activities.title: More and more
activities.intro: Cada vez mais/menos plus an adjective describes a trend that keeps growing or shrinking (getting more/less X). Quanto mais... mais/menos... links two proportional changes together (the more..., the more/less...).

items.hr: Os preços estão cada vez mais altos.
items.en: Prices are getting higher and higher.
items.note: cada vez mais + adjective = more and more

items.hr: Ele fala português cada vez melhor.
items.en: He speaks Portuguese better and better.
items.note: cada vez melhor = better and better, irregular comparative

items.hr: As pessoas saem cada vez menos à noite.
items.en: People go out less and less at night.
items.note: cada vez menos = less and less

items.hr: Quanto mais estudo, mais aprendo.
items.en: The more I study, the more I learn.
items.note: quanto mais... mais... = the more... the more...

items.hr: Quanto mais cedo saíres, menos trânsito encontras.
items.en: The earlier you leave, the less traffic you'll find.
items.note: quanto mais... menos... = the more... the less...

activities.title: Practising trends
activities.intro: Practise linking two changing situations together, then try swapping in your own adjectives instead of the example ones given below.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'A cidade está ___ poluída.'
questions.explanation: 'Cada vez mais + adjective' is the fixed structure for a growing trend.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: '___ trabalhas, ___ ganhas.'
questions.explanation: The correlative structure pairs 'quanto mais' in the first clause with 'mais' in the second.

questions.prompt: Completa: 'O trânsito está cada vez ___, saio de casa mais cedo todos os dias.'
questions.explanation: 'Pior' is the irregular comparative of 'mau', used after 'cada vez' for a worsening trend.

questions.prompt: Completa: 'Quanto mais praticas, ___ te sentes.'
questions.explanation: 'Melhor' (better) completes the 'quanto mais... melhor' pattern about improving confidence.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'The more you read, the more you learn.'
questions.explanation: 'Quanto mais... mais...' links two proportional actions, here reading and learning.

questions.prompt: Listen and complete the sentence: 'Os ___ estão cada vez mais altos.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Os preços estão cada vez mais altos.', which means 'Prices are getting higher and higher.'
questions.audioText: Os preços estão cada vez mais altos.

questions.prompt: Say it in Portuguese, in writing: 'The earlier you leave, the less traffic you'll find.'
questions.answer: Quanto mais cedo saíres, menos trânsito encontras.
questions.explanation: 'The earlier you leave, the less traffic you'll find.' is 'Quanto mais cedo saíres, menos trânsito encontras.'

activities.title: Life in the city
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends discuss how the city is changing, using progression structures.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Notas como a cidade está cada vez mais cheia?
lines.en: Have you noticed how the city is getting more and more crowded?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sim, e o custo de vida está cada vez mais alto.
lines.en: Yes, and the cost of living is getting higher and higher.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Quanto mais gente chega, mais caras ficam as rendas.
lines.en: The more people arrive, the more expensive rents get.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É verdade. E os transportes públicos estão cada vez piores.
lines.en: That's true. And public transport is getting worse and worse.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Talvez por isso cada vez mais pessoas andem de bicicleta.
lines.en: Maybe that's why more and more people are cycling.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Faz sentido. Quanto mais caro fica o combustível, menos gente usa carro.
lines.en: That makes sense. The more expensive fuel gets, the fewer people use a car.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Espero que a situação melhore cada vez mais nos próximos anos.
lines.en: I hope the situation keeps improving more and more in the coming years.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Eu também espero isso.
lines.en: I hope so too.

days.title: Verbs of becoming
days.objective: Express becoming and change of state with ficar + adjective, tornar-se + noun/adjective and pôr-se a + infinitive.
days.paretoFocus: Change-of-state verbs are essential for narrating personal growth, reactions and sudden actions, and Portuguese splits this single English idea across three distinct verbs.
drills: Describe a sudden emotional reaction using 'ficar + adjective'.
Describe someone's long-term change using 'tornar-se'.
Describe a sudden action starting using 'pôr-se a + infinitive'.

items: Recall which change verb suits a quick emotional reaction.
Recall which change verb suits a deep, lasting transformation.
Translate: 'He suddenly started running.'

activities.title: Three ways to become
activities.intro: Ficar + adjective describes a temporary or emotional change (to become/get). Tornar-se + noun/adjective describes a deeper, more lasting transformation (to become/turn into). Pôr-se a + infinitive describes the sudden onset of an action (to start doing something).

items.hr: Fiquei muito contente com a notícia.
items.en: I became very happy with the news.
items.note: ficar + adjective = to become, temporary/emotional change

items.hr: Ela ficou nervosa antes do exame.
items.en: She got nervous before the exam.
items.note: ficar + adjective, sudden emotional reaction

items.hr: Ele tornou-se um médico muito respeitado.
items.en: He became a very respected doctor.
items.note: tornar-se + noun/adjective = lasting change

items.hr: A situação tornou-se complicada.
items.en: The situation became complicated.
items.note: tornar-se + adjective, gradual/lasting change

items.hr: De repente, a criança pôs-se a chorar.
items.en: Suddenly, the child started crying.
items.note: pôr-se a + infinitive = to start doing something

activities.title: Practising verbs of becoming
activities.intro: Choose ficar, tornar-se or pôr-se a for each context.

questions.prompt: Escolhe o verbo correto: 'Quando soube a notícia, ___ muito surpreendido.'
questions.explanation: A sudden emotional reaction uses 'ficar', not 'tornar-se' (lasting change) or 'pôr-se a' (which needs an infinitive).

questions.prompt: Escolhe o verbo correto: 'Com os anos, a empresa ___ uma referência no setor.'
questions.explanation: A gradual, lasting transformation into something new uses 'tornar-se', the strongest of the three verbs for deep change.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'pôr-se a': 'De repente, ele ___ falar sem parar.'
questions.explanation: 'Pôr-se a' is used for a sudden onset of action; the clitic 'se' attaches after the verb here since nothing before it triggers proclisis.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'tornar-se': 'Ao longo dos anos, o problema ___ cada vez mais grave.'
questions.explanation: Gradual worsening over time uses 'tornar-se', with the clitic in enclisis since this is a standalone main clause.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'She suddenly started crying.'
questions.explanation: 'Pôr-se a + infinitive' expresses the sudden start of an action; the clitic attaches after the verb in enclisis.

questions.prompt: Listen, then type the missing word: 'Fiquei muito ___ com a notícia.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Fiquei muito contente com a notícia.', which means 'I became very happy with the news.'
questions.audioText: Fiquei muito contente com a notícia.

questions.prompt: Put this into Portuguese: 'Suddenly, the child started crying.'
questions.answer: De repente, a criança pôs-se a chorar.
questions.explanation: 'Suddenly, the child started crying.' is 'De repente, a criança pôs-se a chorar.'

activities.title: Unexpected news
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend tells you surprising news about someone you both know, and you react with change-of-state verbs.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sabes que o Bruno se tornou chefe de equipa?
lines.en: Did you know Bruno became team leader?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A sério? Fiquei mesmo surpreendido, ele é tão novo.
lines.en: Really? I'm really surprised, he's so young.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Pois é, ele tornou-se muito responsável nos últimos anos.
lines.en: That's right, he's become very responsible in recent years.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Isso é ótimo. E como reagiu a equipa?
lines.en: That's great. And how did the team react?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No início ficaram um bocado inseguros, mas agora estão contentes.
lines.en: At first they were a bit unsure, but now they're happy.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Faz sentido. Quando soube, também me pus a pensar na minha carreira.
lines.en: That makes sense. When I found out, I also started thinking about my own career.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa ideia, nunca é tarde para mudar de rumo.
lines.en: Good idea, it's never too late to change direction.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Concordo plenamente.
lines.en: I completely agree.

days.title: Adding emphasis
days.objective: Emphasise the right part of a sentence with cleft constructions like foi ele que and the focus words mesmo and até.
days.paretoFocus: Clefting and focus words let learners stress exactly the point they mean, a skill that separates flat B1 speech from more natural, expressive Portuguese.
drills: Build three cleft sentences ('Foi... que...') about who did something at home.
Emphasise yourself as the doer of an action using 'eu mesmo/mesma'.
Say something surprising using 'até' before the unexpected element.

items: Recall the cleft frame used to emphasise part of a sentence.
Explain how 'mesmo' agrees with its subject.
Translate: 'It was my sister who called.'

activities.title: Putting the emphasis in the right place
activities.intro: 'Foi + element + que' isolates and stresses exactly that element of a sentence, whether a person, a time or a place. Mesmo/mesma right after a subject reinforces it (he himself). Até (even) goes right before the element being emphasised as unexpected.

items.hr: Foi ele que partiu o copo, não fui eu.
items.en: It was him who broke the glass, not me.
items.note: cleft 'foi + subject + que' isolates the person responsible

items.hr: Foi ontem que ela me ligou, não hoje.
items.en: It was yesterday that she called me, not today.
items.note: cleft isolating the time

items.hr: Ele mesmo confirmou a informação.
items.en: He himself confirmed the information.
items.note: mesmo right after the subject reinforces it

items.hr: Eu mesma resolvi o problema sozinha.
items.en: I myself solved the problem alone.
items.note: mesmo/mesma agrees in gender with the subject

items.hr: Até o professor se enganou naquela pergunta.
items.en: Even the teacher got that question wrong.
items.note: até = even, placed right before the emphasised element

activities.title: Practising emphasis
activities.intro: Practise building your own cleft sentences, then add mesmo for emphasis or até for something unexpected.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a frase que enfatiza corretamente quem telefonou: foi a Marta, não o Rui.
questions.explanation: The cleft structure 'foi + subject + que + verb' puts the emphasis squarely on 'a Marta'.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a opção correta: 'Ela ___ escreveu a carta, sem ajuda de ninguém.'
questions.explanation: 'Mesma' agrees in gender and number with the feminine singular subject 'ela'.

questions.prompt: Completa com a palavra de ênfase correta: '___ o diretor ficou surpreendido com a decisão.'
questions.explanation: 'Até' (even) signals that this is the least expected person to react that way.

questions.prompt: Completa a estrutura enfática: '___ no verão passado que nos conhecemos.'
questions.explanation: 'Foi... que' is the cleft frame used to emphasise 'no verão passado' (last summer).

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'It was my brother who fixed the computer.'
questions.explanation: The cleft 'foi + o meu irmão + que' puts emphasis on who fixed the computer.

questions.prompt: Listen and fill in the word you hear: 'Foi ele que ___ o copo, não fui eu.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Foi ele que partiu o copo, não fui eu.', which means 'It was him who broke the glass, not me.'
questions.audioText: Foi ele que partiu o copo, não fui eu.

questions.prompt: Type the Portuguese for: 'Even the teacher got that question wrong.'
questions.answer: Até o professor se enganou naquela pergunta.
questions.explanation: 'Even the teacher got that question wrong.' is 'Até o professor se enganou naquela pergunta.'

activities.title: Who did what
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You clear up who did what after a small kitchen disaster, using clefts and focus words.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Quem deixou a torneira aberta? A cozinha está toda molhada!
lines.en: Who left the tap running? The kitchen is all wet!

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não fui eu. Foi o teu irmão que lavou a loiça por último.
lines.en: It wasn't me. It was your brother who did the dishes last.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: A sério? Até ele costuma ser cuidadoso com isso.
lines.en: Really? Even he is usually careful about that.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pois, mas hoje estava com pressa, foi ele mesmo que admitiu.
lines.en: Well, today he was in a hurry, he himself admitted it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Está bem, eu mesma limpo isto, não é grave.
lines.en: Okay, I'll clean it up myself, it's not serious.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Deixa que eu ajudo, foi um erro de todos, não só dele.
lines.en: Let me help, it was everyone's mistake, not just his.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Obrigada. Até tu és mais paciente do que eu, às vezes.
lines.en: Thanks. Even you are more patient than me, sometimes.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não exageres, também me irrito de vez em quando.
lines.en: Don't exaggerate, I get irritated sometimes too.

days.title: O discurso indireto: perguntas e pedidos
days.objective: Report questions with perguntar se/onde and requests with pedir que plus the present subjunctive, keeping the reporting verb in the present tense throughout.
days.paretoFocus: Reporting what someone asked or requested is a daily narrative skill, and Portuguese requires a mood switch to the subjunctive for reported requests that English does not have.
drills: Report three yes/no questions someone asked you, using 'perguntar se'.
Report a question with a question word, using 'perguntar onde/quando'.
Report a request someone made to you, then double-check the verb after 'pedir que' took the subjunctive ending, not the indicative.

items: Recall when to use 'se' versus a question word in a reported question.
Recall which mood follows 'pedir que'.
Translate: 'He asks us to close the door.'

activities.title: Perguntas e pedidos reportados
activities.intro: To report a yes/no question, use perguntar se (asks if/whether). To report a question with a question word, keep that word (perguntar onde/quando). To report a request, pedir que forces the subjunctive on the verb that follows, for example 'pediu que fechasse a porta' (he asked that I close the door) - note fechasse, not fecho.

items.hr: Ela pergunta se eu vou à festa.
items.en: She asks if I'm going to the party.
items.note: reported yes/no question with se

items.hr: Ele pergunta onde fica a estação.
items.en: He asks where the station is.
items.note: reported question with a question word, no se needed

items.hr: O professor pergunta quando é o exame.
items.en: The teacher asks when the exam is.
items.note: reported question with quando

items.hr: Ela pede-me que feche a janela.
items.en: She asks me to close the window.
