items.note: pedir que + present subjunctive; enclisis: pede-me

items.hr: O chefe pede que a equipa entregue o relatório hoje.
items.en: The boss asks the team to hand in the report today.
items.note: pedir que + subjunctive (entregue), reporting verb stays present

activities.title: Praticar o discurso indireto
activities.intro: Practise reporting questions and requests.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta para reportar 'Vais à reunião?': 'Ele pergunta ___ eu vou à reunião.'
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'se' (if/whether), not 'que'.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'A professora pede que os alunos ___ o telemóvel.'
questions.explanation: 'Pedir que' is followed by the present subjunctive, here 'desliguem'.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'trazer': 'Ela pede-nos que ___ os documentos amanhã.'
questions.explanation: 'Pedir que' triggers the present subjunctive of 'trazer', irregular stem 'tragamos'.

questions.prompt: Completa a pergunta reportada: 'Ele quer saber ___ o museu abre aos domingos.'
questions.explanation: Reporting a yes/no question uses 'se'.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'She asks us to arrive early.'
questions.explanation: 'Pedir que' is followed by the present subjunctive 'cheguemos', and the reporting verb stays in the present.

questions.prompt: Play the audio and complete: 'Ela ___ se eu vou à festa.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Ela pergunta se eu vou à festa.', which means 'She asks if I'm going to the party.'
questions.audioText: Ela pergunta se eu vou à festa.

questions.prompt: Write it in Portuguese: 'She asks me to close the window.'
questions.answer: Ela pede-me que feche a janela.
questions.explanation: 'She asks me to close the window.' is 'Ela pede-me que feche a janela.'

activities.title: Messages to pass on
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A colleague relays several questions and requests from other people in the office.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: O Rui pergunta se vais à reunião das três.
lines.en: Rui is asking if you're going to the three o'clock meeting.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Diz-lhe que sim, vou com certeza.
lines.en: Tell him yes, I'll definitely go.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E a Sofia pergunta onde fica a sala de reuniões nova.
lines.en: And Sofia is asking where the new meeting room is.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Fica no segundo andar, ao lado da cozinha.
lines.en: It's on the second floor, next to the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Certo. O diretor também pede que enviemos o relatório antes das cinco.
lines.en: Right. The director is also asking that we send the report before five.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Está bem, eu trato disso. Ele pergunta mais alguma coisa?
lines.en: Okay, I'll take care of that. Is he asking anything else?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sim, pede-nos que confirmemos a presença de todos até ao meio-dia.
lines.en: Yes, he's asking us to confirm everyone's attendance by noon.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfeito, vou tratar disso já a seguir.
lines.en: Perfect, I'll take care of that right after this.

days.title: Relatives with a preposition
days.objective: Build relative clauses after prepositions using quem, o qual/a qual and em que.
days.paretoFocus: Prepositional relative clauses are unavoidable in more sophisticated speech and writing, and Portuguese has stricter rules than English about dropping the preposition.
drills: Describe a person you did something with, using 'com quem'.
Describe a project or topic using 'em que' or 'no qual'.
Explain a reason using 'pelo qual/pela qual'.

items: Recall which relative pronoun follows a preposition for people.
Recall how 'o qual' agrees in gender and number.
Translate: 'The city where I was born is beautiful.'

activities.title: Preposition plus relative
activities.intro: After a preposition, quem refers to people, while o qual/a qual (agreeing in gender and number) or que refer to things, and are common after longer prepositions. Onde replaces em que for places.

items.hr: A amiga com quem viajei é muito divertida.
items.en: The friend I traveled with is a lot of fun.
items.note: preposition + quem for people

items.hr: O projeto em que estou a trabalhar é muito interessante.
items.en: The project I'm working on is very interesting.
items.note: preposition + que (em que) for things

items.hr: A empresa para a qual trabalho fica no centro da cidade.
items.en: The company I work for is in the city centre.
items.note: o qual/a qual, agrees in gender and number

items.hr: Este é o motivo pelo qual desisti do curso.
items.en: This is the reason why I gave up on the course.
items.note: pelo qual = por + o qual, fixed contraction

items.hr: A cidade onde nasci fica perto do mar.
items.en: The city where I was born is near the sea.
items.note: onde replaces em que for places

activities.title: Practising relatives with a preposition
activities.intro: Practise choosing the right relative pronoun after a preposition.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'O colega ___ falei ontem já respondeu ao email.'
questions.explanation: After a preposition, 'quem' is used for people, and the preposition must stay attached before it.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'A razão ___ qual ele saiu mais cedo é simples.'
questions.explanation: 'Razão' is feminine, so the contraction is 'pela qual' (por + a + qual).

questions.prompt: Completa: 'A casa ___ eu cresci já não existe.' (usa uma palavra para lugares)
questions.explanation: 'Onde' is the natural relative for places, equivalent to 'em que'.

questions.prompt: Completa: 'O curso ___ estou inscrito começa em setembro.'
questions.explanation: 'Em que' links the preposition 'em' to the relative clause about the course.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'The doctor I spoke with is very kind.'
questions.explanation: 'Com quem' keeps the preposition attached before 'quem' when referring to a person.

questions.prompt: Listen closely and fill the gap: 'A amiga com quem viajei é muito ___.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'A amiga com quem viajei é muito divertida.', which means 'The friend I traveled with is a lot of fun.'
questions.audioText: A amiga com quem viajei é muito divertida.

questions.prompt: Say it in Portuguese, in writing: 'The city where I was born is near the sea.'
questions.answer: A cidade onde nasci fica perto do mar.
questions.explanation: 'The city where I was born is near the sea.' is 'A cidade onde nasci fica perto do mar.'

activities.title: Last month's conference
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You tell a friend about people and things from a conference, using prepositional relative clauses.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Como foi a conferência a que foste no mês passado?
lines.en: How was the conference you went to last month?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Foi ótima. Conheci uma investigadora com quem já trabalhei antes.
lines.en: It was great. I met a researcher I'd worked with before.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Que interessante. E de que falaram?
lines.en: How interesting. And what did you talk about?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Falámos do projeto em que estamos ambos envolvidos.
lines.en: We talked about the project we're both involved in.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Já agora, encontraste a empresa para a qual querias mandar o teu currículo?
lines.en: By the way, did you find the company you wanted to send your résumé to?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Encontrei, e até falei com o diretor pelo qual fui recomendado.
lines.en: I did, and I even spoke with the director I was recommended by.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Que sorte! É esse o motivo pelo qual estás tão animado?
lines.en: What luck! Is that the reason you're so excited?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Exatamente, é por isso que estou com tantas esperanças.
lines.en: Exactly, that's why I have such high hopes.

days.title: The impersonal pronoun in practice: se
days.objective: Explain a multi-step process impersonally with primeiro corta-se, depois deixa-se repousar, keeping clear sequencing.
days.paretoFocus: The impersonal se is the standard, natural way Portuguese speakers give instructions and recipes, and sequencing words keep the steps understandable.
drills: Explain a simple recipe step by step using the impersonal se.
Use three sequencing words: primeiro, depois, por fim.
Explain a non-cooking process using the impersonal se.

items: Recall how the impersonal se verb agrees with a plural object.
Recall two sequencing words for organising steps.
Translate: 'First, the onions are chopped.'

activities.title: First you do it like this
activities.intro: The impersonal/passive se is the natural way to give instructions without naming who does the action. When followed by a plural noun, the verb agrees in the plural (cortam-se os legumes); with a singular or no explicit object, it stays singular (lava-se a fruta). Sequencing words like primeiro, depois, de seguida and por fim organise the steps.

items.hr: Primeiro, lava-se a fruta com água fria.
items.en: First, the fruit is washed with cold water.
items.note: impersonal se + verb, singular with a singular object

items.hr: Depois, corta-se em pedaços pequenos.
items.en: Then, it's cut into small pieces.
items.note: sequencing word depois + impersonal se

items.hr: De seguida, mistura-se tudo numa tigela grande.
items.en: Next, everything is mixed in a large bowl.
items.note: de seguida = next, another sequencing connector

items.hr: Deixa-se repousar durante trinta minutos.
items.en: It's left to rest for thirty minutes.
items.note: deixar-se + infinitive, common in recipes and instructions

items.hr: Por fim, serve-se bem fresco.
items.en: Finally, it's served nice and cold.
items.note: por fim = finally, closing the sequence

activities.title: Practising the impersonal: se
activities.intro: Practise the impersonal se and the agreement it needs.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'Primeiro, ___ os legumes em cubos pequenos.'
questions.explanation: With a plural object 'os legumes', the impersonal se verb agrees in the plural, 'cortam-se'.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'Depois, ___ as batatas em azeite bem quente.'
questions.explanation: 'As batatas' is plural, so the impersonal se construction agrees in the plural: 'fritam-se'.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'misturar': 'De seguida, ___ o açúcar com a farinha.'
questions.explanation: 'O açúcar' (singular) takes the singular impersonal se form.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'deixar': 'Por fim, ___ arrefecer antes de servir.'
questions.explanation: 'Deixar-se + infinitive' in the impersonal se form closes the instructions, telling the reader to let it cool.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'First, the vegetables are washed well.'
questions.explanation: 'Os legumes' is plural, so the impersonal se verb 'lavam-se' agrees in the plural.

questions.prompt: Type the word you hear: 'Primeiro, lava-se a ___ com água fria.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Primeiro, lava-se a fruta com água fria.', which means 'First, the fruit is washed with cold water.'
questions.audioText: Primeiro, lava-se a fruta com água fria.

questions.prompt: Put this into Portuguese: 'Finally, it's served nice and cold.'
questions.explanation: 'Finally, it's served nice and cold.' is 'Por fim, serve-se bem fresco.'

activities.title: Grandmother's recipe
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend asks how to make a family soup recipe, and you explain the steps impersonally.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Como se faz aquela sopa deliciosa que fizeste no domingo?
lines.en: How do you make that delicious soup you made on Sunday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É fácil. Primeiro, descascam-se os legumes todos.
lines.en: It's easy. First, all the vegetables are peeled.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E depois, corta-se tudo em pedaços grandes ou pequenos?
lines.en: And then, is everything cut into big or small pieces?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Cortam-se em pedaços médios, para cozinhar mais depressa.
lines.en: They're cut into medium pieces, to cook faster.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Percebi. E o tempero, quando se junta?
lines.en: Got it. And the seasoning, when is it added?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: De seguida, tempera-se com sal, azeite e um pouco de alho.
lines.en: Next, it's seasoned with salt, olive oil and a bit of garlic.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E depois é só deixar cozinhar?
lines.en: And then it's just left to cook?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Exato, deixa-se cozinhar meia hora e, por fim, serve-se bem quente.
lines.en: Exactly, it's left to cook for half an hour and, finally, it's served nice and hot.

days.title: Back then and nowadays
days.objective: Contrast past habits and today's reality using dantes, antigamente, costumava, já não and ainda.
days.paretoFocus: Comparing then and now is a staple of B1 narration and opinion essays, and these markers let learners frame change clearly instead of just listing disconnected facts.
drills: Describe three things that were different 'antigamente'.
Say one habit you no longer have, using 'já não'.
Say one habit you still have, using 'ainda'.

items: Recall the difference between 'já não' and 'ainda'.
Recall how 'costumava' is used to describe a past habit.
Translate: 'Nowadays, I no longer watch as much television.'

activities.title: In the past and today
activities.intro: Antigamente and dantes (in the past, dantes is more informal) set up a contrast with hoje em dia (nowadays). Costumava + infinitive describes a past habit. Já não marks a habit that has stopped, while ainda marks one that continues.

items.hr: Antigamente, as pessoas escreviam cartas em vez de mensagens.
items.en: In the past, people wrote letters instead of messages.
items.note: antigamente = in the past, sets up a contrast

items.hr: Dantes eu costumava andar sempre de autocarro.
items.en: I used to always go by bus.
items.note: dantes = before, informal; costumava + infinitive = used to

items.hr: Hoje em dia, quase toda a gente tem telemóvel.
items.en: Nowadays, almost everyone has a mobile phone.
items.note: hoje em dia = nowadays, contrasts with antigamente/dantes

items.hr: Já não vou tantas vezes ao cinema como antes.
items.en: I no longer go to the cinema as often as before.
items.note: já não = no longer, marks a habit that stopped

items.hr: Ainda hoje visito os meus avós todos os domingos.
items.en: I still visit my grandparents every Sunday today.
items.note: ainda = still, marks a habit that continues

activities.title: Practising then and now
activities.intro: Practise switching between a past-habit marker and a present-continuation marker within the same sentence, then check your verb tense agrees.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: '___, as famílias jantavam todas juntas em casa.'
questions.explanation: 'Antigamente' sets a past-time frame that matches the imperfect 'jantavam'.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'Ele ___ fumar, mas deixou há dois anos.'
questions.explanation: 'Costumava + infinitive' describes a past habit that has since stopped.

questions.prompt: Completa: 'Ela ___ mora na mesma casa onde nasceu, nunca se mudou.'
questions.explanation: 'Ainda' shows the habit or state has continued unbroken since the past.

questions.prompt: Completa: 'Ele ___ trabalha na mesma empresa, mudou de emprego há um ano.'
questions.explanation: 'Já não' marks that a past state has ended.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'Nowadays, people no longer write letters.'
questions.explanation: 'Hoje em dia' frames the present, contrasted with 'já não' marking the discontinued habit of letter-writing.

questions.prompt: Listen and complete the sentence: 'Antigamente, as pessoas ___ cartas em vez de mensagens.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Antigamente, as pessoas escreviam cartas em vez de mensagens.', which means 'In the past, people wrote letters instead of messages.'
questions.audioText: Antigamente, as pessoas escreviam cartas em vez de mensagens.

questions.prompt: Type the Portuguese for: 'I still visit my grandparents every Sunday today.'
questions.answer: Ainda hoje visito os meus avós todos os domingos.
questions.explanation: 'I still visit my grandparents every Sunday today.' is 'Ainda hoje visito os meus avós todos os domingos.'

activities.title: How it used to be
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You talk with an older relative about how daily life has changed over the years.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sabes, antigamente não havia telemóveis nem internet.
lines.en: You know, in the past there were no mobile phones or internet.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A sério? E como é que as pessoas se falavam?
lines.en: Really? And how did people talk to each other?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Dantes escrevíamos cartas ou usávamos o telefone de casa.
lines.en: Back then we wrote letters or used the house phone.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Isso parece tão diferente do que é hoje em dia.
lines.en: That seems so different from how it is nowadays.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Também costumávamos passar mais tempo ao ar livre.
lines.en: We also used to spend more time outdoors.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ainda hoje gosto de passear ao ar livre, mas já não é tão comum.
lines.en: I still enjoy walking outdoors today, but it's no longer as common.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Pois, hoje em dia as pessoas ficam mais tempo em casa, com os ecrãs.
lines.en: Right, nowadays people stay home more, with their screens.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É verdade, mas ainda bem que algumas coisas boas não mudam.
lines.en: That's true, but thankfully some good things don't change.

days.title: Numbers in speech
days.objective: Talk about simple statistics using por cento, a maioria, um terço, metade and quase todos, with correct agreement.
days.paretoFocus: Reporting statistics in plain language is a common B1 reading and speaking task, and the agreement rules for these quantity expressions are easy to get wrong.
drills: Describe a survey result using a percentage and 'por cento'.
Say what 'a maioria' of your friends prefer, with correct singular agreement.
Use 'um terço' in one sentence and 'quase todos' in another, then check whether each takes a singular or plural verb.

items: Recall which quantity expressions take a singular verb.
Recall which quantity expressions take a plural verb.
Translate: 'Almost all the students passed the exam.'

activities.title: Talking about statistics
activities.intro: Por cento and quase todos refer directly to countable people or things and take a plural verb. A maioria and metade are themselves singular nouns, so in careful Portuguese the verb agrees with them in the singular, even though a plural noun follows.

items.hr: Cinquenta por cento dos alunos passaram no exame.
items.en: Fifty percent of the students passed the exam.
items.note: por cento = percent, verb agrees with the plural noun

items.hr: A maioria dos portugueses vive perto do litoral.
items.en: The majority of Portuguese people live near the coast.
items.note: a maioria de + plural noun, usually takes a singular verb

items.hr: Um terço da turma chegou atrasado.
items.en: A third of the class arrived late.
items.note: um terço de = a third of, singular verb agreeing with um terço

items.hr: Metade das pessoas inquiridas prefere trabalhar a partir de casa.
items.en: Half of the people surveyed prefer to work from home.
items.note: metade de + plural noun, verb stays singular

items.hr: Quase todos os participantes concordaram com a proposta.
items.en: Almost all the participants agreed with the proposal.
items.note: quase todos + plural noun + plural verb

activities.title: Practising percentages
activities.intro: Practise agreement with por cento, a maioria, metade and quase todos.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'Trinta por cento dos inquiridos ___ contra a proposta.'
questions.explanation: With 'por cento dos + plural noun', the verb agrees in the plural, 'votaram'.

questions.prompt: Escolhe a forma correta: 'A maioria dos funcionários ___ satisfeita com o novo horário.'
questions.explanation: 'A maioria' is a singular noun, so the verb agrees with it in the singular, 'está', even though 'funcionários' is plural.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'concordar': 'Quase todos os colegas ___ com a nova política.'
questions.explanation: 'Quase todos' is a plural quantifier and takes a plural verb, unlike 'a maioria' or 'metade'.

questions.prompt: Completa com a forma correta de 'preferir': 'Metade dos clientes ___ pagar online.'
questions.explanation: 'Metade' is singular, so the verb stays singular, 'prefere', agreeing with 'metade' rather than with 'clientes'.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'A third of the workers work from home.'
questions.explanation: 'Um terço' is singular, so the verb 'trabalha' agrees with it in the singular, not with the plural 'trabalhadores'.

questions.prompt: Listen, then type the missing word: 'Cinquenta por cento dos alunos ___ no exame.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Cinquenta por cento dos alunos passaram no exame.', which means 'Fifty percent of the students passed the exam.'
questions.audioText: Cinquenta por cento dos alunos passaram no exame.

questions.prompt: Write it in Portuguese: 'Almost all the participants agreed with the proposal.'
questions.answer: Quase todos os participantes concordaram com a proposta.
questions.explanation: 'Almost all the participants agreed with the proposal.' is 'Quase todos os participantes concordaram com a proposta.'

activities.title: The survey results
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You and a colleague go over survey results using percentages and quantity expressions.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Já viste os resultados do inquérito sobre o trabalho remoto?
lines.en: Have you seen the survey results about remote work?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vi. A maioria dos funcionários está satisfeita com o novo sistema.
lines.en: I have. The majority of employees are satisfied with the new system.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E quantos preferem trabalhar sempre a partir de casa?
lines.en: And how many prefer to always work from home?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Cerca de quarenta por cento preferem isso, segundo os dados.
lines.en: About forty percent prefer that, according to the data.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E os outros? Metade quer voltar ao escritório?
lines.en: And the others? Does half want to go back to the office?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Mais ou menos. Um terço prefere um modelo misto.
lines.en: More or less. A third prefers a hybrid model.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Interessante. E quase todos os gestores concordam com essa opção?
lines.en: Interesting. And do almost all the managers agree with that option?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sim, quase todos concordam, o que facilita a decisão final.
lines.en: Yes, almost all agree, which makes the final decision easier.

days.title: Prefixes: des-, re-, in-
days.objective: Recognize and use the prefixes des-, re- and in-/im- to build and decode new Portuguese words from ones already known.
days.paretoFocus: These three prefixes unlock dozens of extra words for free once the base word is known, a major vocabulary multiplier for reading and speaking.
drills: List five verbs you know and add des- or re- to each, checking if the new word makes sense.
Spot the prefix in five words from a recent lesson and guess the meaning before checking.
Say three sentences using desligar, refazer and impossível.

items: Recall: what does des- usually do to a verb's meaning?
Recall: what does re- add to a verb's meaning?
Translate: 'This exercise is impossible to redo.'

activities.title: Des-, re- e in-/im-
activities.intro: Portuguese builds new words constantly by adding prefixes to verbs and adjectives you already know. Des- often reverses an action or state, re- repeats it, and in-/im- negates an adjective.

items.hr: Desliguei o computador antes de sair.
items.en: I switched off the computer before leaving.
items.note: des- + ligar = to disconnect/undo an action

items.hr: Tive de refazer o relatório todo.
items.en: I had to redo the whole report.
items.note: re- + fazer = to do again

items.hr: Isso é impossível de aceitar.
items.en: That's impossible to accept.
items.note: in-/im- + possível; im- before p, b or m

items.hr: O quarto está desarrumado outra vez.
items.en: The room is untidy again.
items.note: des- + arrumado = the opposite, untidy

items.hr: Acho essa decisão completamente injusta.
items.en: I find that decision completely unfair.
items.note: in- + justo = injusta, unfair

activities.title: Prefixes in action
activities.intro: Practise building five new words on the spot by adding a prefix to a base word you already know, then check your guess in a dictionary.

questions.prompt: Which prefix turns 'ligar' (to connect) into its opposite, 'to disconnect'?
questions.explanation: Des- reverses the action or state expressed by the base verb.

questions.prompt: What does 'refazer' mean?
questions.explanation: Re- adds the meaning of repetition to a verb.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'O quarto está tudo ___, precisamos de arrumar.' (the opposite of arrumado)
questions.explanation: Des- + arrumado reverses the state expressed by arrumado, tidy.

questions.prompt: Complete with a single word meaning 'to read again': 'Vou ___ este contrato antes de assinar.'
questions.explanation: Re- + ler = to read again.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I find that decision completely unfair.'
questions.explanation: In- + justo becomes injusta, unfair, agreeing with decisão.

questions.prompt: Listen and fill in the word you hear: 'Desliguei o ___ antes de sair.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Desliguei o computador antes de sair.', which means 'I switched off the computer before leaving.'
questions.audioText: Desliguei o computador antes de sair.

questions.prompt: Say it in Portuguese, in writing: 'I find that decision completely unfair.'
questions.explanation: 'I find that decision completely unfair.' is 'Acho essa decisão completamente injusta.'

activities.title: A day of tidying up
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends tidy up before a trip, working prefixed vocabulary into the conversation naturally.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Porque é que estás a refazer a mala outra vez?
lines.en: Why are you repacking the bag again?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Porque a fiz toda desarrumada e agora está impossível de fechar.
lines.en: Because I packed it all messy and now it's impossible to close.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Deixa-me ajudar. Primeiro vamos desligar a televisão, está a distrair-nos.
lines.en: Let me help. First let's turn off the TV, it's distracting us.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Boa ideia. E depois tenho de reler a lista, para não esquecer nada.
lines.en: Good idea. And then I have to reread the list, so I don't forget anything.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Achas justo levares tanta roupa só para um fim de semana?
lines.en: Do you think it's fair to take so much clothing just for a weekend?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tens razão, isso é um pouco injusto para a mala. Vou tirar metade.
lines.en: You're right, that's a bit unfair to the bag. I'll take out half.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Assim já parece mais organizada.
lines.en: Now it looks more organized.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Obrigado pela ajuda, sozinho ia refazer isto três vezes.
lines.en: Thanks for the help, alone I'd have redone this three times.

days.title: Suffixes: -oso, -ável, -eiro
days.objective: Form and understand adjectives and agent nouns using the suffixes -oso, -ável/-ível and -eiro.
days.paretoFocus: These three suffixes are extremely productive, recognizing them lets a learner guess the meaning of many unfamiliar words while reading or listening.
drills: Turn five nouns you know into -oso adjectives and check if they exist.
Guess the job from five -eiro nouns before checking a dictionary.
Say three sentences using chuvoso, saudável and cozinheiro.

items: Recall: what kind of word does -oso usually create?
Recall: what does -eiro often indicate about a person?
Translate: 'This soup is very tasty and healthy.'

activities.title: He is very careful
activities.intro: Portuguese suffixes turn familiar nouns and verbs into new adjectives and agent nouns. -Oso/-osa means full of a quality, -ável/-ível means capable of being done, and -eiro/-eira names a person's trade or role.

items.hr: Hoje está um dia muito chuvoso.
items.en: Today is a very rainy day.
items.note: chuva (rain) + -oso = rainy, full of rain

items.hr: Este exercício é bastante saudável para as costas.
items.en: This exercise is quite healthy for the back.
items.note: saúde (health) + -ável = saudável, healthy

items.hr: O cozinheiro do restaurante é muito atencioso.
items.en: The restaurant's cook is very attentive.
items.note: cozinha (kitchen) + -eiro = person who works there, cook

items.hr: Ele é uma pessoa muito cuidadosa com o dinheiro.
items.en: He's a very careful person with money.
items.note: cuidado (care) + -osa = careful, full of care

items.hr: Este problema é facilmente resolvível.
items.en: This problem is easily solvable.
items.note: resolver + -ível = resolvível, able to be resolved

activities.title: Suffixes in action
activities.intro: Practise turning five familiar nouns into new adjectives or job names, then guess their meaning before checking a dictionary.

questions.prompt: Which suffix typically means 'full of' or 'having a lot of', as in chuvoso (rainy)?
questions.explanation: -Oso/-osa attaches to a noun to mean 'full of' that quality.

questions.prompt: What does the suffix -eiro usually indicate in words like cozinheiro or padeiro?
questions.explanation: -Eiro/-eira names the person who does or works with the base noun.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Este chá é ótimo para a saúde e muito ___.' (healthy)
questions.explanation: Saúde + -ável = saudável, healthy.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'A pessoa que trabalha na padaria chama-se ___.' (baker)
questions.explanation: -Eiro forms the agent noun for a trade, here from pão/padaria.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'This soup is tasty and healthy.'
questions.explanation: Saboroso from sabor + -oso; saudável from saúde + -ável.

questions.prompt: Play the audio and complete: 'Hoje está um dia muito ___.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Hoje está um dia muito chuvoso.', which means 'Today is a very rainy day.'
questions.audioText: Hoje está um dia muito chuvoso.

questions.prompt: Put this into Portuguese: 'This problem is easily solvable.'
questions.explanation: 'This problem is easily solvable.' is 'Este problema é facilmente resolvível.'

activities.title: At the market
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends chat at a food market, using -oso, -ável and -eiro adjectives and nouns.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Prova esta sopa, é caseira e muito saborosa.
lines.en: Try this soup, it's homemade and very tasty.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Cheira mesmo bem. É saudável, ou tem muita gordura?
lines.en: It smells really good. Is it healthy, or does it have a lot of fat?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: É bastante saudável, o cozinheiro usa pouco óleo.
lines.en: It's quite healthy, the cook uses little oil.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Boa. Hoje está um dia tão chuvoso, apetece uma sopa quente.
lines.en: Good. Today is such a rainy day, a hot soup sounds great.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sim, e o pão também é fresco, o padeiro trouxe-o esta manhã.
lines.en: Yes, and the bread is fresh too, the baker brought it this morning.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Este mercado é muito acolhedor, sempre gostei de vir cá.
lines.en: This market is very welcoming, I've always liked coming here.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: É verdade, e os preços são razoáveis para a qualidade.
lines.en: True, and the prices are reasonable for the quality.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vou levar um bocado desta sopa saborosa para casa.
lines.en: I'm going to take some of this tasty soup home.

days.title: Verbs that do a lot: apanhar, pôr, tirar
days.objective: Use apanhar, pôr and tirar correctly across their many everyday meanings, from catching transport to setting a table to taking a course.
days.paretoFocus: These three verbs appear constantly in daily Portuguese with meanings that don't map onto a single English verb, mastering their range prevents dozens of small errors.
drills: List three things you can apanhar (catch) and say a sentence for each.
Say three things you might pôr (put/set) in a typical morning.
Say three things you can tirar (take/remove) in daily life.

items: Recall: three different meanings of apanhar.
Recall: what does 'pôr a mesa' mean?
Translate: 'I'm going to take a Portuguese course.'

activities.title: Catch, put, take
activities.intro: Apanhar, pôr and tirar are three of the most overused verbs in everyday Portuguese, each covering many English verbs at once. Learn their common fixed combinations rather than translating word for word.

items.hr: Tenho de apanhar o autocarro das oito.
items.en: I have to catch the eight o'clock bus.
items.note: apanhar = to catch, transport

items.hr: Acho que apanhei uma constipação.
items.en: I think I've caught a cold.
items.note: apanhar uma constipação = to catch a cold

items.hr: Podes pôr a mesa para o jantar?
items.en: Can you set the table for dinner?
items.note: pôr a mesa = to set the table

items.hr: Decidi tirar um curso de fotografia.
items.en: I decided to take a photography course.
items.note: tirar um curso = to take/do a course

items.hr: Tirei uma fotografia linda da praia.
items.en: I took a beautiful photo of the beach.
items.note: tirar uma fotografia = to take a photo

activities.title: Which of the three?
activities.intro: Practise the many senses of apanhar, pôr and tirar.

questions.prompt: What does 'apanhar uma constipação' mean?
questions.explanation: Apanhar uma constipação is the fixed way to say 'to catch a cold'.

questions.prompt: Which verb goes with 'a mesa' to mean 'to set the table'?
questions.explanation: Pôr a mesa is the fixed expression for setting the table.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Vou ___ um curso de inglês este ano.' (to take/do a course)
questions.explanation: Tirar um curso means to take or do a course.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Preciso de sair já para conseguir ___ o comboio das nove.' (to catch, transport)
questions.explanation: Apanhar is used for catching transport.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'Can you set the table for dinner?'
questions.explanation: Pôr a mesa is the fixed expression for setting the table.

questions.prompt: Listen closely and fill the gap: 'Tenho de apanhar o ___ das oito.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Tenho de apanhar o autocarro das oito.', which means 'I have to catch the eight o'clock bus.'
questions.audioText: Tenho de apanhar o autocarro das oito.

questions.prompt: Type the Portuguese for: 'I took a beautiful photo of the beach.'
questions.answer: Tirei uma fotografia linda da praia.
questions.explanation: 'I took a beautiful photo of the beach.' is 'Tirei uma fotografia linda da praia.'

activities.title: Before dinner
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two housemates get ready for dinner, using apanhar, pôr and tirar in their different everyday senses.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Já apanhaste o autocarro, ou vens a pé?
lines.en: Did you already catch the bus, or are you walking?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vim a pé, mas acho que apanhei uma leve constipação com este frio.
lines.en: I walked, but I think I caught a mild cold in this weather.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Coitado. Podes pôr a mesa entretanto, os convidados chegam já.
lines.en: Poor you. Can you set the table meanwhile, the guests are arriving soon.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro. E tu, tiraste aquele curso de culinária afinal?
lines.en: Sure. And you, did you end up taking that cooking course?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tirei sim, e hoje vou pôr em prática uma receita nova.
lines.en: I did, and today I'm going to put a new recipe into practice.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ótimo, vou tirar uma fotografia do prato antes do jantar.
lines.en: Great, I'll take a photo of the dish before dinner.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa ideia, mas despacha-te, a mesa ainda está por pôr.
lines.en: Good idea, but hurry up, the table still isn't set.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Já vou, dá-me só dois minutos.
lines.en: Coming, just give me two minutes.

days.title: False friends: constipado, esquisito, puxar
days.objective: Correctly use classic Portuguese-English false friends without importing their English meaning.
days.paretoFocus: These false friends look identical to English words but mean something different, getting them wrong causes instant miscommunication.
drills: Say what 'constipado' really means, out loud, before checking.
Use 'atualmente' and 'pretender' each in one true sentence about yourself.
List the false friends from this lesson and their real Portuguese meaning from memory.

items: Recall: what does 'estar constipado' mean in Portuguese?
Recall: what is the real meaning of 'esquisito'?
Translate: 'Currently I intend to succeed in this project.'

activities.title: Deceptive words
activities.intro: Some Portuguese words look almost identical to English words but mean something completely different. Getting these false friends wrong causes real misunderstandings, so learn their true meaning as a fixed pair with the English lookalike.

items.hr: Estou constipado, tenho o nariz entupido.
items.en: I have a cold, my nose is blocked.
items.note: constipado = has a cold, not constipated

items.hr: Achei esquisito ele não ter respondido.
items.en: I found it strange that he didn't reply.
items.note: esquisito = strange/odd, not exquisite

items.hr: Tens de puxar a porta, não empurrar.
items.en: You have to pull the door, not push.
items.note: puxar = to pull, not to push

items.hr: Atualmente vivo em Lisboa.
items.en: Currently I live in Lisbon.
items.note: atualmente = currently/nowadays, not actually

items.hr: Não pretendo mudar de emprego para já.
items.en: I don't intend to change jobs for now.
items.note: pretender = to intend, not to pretend

days.title: Everyday expressions: dar jeito, deixa lá
days.objective: Use natural colloquial European Portuguese expressions like dar jeito, deixa lá, não faz mal, ter a ver com and desenrascar-se.
days.paretoFocus: These fixed expressions are used constantly by native speakers and have no direct word-for-word English translation, learning them as chunks makes speech sound far more natural.
drills: Use 'dar jeito' about something useful you own.
Say 'deixa lá' and 'não faz mal' in response to two different small problems.
Explain what 'desenrascar-se' means, in your own words, out loud.

items: Recall: what does 'dar jeito' mean?
Recall: what does 'ter a ver com' actually mean, and how is it different from agreeing with someone?
Translate: 'Never mind, we'll manage somehow.'

activities.title: Never mind, it does not matter
activities.intro: European Portuguese relies on a handful of fixed conversational expressions that have no direct English equivalent. Learning them as whole chunks makes everyday speech sound far more natural.

items.hr: Este dinheiro extra vai dar mesmo jeito.

items.hr: Deixa lá, para a próxima corre melhor.
items.en: Never mind, next time it'll go better.
items.note: deixa lá = never mind, let it go

items.hr: Não faz mal, ainda temos tempo.
items.en: It's fine, we still have time.
items.note: não faz mal = it doesn't matter, no harm done

items.hr: Isso não tem nada a ver com o problema.
items.en: That has nothing to do with the problem.
items.note: ter a ver com = to be related to

items.hr: Não tinha ferramentas, mas consegui desenrascar-me.

days.title: Conversation markers: pois, pronto, ora bem
days.objective: Manage real spoken conversation using discourse markers and response fillers like pois, pois é, pronto, ora bem and então.
days.paretoFocus: Native speech is full of these small connective words, using them correctly is what makes spoken Portuguese sound fluent rather than textbook-like.
drills: Listen for 'pronto' and 'pois' the next time you hear Portuguese spoken and note their function.
Practice starting an explanation with 'Ora bem,' out loud.
Use 'então' three times with three different functions: question, conclusion, filler.

items: Recall: what does 'pronto' signal at the start or end of a turn?
Recall: how is 'pois é' used to agree?
Translate: 'Right, so, let's begin.'

activities.title: Right, ok, well then
activities.intro: Spoken Portuguese is full of small connective words that manage turn-taking and reactions rather than adding new information. Pois often reacts to what was just said, pronto can open or close a turn, and ora bem signals you're about to explain something properly.

items.hr: Pois é, tens toda a razão.
items.en: Right, you're totally right.
items.note: pois é = agreement filler, 'that's right'

items.hr: Pronto, vamos começar então.
items.en: Right then, let's get started.
items.note: pronto = ok/right then, marks a transition

items.hr: Ora bem, o primeiro ponto é este.
items.en: Right then, the first point is this.
items.note: ora bem = well then, introduces an explanation

items.hr: Então, o que achaste do filme?
items.en: So, what did you think of the movie?
items.note: então = so, used to open a question or topic

items.hr: Pois, isso complica um pouco as coisas.
items.en: Well, that complicates things a bit.
items.note: pois (alone) = well/indeed, a soft acknowledging filler

days.title: Small talk: striking up a conversation
days.objective: Start, sustain and politely close small talk with a stranger or neighbour using natural openers, follow-up questions and reactions.
days.paretoFocus: Small talk follows its own set formulas, mastering the openers and closers removes the biggest source of awkward silence for intermediate learners.
drills: Say three ways to start small talk with a neighbour about the weather or the building.
Practice one follow-up question that keeps a conversation going after a yes/no answer.
Say two polite ways to end a conversation and leave.

items: Recall: two openers for small talk with someone you barely know.
Recall: one natural way to end small talk politely.
Translate: 'Well, I have to go now, but it was nice talking to you.'

activities.title: Puxar conversa
activities.intro: Chatting with someone you don't know well follows a loose but recognizable pattern: an opener, a follow-up question, a reaction, and a polite closer. These lines are just as important to learn as grammar.

items.hr: Então, como é que tem corrido tudo por aí?
items.en: So, how has everything been going?
items.note: a common vague opener to start small talk

items.hr: Este tempo não larga, não é verdade?
items.en: This weather just won't let up, right?
items.note: commenting on the weather is a classic icebreaker

items.hr: E os seus, estão todos bem?
items.en: And your family, are they all well?
items.note: asking after family shows interest and keeps talk going

items.hr: Ah, isso é interessante, conte-me mais.
items.en: Ah, that's interesting, tell me more.
items.note: a follow-up reaction that invites more detail

items.hr: Bem, tenho de ir andando, mas foi um gosto falar consigo.
items.en: Well, I have to get going, but it was a pleasure talking to you.
items.note: a polite closer for small talk in the formal register

days.title: Concordar e discordar: participar num debate
days.objective: Take a position in a discussion: fully agree, partially concede, or politely disagree.
days.paretoFocus: Debate language lets a learner participate in real opinion exchanges rather than only stating facts, a core intermediate speaking skill.
drills: State an opinion, then agree with it using 'tem razão' and disagree using 'discordo'.
Practice a partial concession: 'Lá isso é verdade, mas...' followed by a counterpoint.
Give one polite way to disagree without sounding rude.

items: Recall: a phrase for fully agreeing with someone.
Recall: a phrase for partially conceding a point before disagreeing.
Translate: 'I understand your point, but I don't fully agree.'

activities.title: You are right, but...
activities.intro: Taking part in a discussion means being able to fully agree, partly concede, or politely disagree, each with its own set phrase. Using these formulas keeps a disagreement civil.

items.hr: Tem toda a razão, concordo consigo.
items.en: You're completely right, I agree with you.
items.note: tem razão = you're right, a strong agreement formula

items.hr: Lá isso é verdade, mas há outros fatores a considerar.
items.en: That much is true, but there are other factors to consider.
items.note: a partial concession before disagreeing

items.hr: Discordo, acho que a situação é mais complicada.
items.en: I disagree, I think the situation is more complicated.
items.note: discordo = I disagree, direct but polite

items.hr: Compreendo o seu ponto de vista, mas não concordo totalmente.
items.en: I understand your point of view, but I don't fully agree.
items.note: acknowledging before disagreeing softens the tone

items.hr: Na minha opinião, a proposta devia ser revista.
items.en: In my opinion, the proposal should be revised.
items.note: devia + infinitive for a soft recommendation

days.title: Desmarcar e remarcar: justificar-se com educação
days.objective: Cancel or reschedule an appointment politely, apologise and give a credible justification using lamento que with the present subjunctive.
days.paretoFocus: Rescheduling politely and justifying oneself is a common real-life speaking task, and it recycles the present subjunctive in a very natural context.
drills: Practice cancelling an appointment politely with 'lamento, mas surgiu um imprevisto'.

items: Recall: a polite formula to cancel an appointment.

activities.title: I am sorry, something came up
activities.intro: Cancelling or rescheduling an appointment politely follows a set pattern: apologise, give a reason, and propose an alternative. Lamentar que triggers the present subjunctive in the reason that follows.

items.hr: Lamento, mas surgiu um imprevisto e não posso ir à consulta.

items.hr: Seria possível remarcar para a próxima semana?

items.note: seria possível = conditional for a very polite request

items.hr: Lamento que não possa vir à reunião hoje.
items.en: I'm sorry that you can't come to the meeting today.
items.note: lamento que + present subjunctive (possa, from poder)

items.hr: Peço desculpa pelo aviso em cima da hora.
items.en: I apologize for the last-minute notice.
items.note: peço desculpa = I apologize, formal

items.hr: Fico à espera de uma nova data que lhe seja conveniente.

days.title: Neighbours and the residents' committee: resolving conflicts
days.objective: Raise a problem with a neighbour or at a building meeting firmly but politely, and propose a fair solution.
days.paretoFocus: Living close to neighbours makes conflict inevitable, having ready-made firm-but-polite formulas prevents small issues turning into lasting disputes.
drills: Practice raising a noise complaint firmly but politely, in one sentence.

items: Recall: a firm but polite way to raise a noise complaint.

activities.title: Desculpe incomodar, mas...
activities.intro: Living close to neighbours means conflicts over noise, works or shared costs are inevitable. A firm but polite formula, acknowledging the other side before insisting, keeps the relationship intact.

items.hr: Desculpe incomodar, mas o barulho tem sido constante à noite.
items.en: Sorry to bother you, but the noise has been constant at night.

items.hr: Percebo a situação, mas isto já se arrasta há semanas.

items.hr: Proponho que as obras fiquem pelo condomínio a dividir em partes iguais.
items.en: I propose that the repair costs be split equally among the building.

items.hr: Convém marcar uma reunião de condomínio para resolver isto.
items.en: It's a good idea to schedule a building meeting to sort this out.
items.note: convém + infinitive, an impersonal recommendation

activities.title: I hope everyone comes
activities.intro: Organising an event combines inviting people, coordinating logistics and following up politely on replies. items.hr: Vem ao meu jantar de despedida, no sábado à noite.

days.title: Mensagens informais e escrita cuidada: os registos
days.objective: Move between informal messaging style and careful written Portuguese, choosing greetings, forms of address and closings that fit the reader.
days.paretoFocus: Choosing the wrong register in writing is a common and noticeable learner error, this lesson makes the choice explicit.
drills: Write the same short message twice, once informal to a friend and once formal to an institution.

items: Recall: a formal written greeting versus an informal one.

activities.title: Writing for your reader
activities.intro: Portuguese writing shifts dramatically between an informal text to a friend and a careful formal letter or email. Choosing the wrong register, texting a boss like a friend or emailing a friend like an institution, is a common and noticeable mistake.

items.hr: Olá! Tudo bem? Vemo-nos logo, bjs.
items.en: Hey! How's it going? See you later, kisses.
items.note: bjs = beijos, a very informal texting sign-off between friends

items.hr: Exmo. Sr., venho por este meio solicitar informações.
items.en: Dear Sir, I am writing to request information.
items.note: Exmo. Sr. = a formal written opener; solicitar is more formal than pedir

items.hr: Fico a aguardar a vossa resposta com a maior brevidade possível.
items.en: I look forward to your reply as soon as possible.
items.note: a careful formal closing line for written requests

items.hr: Ent tipo, vais ou não vais? Diz lá.
items.en: So like, are you going or not? Just tell me.
items.note: ent = então and tipo = 'like', very informal texting style

items.hr: Os melhores cumprimentos,
items.en: Best regards,
items.note: a shorter formal written closing before the signature

days.title: The CV: telling your career story
days.objective: Narrate a professional career path for a CV or interview: education, work experience, skills and any gaps, in a clear chronological order.
days.paretoFocus: A handful of career-narrative connectors (formei-me em, trabalhei como, de X a Y, atualmente) let you tell your whole work history in one coherent paragraph, the single most common B1 interview task.
drills: Write four sentences narrating your own education and work history in order.
Say out loud one sentence that explains a gap in your career path.

items: Recall two verbs for finishing a course or degree.

Recall a phrase for explaining an unemployment gap without going into personal detail.

activities.title: O percurso profissional
activities.intro: Portuguese career narration follows a clear order: education, experience, current role and skills, with gaps explained briefly and without excessive detail. Verbs like formar-se, trabalhar como and estar sem emprego cover almost every stage of a work history.

items.hr: Formei-me em Gestão em 2016 e comecei logo a trabalhar num banco.
items.en: I graduated in Management in 2016 and started working at a bank right away.
items.note: formar-se em = to graduate in

items.hr: Trabalhei como assistente administrativa durante quatro anos.
items.en: I worked as an administrative assistant for four years.
items.note: trabalhar como + profession, no article

items.hr: Estive dois anos sem emprego enquanto cuidava da minha mãe.
items.en: I was out of work for two years while I looked after my mother.
items.note: estar sem emprego = to be out of work

items.hr: Atualmente trabalho como coordenador de projetos numa pequena empresa.
items.en: I currently work as a project coordinator at a small company.
items.note: atualmente = currently

items.hr: Tenho experiência em atendimento ao público e sei falar três línguas.
items.en: I have experience in customer service and I can speak three languages.

days.title: Work meetings: suggesting and agreeing
days.objective: Contribute actively in a work meeting in Portuguese: propose an idea with the subjunctive, support or object to a colleague's suggestion, and summarise what was agreed.
days.paretoFocus: Sugiro que + present subjunctive is the single structure that turns a flat statement into a real proposal, and combined with three or four meeting phrases it covers almost everything you need to speak up in a meeting.
drills: Make three suggestions in a meeting using 'Sugiro que...' with different verbs.

activities.title: Making a suggestion in a meeting
activities.intro: Sugiro que and proponho que are followed by the present subjunctive, not the indicative, because they express a wish rather than a fact. This lesson also covers phrases for supporting an idea, objecting politely, and summarising a decision once the meeting ends.

items.hr: Sugiro que comecemos a reunião pelo ponto mais urgente.
items.en: I suggest we start the meeting with the most urgent item.
items.note: sugiro que + presente do conjuntivo (comecemos)

items.hr: Proponho que adiemos essa decisão para a próxima semana.
items.en: I propose we postpone that decision until next week.
items.note: proponho que + presente do conjuntivo

items.hr: Concordo consigo, mas acho que devíamos ouvir mais opiniões.
items.en: I agree with you, but I think we should hear more opinions.
items.note: support followed by a soft objection

items.hr: Discordo um pouco; talvez seja melhor esperar mais dados.
items.en: I disagree a little; it might be better to wait for more data.
items.note: talvez + presente do conjuntivo (seja)

items.hr: Ficou combinado que enviamos a proposta até sexta-feira.

days.title: O teletrabalho: vantagens e desvantagens
days.objective: Argue for and against remote work and describe your ideal working arrangement using por um lado... por outro lado to balance two sides of an argument.
days.paretoFocus: This is the one connector most B1 learners lean on for structuring any two-sided argument, so mastering it here pays off far beyond the topic of remote work.
drills: Write two sentences weighing the pros and cons of teleworking, opening the second with 'por outro lado'.

items: Recall the connector you'd use to introduce the counterpoint after stating your first point.

activities.title: Vantagens e desvantagens
activities.intro: Use 'por um lado' to introduce your first point and 'por outro lado' to pivot to the counterpoint, the standard frame for any Portuguese opinion piece, not just remote work. This lesson also reviews comparatives and superlatives for describing advantages and disadvantages.

items.hr: Por um lado, o teletrabalho poupa tempo de deslocação; por outro lado, isola um pouco.
items.en: On one hand, remote work saves commuting time; on the other hand, it isolates you a little.
items.note: por um lado... por outro lado

items.hr: Trabalhar em casa exige mais disciplina do que trabalhar num escritório.
items.en: Working from home requires more discipline than working in an office.
items.note: comparative: mais... do que

items.hr: Prefiro um modelo híbrido, com dois dias em casa e três no escritório.
items.en: I prefer a hybrid model, with two days at home and three in the office.
items.note: modelo híbrido = hybrid model

items.hr: A maior vantagem é a flexibilidade de horário; a maior desvantagem é a falta de contacto com a equipa.
items.en: The biggest advantage is schedule flexibility; the biggest disadvantage is the lack of contact with the team.
items.note: superlative: a maior vantagem / desvantagem

items.hr: No fundo, depende muito da personalidade de cada pessoa.
items.en: Deep down, it depends a lot on each person's personality.
items.note: no fundo = deep down

items.hr: Poupo uma hora de deslocação por dia.
items.en: I save an hour of commuting a day.

items.hr: Sinto falta do contacto com a equipa.
items.en: I miss the contact with the team.
items.note: sentir falta de is to miss something.

activities.title: The terms of the contract

items.hr: A mochila era preta, com um bolso vermelho à frente.

items.hr: Pode dizer-me exatamente a que horas isso aconteceu?

activities.title: Filing a report
