days.title: Online scams: spotting and warning
days.objective: Recognise a common online scam message, warn someone about it using the imperative, and describe in general terms how the scheme works.
days.paretoFocus: A short set of warning phrases in the imperative (desconfia, não abras, não clica) plus scam-description vocabulary lets you protect yourself and warn others in exactly the moment it matters.
drills: Practise warning a friend about a suspicious message using the imperative.
Describe in two sentences how a fictional scam message tries to trick people.
List two signs that a message might be a scam.

items: Recall an imperative phrase for warning someone not to click a link.
Recall the word for a suspicious or fake message.
Recall one common sign of an online scam.

activities.title: Spotting a scam
activities.intro: Recognising an online scam and warning someone about it both rely on the imperative mood, desconfia, não abras, plus vocabulary for describing how a scheme tries to trick people. This lesson practises both recognising and warning in natural spoken Portuguese.

items.hr: Desconfia sempre de mensagens que pedem dados bancários com urgência.
items.en: Always be suspicious of messages that ask for bank details urgently.
items.note: imperative desconfia, tu form

items.hr: Não abras esse link, parece uma mensagem falsa.
items.en: Don't open that link, it looks like a fake message.
items.note: negative imperative

items.hr: A mensagem finge ser de uma empresa a pedir para confirmar uma entrega.
items.en: The message pretends to be from a company asking to confirm a delivery.
items.note: a generic scam scenario, no real company named

items.hr: Um sinal de burla é o remetente insistir que precisas de decidir já.
items.en: One sign of a scam is the sender insisting that you need to decide right away.
items.note: describing a red flag

items.hr: Se recebes uma mensagem assim, avisa logo um familiar.
items.en: If you receive a message like that, warn a family member right away.
items.note: se + presente do indicativo + imperativo

activities.title: Warning about scams
activities.intro: Practise recognising and warning about online scams.

questions.prompt: Qual é um sinal comum de uma mensagem de burla?
questions.explanation: Urgent requests for bank details are a classic scam warning sign.

questions.prompt: Qual frase avisa alguém para não abrir um link suspeito?
questions.explanation: Não abras is the negative tu imperative, used here to warn someone.

questions.prompt: Complete: '___ sempre de mensagens que pedem dados bancários com urgência.' (be suspicious, tu imperative)
questions.explanation: Desconfia is the tu imperative of desconfiar, to be suspicious.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Se ___ uma mensagem assim, avisa logo um familiar.' (you receive)
questions.explanation: Se + presente do indicativo states a real, possible condition: se recebes.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'The message pretends to be from a company asking to confirm a delivery.'
questions.explanation: Fingir ser de + noun describes a message pretending to come from somewhere.

questions.prompt: Listen closely and fill the gap: 'Desconfia sempre de ___ que pedem dados bancários com urgência.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Desconfia sempre de mensagens que pedem dados bancários com urgência.', which means 'Always be suspicious of messages that ask for bank details urgently.'
questions.audioText: Desconfia sempre de mensagens que pedem dados bancários com urgência.

questions.prompt: Type the Portuguese for: 'If you receive a message like that, warn a family member right away.'
questions.answer: Se recebes uma mensagem assim, avisa logo um familiar.
questions.explanation: 'If you receive a message like that, warn a family member right away.' is 'Se recebes uma mensagem assim, avisa logo um familiar.'

activities.title: A suspicious message
activities.intro: Play 'Me' warning a friend about a scam message they received.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Recebi uma mensagem estranha, dizem que preciso de confirmar uma entrega e pedem os dados do cartão.
lines.en: I got a strange message, they say I need to confirm a delivery and they're asking for my card details.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não confies nisso, parece claramente uma burla.
lines.en: Don't trust that, it clearly looks like a scam.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Mas o remetente insiste que é urgente.
lines.en: But the sender insists it's urgent.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É exatamente por isso que devias desconfiar; as burlas criam sempre urgência.
lines.en: That's exactly why you should be suspicious; scams always create urgency.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Achas que não devo clicar no link, então?
lines.en: So you think I shouldn't click the link?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não abras esse link de forma nenhuma, e não dês nenhum dado bancário.
lines.en: Don't open that link at all, and don't give any bank details.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ok, vou apagar a mensagem.
lines.en: Okay, I'll delete the message.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Boa ideia. Se recebes outra mensagem assim, avisa-me logo.
lines.en: Good idea. If you get another message like that, let me know right away.

days.title: Civic life: elections and taking part
days.objective: Talk about civic life in general terms: elections, voting and local participation, and give a personal opinion on why civic participation matters.
days.paretoFocus: A small set of civic nouns and opinion connectors (votar, participação cívica, na minha opinião) lets you hold a full everyday conversation about civic life without ever needing exam-level detail.
drills: Say one sentence about whether you usually vote in elections.
Give your opinion on why local participation matters, using 'na minha opinião'.
Describe one way someone can participate in their community besides voting.

items: Recall the verb for casting a vote.
Recall a phrase for introducing a personal opinion.
Recall one form of civic participation besides voting.

activities.title: Talking about civic life
activities.intro: Talking about civic life at B1 level is mostly opinion vocabulary: votar, participação cívica, and connectors like na minha opinião. This lesson treats elections and local participation purely as an everyday conversation topic, not as exam content.

items.hr: Costumo votar sempre que há eleições.
items.en: I always tend to vote whenever there are elections.
items.note: votar = to vote

items.hr: Na minha opinião, participar na vida da comunidade é tão importante como votar.
items.en: In my opinion, participating in community life is as important as voting.
items.note: na minha opinião = in my opinion

items.hr: Há pessoas que participam em reuniões locais para discutir problemas do bairro.
items.en: Some people take part in local meetings to discuss neighbourhood issues.
items.note: a generic form of civic participation

items.hr: Acho que muita gente da minha idade vota pouco.
items.en: I think a lot of people my age vote very little.
items.note: opinion plus a generalisation

items.hr: Acredito que cada voto conta, por isso não vale a pena ficar em casa.
items.en: I believe every vote counts, so it's not worth staying at home.
items.note: acredito que = I believe that

activities.title: Talking about elections
activities.intro: Practise talking about civic life and elections, and giving your opinion.

questions.prompt: Qual verbo se usa para descrever o ato de escolher um candidato numa eleição?
questions.explanation: Votar is the verb for casting a vote in an election.

questions.prompt: Qual frase serve para introduzir uma opinião pessoal?
questions.explanation: Na minha opinião is the standard opener for a personal opinion.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Há pessoas que participam em reuniões para discutir problemas ___.' (local, adjective)
questions.explanation: Locais here is the plural adjective agreeing with problemas.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Acredito que cada voto ___, por isso não vale a pena ficar em casa.' (counts)
questions.explanation: Conta is the third person singular present of contar, here meaning to count/matter.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'In my opinion, participating in community life is as important as voting.'
questions.explanation: Tão importante como is the comparative structure for as important as.

questions.prompt: Type the word you hear: 'Costumo votar sempre que há ___.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Costumo votar sempre que há eleições.', which means 'I always tend to vote whenever there are elections.'
questions.audioText: Costumo votar sempre que há eleições.

questions.prompt: Write it in Portuguese: 'I think a lot of people my age vote very little.'
questions.answer: Acho que muita gente da minha idade vota pouco.
questions.explanation: 'I think a lot of people my age vote very little.' is 'Acho que muita gente da minha idade vota pouco.'

activities.title: A conversation about taking part
activities.intro: Play 'Me' discussing elections and civic participation, giving your opinion.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vais votar nas próximas eleições?
lines.en: Are you going to vote in the next elections?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vou, sim, costumo votar sempre.
lines.en: Yes, I am, I always tend to vote.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Achas que vale mesmo a pena votar?
lines.en: Do you think it's really worth voting?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Acredito que sim, acho que cada voto conta.
lines.en: I believe so, I think every vote counts.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E participas de outra forma na vida da comunidade?
lines.en: And do you participate in community life in any other way?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Às vezes vou a reuniões locais para discutir problemas do bairro.
lines.en: Sometimes I go to local meetings to discuss neighbourhood issues.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Interessante. Achas que os jovens participam pouco?
lines.en: Interesting. Do you think young people participate little?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Na minha opinião, sim, muita gente da minha idade vota pouco.
lines.en: In my opinion, yes, a lot of people my age vote very little.

days.title: Social problems: describing them and proposing solutions
days.objective: Describe a social problem and propose solutions using é preciso que and para que with the present subjunctive.
days.paretoFocus: These two triggers cover most everyday arguments for change, from housing policy to a noisy neighbour, so they generalize far beyond this lesson's topic.
drills: Describe one social problem you notice in your city in two sentences.
Propose a solution starting with 'É preciso que...'
Explain the purpose of your solution starting with 'para que...'

items: Recall two verbs in the present subjunctive: construir, ajudar.
Say a sentence with 'é preciso que' about housing.
Say a sentence with 'para que' about loneliness.

activities.title: Proposing solutions
activities.intro: Both é preciso que (it's necessary that) and para que (so that) force the verb that follows into the subjunctive, for example 'é preciso que haja mais transportes públicos', not 'há'. This lesson also covers everyday vocabulary for social problems like housing, loneliness and inequality.

items.hr: O preço das casas subiu tanto que os jovens já não conseguem sair de casa dos pais.
items.en: House prices have risen so much that young people can no longer move out of their parents' house.
items.note: sets up the problem before proposing a solution

items.hr: É preciso que o governo construa mais casas a preços acessíveis.
items.en: It is necessary that the government build more affordable housing.
items.note: é preciso que + present subjunctive (construa)

items.hr: Muitos idosos vivem sozinhos; é importante que os vizinhos os visitem, para que não se sintam isolados.
items.en: Many elderly people live alone; it's important that neighbours visit them, so that they don't feel isolated.
items.note: para que + present subjunctive (sintam) expresses purpose

items.hr: A desigualdade aumenta quando os salários não acompanham os preços.
items.en: Inequality increases when wages don't keep up with prices.
items.note: quando + indicative for general facts, no subjunctive here

items.hr: Proponho que se criem mais espaços comunitários, para que os vizinhos se conheçam melhor.
items.en: I propose that more communal spaces be created, so that neighbours get to know each other better.
items.note: propor que also triggers the subjunctive (criem, conheçam)

items.hr: As rendas subiram demasiado.
items.en: Rents have gone up too much.

items.hr: É preciso agir depressa.
items.en: We need to act quickly.
items.note: É preciso plus an infinitive when there is no particular subject.

activities.title: It is necessary that...
activities.intro: Practise choosing and forming the present subjunctive after each of these two phrases: é preciso que, then para que, saying your sentence out loud before checking it.

questions.prompt: Which expression always introduces a purpose clause with the subjunctive?
questions.explanation: 'Para que' introduces a purpose clause and requires the subjunctive; 'porque', 'quando' and 'mas' take the indicative here.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: 'É preciso que os vizinhos ___ uns aos outros.'
questions.explanation: After é preciso que the verb goes into the present subjunctive: ajudem.

questions.prompt: É preciso que se ___ mais casas a preços acessíveis. (be built)
questions.explanation: Present subjunctive of construir, agreeing with 'casas': construam.

questions.prompt: Para que os idosos não se sintam sós, é preciso que a comunidade os ___ com frequência. (visit)
questions.explanation: Present subjunctive of visitar (a comunidade = singular subject): visite.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'It is necessary that the government invest more in housing.'
questions.explanation: 'É preciso que' + present subjunctive (invista) to say what needs to happen.

questions.prompt: Listen and complete the sentence: 'É preciso que o governo construa mais casas a preços ___.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'É preciso que o governo construa mais casas a preços acessíveis.', which means 'It is necessary that the government build more affordable housing.'
questions.audioText: É preciso que o governo construa mais casas a preços acessíveis.

activities.title: An idea for the neighbourhood
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A neighbour vents about a problem in the building; respond with a solution of your own, using this lesson's two subjunctive triggers naturally.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Já reparaste que há cada vez mais pessoas sem casa aqui perto?
lines.en: Have you noticed there are more and more homeless people around here?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sim, é preciso que a câmara faça algo, os preços das rendas estão impossíveis.
lines.en: Yes, it's necessary that the council do something, rents are impossible.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Concordo. Também acho que os idosos do prédio ao lado vivem muito sozinhos.
lines.en: I agree. I also think the elderly people in the building next door live very lonely lives.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Podíamos organizar um almoço mensal, para que todos se conheçam melhor.
lines.en: We could organise a monthly lunch, so that everyone gets to know each other better.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa ideia! E para que os jovens participem, podíamos publicar um cartaz no prédio.
lines.en: Great idea! And so that young people take part, we could put up a poster in the building.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É preciso que alguém trate da comida, eu posso tratar disso.
lines.en: Someone needs to handle the food, I can take care of that.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Eu falo com a vizinha do terceiro andar, ela conhece toda a gente.
lines.en: I'll talk to the neighbour on the third floor, she knows everyone.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ótimo. Assim, para que ninguém se sinta sozinho, começamos já este mês.
lines.en: Great. That way, so that no one feels alone, we'll start this very month.

days.title: Science in the news: understanding a discovery
days.objective: Understand and retell a short popular-science news item about a study, its discovery, cause and the caution scientists give about conclusions.
days.paretoFocus: News about science follows a fixed pattern (study, finding, possible cause, caution) that, once recognised, makes any science article easier to follow.
drills: Read a short fictional science headline aloud and identify the main discovery.
Retell the finding in your own words in one sentence.
Say one sentence of caution about the conclusion, starting with 'Isto não significa que...'

items: Recall the pt-PT word for 'a study' and 'researchers'.
Say a sentence reporting what a study revealed.
Say a sentence of caution about a scientific conclusion.

activities.title: How a discovery gets reported
activities.intro: Popular-science news follows a pattern: what the study found, a possible cause, and a caution that correlation isn't the same as certainty.

items.hr: Um novo estudo revelou que as pessoas que caminham todos os dias dormem melhor.
items.en: A new study revealed that people who walk every day sleep better.
items.note: revelar = to reveal, common verb for reporting findings

items.hr: Os investigadores analisaram os hábitos de várias pessoas durante seis meses.
items.en: The researchers analysed several people's habits over six months.
items.note: o investigador = researcher

items.hr: Segundo os autores, a causa pode estar ligada à exposição à luz natural.
items.en: According to the authors, the cause may be linked to exposure to natural light.
items.note: segundo + noun = according to

items.hr: No entanto, os cientistas alertam que é preciso confirmar estes resultados com mais estudos.
items.en: However, the scientists warn that these results need to be confirmed with more studies.
items.note: alertar que = to warn that; introduces the caution

items.hr: Isto não significa que caminhar resolva todos os problemas de sono, mas ajuda.
items.en: This doesn't mean that walking solves all sleep problems, but it helps.
items.note: não significa que + subjunctive (resolva) to soften a conclusion

activities.title: Reading a science story
activities.intro: Practise the vocabulary and structures used to report a scientific discovery and its limits.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'researchers' in Portuguese?
questions.explanation: 'Os investigadores' means researchers; 'inventores' means inventors, a different word.

questions.prompt: Which phrase introduces a scientific finding, similar to 'a study revealed that'?
questions.explanation: 'Revelar que' + indicative reports a finding as fact.

questions.prompt: Segundo os autores, a causa pode estar ___ à exposição à luz natural. (linked)
questions.explanation: Past participle used as an adjective agreeing with 'a causa' (feminine): ligada.

questions.prompt: Os cientistas ___ que é preciso confirmar os resultados. (warn)
questions.explanation: Present tense of alertar, agreeing with 'os cientistas' (plural subject): alertam.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'This doesn't mean that walking solves the problem.'
questions.explanation: 'Não significa que' triggers the present subjunctive: resolva.

questions.prompt: Listen, then type the missing word: 'Os ___ analisaram os hábitos de várias pessoas durante seis meses.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Os investigadores analisaram os hábitos de várias pessoas durante seis meses.', which means 'The researchers analysed several people's habits over six months.'
questions.audioText: Os investigadores analisaram os hábitos de várias pessoas durante seis meses.

activities.title: I saw an odd news story
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend read a science headline that sounds too good to be true; explain what the study actually found and add a caution.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vi uma notícia que diz que comer chocolate todos os dias faz bem à memória!
lines.en: I saw a news story saying that eating chocolate every day is good for your memory!

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Calma, li o mesmo estudo. Os investigadores só analisaram um grupo pequeno.
lines.en: Wait, I read the same study. The researchers only analysed a small group.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ah, então talvez não seja assim tão simples.
lines.en: Ah, so maybe it's not that simple.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Exatamente. Eles revelaram uma ligação, mas não provaram a causa.
lines.en: Exactly. They revealed a link, but they didn't prove the cause.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E qual é a causa que eles sugerem?
lines.en: And what cause do they suggest?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Segundo os autores, pode estar ligada aos antioxidantes, mas não têm a certeza.
lines.en: According to the authors, it may be linked to antioxidants, but they're not sure.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então não vou mudar os meus hábitos por causa de uma notícia.
lines.en: So I'm not going to change my habits because of one news story.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Boa ideia. Isto não significa que o chocolate seja mau, só que é preciso mais estudos.
lines.en: Good idea. This doesn't mean chocolate is bad, just that more studies are needed.

days.title: Talking about a book: summarising and recommending
days.objective: Summarise a book's plot in the present tense, describe a character, and recommend it giving reasons.
days.paretoFocus: The literary present for plot summary and set recommendation phrases are reusable for any book, film or show a learner wants to talk about.
drills: Summarise the plot of a book you know in three present-tense sentences.
Describe one character's personality in one sentence.
Recommend the book giving one reason, starting with 'Recomendo porque...'

items: Recall why Portuguese uses the present tense even for a book you finished reading last year.
Say a sentence describing a character.
Say a recommendation sentence with a reason.

activities.title: The summary and the recommendation
activities.intro: When summarising a plot, Portuguese uses the present tense even for a book you already finished, and set phrases exist for describing characters and recommending.

items.hr: 'A Casa do Rio' conta a história de uma família que se muda para uma aldeia perto do Douro.
items.en: 'A Casa do Rio' tells the story of a family that moves to a village near the Douro.
items.note: the literary present, used even though the book is already written

items.hr: A personagem principal, Inês, é teimosa mas muito leal aos amigos.
items.en: The main character, Inês, is stubborn but very loyal to her friends.
items.note: describing personality with ser + adjective

items.hr: Ao longo da história, ela descobre segredos antigos sobre a sua família.
items.en: Throughout the story, she discovers old secrets about her family.
items.note: ao longo de = throughout

items.hr: O livro prende o leitor do início ao fim, sobretudo no último capítulo.
items.en: The book grips the reader from start to finish, especially in the last chapter.
items.note: prender o leitor = to grip the reader, common review phrase

items.hr: Recomendo este livro porque a escrita é simples e a história emociona sem ser previsível.
items.en: I recommend this book because the writing is simple and the story is moving without being predictable.
items.note: recomendo porque + reason

items.hr: Vale mesmo a pena ler.
items.en: It is really worth reading.
items.note: valer a pena is to be worth it.

items.hr: Não consegui pousar o livro.
items.en: I could not put the book down.

activities.title: Resumir e recomendar
activities.intro: Practise the literary present and the vocabulary for describing characters and recommending books.

questions.prompt: Which tense is normally used to summarise a book's plot?
questions.explanation: Plot summaries use the literary present, even for finished books.

questions.prompt: Which adjective best fits: 'A personagem é teimosa mas muito ___ aos amigos.' (loyal)
questions.explanation: 'Leal' means loyal; the other options are false friends or unrelated words.

questions.prompt: Ao longo da história, ela ___ segredos antigos sobre a família. (discovers)
questions.explanation: Present tense of descobrir for plot summary: descobre.

questions.prompt: ___ este livro porque a história emociona sem ser previsível. (I recommend)
questions.explanation: 'Recomendo' is the first-person present of recomendar, used to introduce a recommendation.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'The book grips the reader from start to finish.'
questions.explanation: 'Prender o leitor' is the set phrase for a gripping book.

questions.prompt: Listen and fill in the word you hear: 'A ___ principal, Inês, é teimosa mas muito leal aos amigos.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'A personagem principal, Inês, é teimosa mas muito leal aos amigos.', which means 'The main character, Inês, is stubborn but very loyal to her friends.'
questions.audioText: A personagem principal, Inês, é teimosa mas muito leal aos amigos.

activities.title: Have you read that book?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Recommend a book to a friend, summarising the plot and describing a character.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Andas a ler alguma coisa boa ultimamente?
lines.en: Are you reading anything good lately?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sim, 'A Casa do Rio'. Conta a história de uma família que se muda para uma aldeia.
lines.en: Yes, 'A Casa do Rio'. It tells the story of a family that moves to a village.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Parece interessante. Como é a personagem principal?
lines.en: Sounds interesting. What's the main character like?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A Inês é teimosa mas muito leal, e ao longo da história descobre segredos da família.
lines.en: Inês is stubborn but very loyal, and throughout the story she discovers family secrets.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E vale mesmo a pena ler até ao fim?
lines.en: And is it really worth reading to the end?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sem dúvida, o livro prende do início ao fim, sobretudo no último capítulo.
lines.en: No doubt, the book grips you from start to finish, especially in the last chapter.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então vou pedi-lo emprestado. Obrigada pela recomendação!
lines.en: Then I'll borrow it. Thanks for the recommendation!

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: De nada, recomendo porque a escrita é simples mas a história emociona.
lines.en: You're welcome, I recommend it because the writing is simple but the story is moving.

days.title: Museums and shows: a cultural outing
days.objective: Plan and describe a cultural outing (exhibitions, plays, concerts), buying tickets and sharing impressions afterwards.
days.paretoFocus: Cultural-outing vocabulary (bilhete, exposição, peça, plateia) covers planning, attending and reviewing any cultural event, a very common conversation topic.
drills: Plan a cultural outing in three sentences: what, when, and how you'll get tickets.
Describe what you see at an exhibition or show in two sentences.
Give your impression afterwards in one sentence.

items: Recall the pt-PT words for 'ticket', 'exhibition' and 'play'.
Say a sentence planning a cultural outing.
Say a sentence giving your impression of a show.

activities.title: A cultural outing
activities.intro: Vocabulary and phrases for planning a cultural outing, buying tickets, and sharing your impressions of an exhibition, play or concert afterwards.

items.hr: Vamos a uma exposição de fotografia no sábado, queres vir?
items.en: We're going to a photography exhibition on Saturday, do you want to come?
items.note: a exposição = exhibition

items.hr: É melhor comprar os bilhetes com antecedência, porque costuma esgotar.
items.en: It's better to buy the tickets in advance, because it usually sells out.
items.note: o bilhete = ticket; com antecedência = in advance

items.hr: A peça começa às nove, por isso convém chegar cedo para arranjar bons lugares.
items.en: The play starts at nine, so it's a good idea to arrive early to get good seats.
items.note: a peça = play; o lugar = seat

items.hr: O concerto foi ótimo, mas a plateia estava um bocadinho barulhenta.
items.en: The concert was great, but the audience was a bit noisy.
items.note: a plateia = the audience

items.hr: Gostei imenso da exposição, sobretudo das fotografias a preto e branco.
items.en: I really enjoyed the exhibition, especially the black and white photographs.
items.note: gostar imenso de = to really enjoy

activities.title: Tickets and impressions
activities.intro: Practise vocabulary for planning a cultural outing and describing your impressions afterwards.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'ticket' in Portuguese?
questions.explanation: 'O bilhete' is a ticket; 'o cartaz' is a poster.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: 'A ___ estava um bocadinho barulhenta durante o concerto.' (audience)
questions.explanation: 'A plateia' means the audience in a theatre or concert hall.

questions.prompt: É melhor comprar os bilhetes com ___, porque costuma esgotar. (in advance)
questions.explanation: 'Com antecedência' means in advance.

questions.prompt: A peça ___ às nove, por isso convém chegar cedo. (starts)
questions.explanation: Present tense of começar for a scheduled event: começa.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I really enjoyed the exhibition, especially the photographs.'
questions.explanation: 'Gostar imenso de' + noun to say you really enjoyed something.

questions.prompt: Play the audio and complete: 'Vamos a uma exposição de ___ no sábado, queres vir?'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Vamos a uma exposição de fotografia no sábado, queres vir?', which means 'We're going to a photography exhibition on Saturday, do you want to come?'
questions.audioText: Vamos a uma exposição de fotografia no sábado, queres vir?

activities.title: Shall we go to the exhibition?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Plan a cultural outing with a friend and share your impressions afterwards.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sabes que há uma exposição de fotografia no centro? Vamos no sábado?
lines.en: Did you know there's a photography exhibition downtown? Shall we go on Saturday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Boa ideia! É melhor comprar os bilhetes com antecedência, dizem que esgota depressa.
lines.en: Great idea! It's better to buy tickets in advance, they say it sells out fast.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Certo, compro já online. Depois podíamos ver aquela peça de teatro à noite.
lines.en: Right, I'll buy them online now. Afterwards we could see that play at night.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Boa, mas convém chegar cedo, assim conseguimos bons lugares.
lines.en: Good, but it's a good idea to arrive early, that way we get good seats.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então, o que achaste da exposição no fim?
lines.en: So, what did you think of the exhibition in the end?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Gostei imenso, sobretudo das fotografias a preto e branco.
lines.en: I really enjoyed it, especially the black and white photographs.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E a peça? A plateia estava cheia?
lines.en: And the play? Was the audience full?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Estava, mas um bocadinho barulhenta durante o intervalo.
lines.en: It was, but a bit noisy during the interval.

days.title: Understanding adverts and notices
days.objective: Extract key information from short public notices, classified ads and announcements, including common abbreviations.
days.paretoFocus: Classified ads and public notices are full of abbreviations (T2, c/, elev.) that block comprehension until decoded once.
drills: Read a short classified ad aloud and identify the price and key features.
Decode three abbreviations commonly found in Portuguese ads.
Write one short notice of your own using at least one abbreviation.

items: Recall what 'T2' and 'c/' mean in a housing ad.
Say the full form of one abbreviated word from an ad.
Recall two pieces of information you'd expect to find in a classified ad.

activities.title: Reading an advert
activities.intro: Public notices and classified ads use abbreviations to save space; learning the common ones (T2, c/, elev., inf.) unlocks quick, everyday reading.

items.hr: Aluga-se T2 c/ varanda, 3.º andar, elev., perto do metro. Inf.: 912 345 678.
items.en: T2 apartment for rent with balcony, 3rd floor, lift, near the metro. Info: 912 345 678.
items.note: T2 = two-bedroom flat; c/ = com (with); elev. = elevador; Inf. = informações

items.hr: Vende-se sofá, pouco uso, bom estado, entrega incluída.
items.en: Sofa for sale, lightly used, good condition, delivery included.
items.note: pouco uso = lightly used

items.hr: Aviso: obras na rua principal a partir de segunda-feira, trânsito condicionado.
items.en: Notice: roadworks on the main street from Monday, traffic restricted.
items.note: trânsito condicionado = restricted traffic

items.hr: Precisa-se de empregado de mesa c/ experiência, horário flexível.
items.en: Waiter needed with experience, flexible hours.
items.note: precisa-se de = wanted (job ad)

items.hr: Perdeu-se gato preto e branco, atende pelo nome de Mimi, últ. visto perto do parque.
items.en: Lost black and white cat, answers to the name Mimi, last seen near the park.
items.note: últ. = último, another common abbreviation

activities.title: Decoding adverts
activities.intro: Practise decoding abbreviations and extracting key information from notices and classified ads.

questions.prompt: In a housing ad, what does 'T2' mean?
questions.explanation: In Portuguese housing ads, T followed by a number indicates the number of bedrooms.

questions.prompt: What does 'c/' stand for in an ad?
questions.explanation: 'c/' is a common abbreviation for 'com' (with).

questions.prompt: 'Elev.' is an abbreviation for the pt-PT word for lift/elevator: ___.
questions.explanation: 'Elev.' abbreviates 'elevador'.

questions.prompt: Complete the ad: 'Precisa-se de empregado de mesa c/ ___, horário flexível.' (experience)
questions.explanation: 'Experiência' means experience; job ads often ask for it.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'Roadworks on the main street from Monday.'
questions.explanation: 'A partir de' means 'from' (a point in time onward), common in public notices.

questions.prompt: Listen closely and fill the gap: 'Aluga-se T2 c/ ___, 3.º andar, elev., perto do metro. Inf.: 912 345 678.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Aluga-se T2 c/ varanda, 3.º andar, elev., perto do metro. Inf.: 912 345 678.', which means 'T2 apartment for rent with balcony, 3rd floor, lift, near the metro. Info: 912 345 678.'
questions.audioText: Aluga-se T2 c/ varanda, 3.º andar, elev., perto do metro. Inf.: 912 345 678.

questions.prompt: Say it in Portuguese, in writing: 'Sofa for sale, lightly used, good condition, delivery included.'
questions.answer: Vende-se sofá, pouco uso, bom estado, entrega incluída.
questions.explanation: 'Sofa for sale, lightly used, good condition, delivery included.' is 'Vende-se sofá, pouco uso, bom estado, entrega incluída.'

activities.title: I saw an advert
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend saw a classified ad but doesn't understand the abbreviations; explain what they mean.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vi este anúncio: 'Aluga-se T2 c/ varanda, elev., perto do metro.' O que quer dizer T2?
lines.en: I saw this ad: 'T2 apartment for rent with balcony, lift, near the metro.' What does T2 mean?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: T2 é um apartamento com dois quartos. E 'c/' é só a abreviatura de 'com'.
lines.en: T2 is a two-bedroom flat. And 'c/' is just the abbreviation for 'with'.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ah, faz sentido. E 'elev.'? Percebi que é elevador, mas 'Inf.'?
lines.en: Ah, that makes sense. And 'elev.'? I got that it's lift, but 'Inf.'?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: 'Inf.' quer dizer 'informações', geralmente vem antes do número de telefone.
lines.en: 'Inf.' means 'information', it usually comes before the phone number.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ótimo, agora já consigo perceber estes anúncios sozinha.
lines.en: Great, now I can understand these ads on my own.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: É só uma questão de decorar as abreviaturas mais comuns.
lines.en: It's just a matter of memorising the most common abbreviations.

days.title: O e-mail formal: pedir informações
days.objective: Write a formal inquiry email using the standard frame: Exmos. Senhores, venho por este meio, agradeço desde já.
days.paretoFocus: This fixed formal-email frame is reusable for almost any inquiry a learner will ever need to send in Portuguese.
drills: Write the opening line of a formal email requesting information.
Write one sentence stating what information you need.
Write the closing line thanking in advance.

items: Recall the formal greeting for an email to an unknown recipient.
Recall the phrase meaning 'I am writing to...'
Recall the phrase meaning 'thank you in advance'.

activities.title: Asking for information by email
activities.intro: Formal Portuguese emails follow a fixed structure: a formal greeting, a phrase to introduce the request, the request itself, and a thank-you close.

items.hr: Exmos. Senhores,
items.en: Dear Sirs/Madams,
items.note: standard formal opening when you don't know the recipient's name

items.hr: Venho por este meio solicitar informações sobre os vossos horários de funcionamento.
items.en: I am writing to request information about your opening hours.
items.note: venho por este meio = I am writing hereby, fixed formal opener

items.hr: Gostaria de saber se é possível marcar uma visita durante a próxima semana.
items.en: I would like to know if it's possible to arrange a visit next week.
items.note: gostaria de saber se = polite way to ask a question

items.hr: Agradeço desde já a atenção dispensada e fico a aguardar a vossa resposta.
items.en: I thank you in advance for your attention and look forward to your reply.
items.note: agradeço desde já = thank you in advance, standard formal close

items.hr: Com os melhores cumprimentos,
items.en: Best regards,
items.note: standard formal sign-off before the name

activities.title: The structure of a formal email
activities.intro: Practise the fixed phrases used to open, request and close a formal inquiry email.

questions.prompt: Which greeting is correct for a formal email to an unknown recipient?
questions.explanation: 'Exmos. Senhores' is the standard formal greeting when you don't know who will read the email.

questions.prompt: Which phrase best introduces the purpose of a formal inquiry email?
questions.explanation: 'Venho por este meio' is the fixed formal phrase for stating the purpose of the email.

questions.prompt: Complete the closing: 'Agradeço desde já a atenção ___.' (given/paid)
questions.explanation: 'A atenção dispensada' is a fixed formal phrase meaning 'the attention given'.

questions.prompt: Gostaria de ___ se é possível marcar uma visita. (to know)
questions.explanation: 'Gostaria de saber se' is a polite way to ask a yes/no question formally.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I am writing to request information about your opening hours.'
questions.explanation: 'Venho por este meio solicitar' + noun is the fixed formal way to request information.

questions.prompt: Type the word you hear: 'Venho por este meio solicitar informações sobre os vossos horários de ___.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Venho por este meio solicitar informações sobre os vossos horários de funcionamento.', which means 'I am writing to request information about your opening hours.'
questions.audioText: Venho por este meio solicitar informações sobre os vossos horários de funcionamento.

activities.title: Helping to write the email
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend is helping you draft a formal inquiry email; confirm the right formal phrases together.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Como é que começas um e-mail formal quando não sabes o nome da pessoa?
lines.en: How do you start a formal email when you don't know the person's name?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Começo com 'Exmos. Senhores,' e depois explico logo o motivo.
lines.en: I start with 'Exmos. Senhores,' and then I explain the reason right away.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E como pedes a informação, sem parecer maleducado?
lines.en: And how do you ask for the information, without seeming rude?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Escrevo 'Venho por este meio solicitar informações sobre os horários'.
lines.en: I write 'I am writing to request information about the hours'.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E no fim? Como fechas o e-mail?
lines.en: And at the end? How do you close the email?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Agradeço desde já a atenção dispensada, e assino com 'Com os melhores cumprimentos'.
lines.en: I thank them in advance for their attention, and sign off with 'Best regards'.

days.title: The letter of complaint
days.objective: Write a formal complaint letter that states the facts in order, explains what went wrong and politely demands a concrete remedy.
days.paretoFocus: A clear facts-problem-remedy structure is what makes any complaint effective and taken seriously in formal Portuguese.
drills: State one fact of a complaint in chronological order.
Say what went wrong in one sentence.
Demand a concrete remedy politely using 'solicito que'.

items: Recall the three parts of a complaint letter: facts, problem, remedy.
Recall a polite phrase for demanding a remedy.
Say a sentence stating what went wrong with an order.

activities.title: Reclamar por escrito
activities.intro: A formal complaint opens with a short summary of what happened, then lays out each fact chronologically, explains clearly what went wrong, and ends with a polite but concrete demand for a remedy, often using solicito que + subjunctive.

items.hr: No dia 10 de março, encomendei um casaco à empresa Lãzul, com entrega prevista para uma semana depois.
items.en: On March 10th, I ordered a coat from the Lãzul company, with delivery expected a week later.
items.note: sets the facts in chronological order; Lãzul is a fictional company

items.hr: Passaram três semanas e a encomenda ainda não chegou.
items.en: Three weeks passed and the order still hasn't arrived.
items.note: states what went wrong clearly and factually

items.hr: Quando finalmente chegou, o casaco vinha com um rasgão na manga.
items.en: When it finally arrived, the coat had a tear in the sleeve.
items.note: second problem, adds detail

items.hr: Solicito que me seja devolvido o valor pago ou enviado um artigo em bom estado.
items.en: I request that the amount paid be refunded to me or a replacement item in good condition be sent.
items.note: solicito que + present subjunctive (seja) for a polite formal demand

items.hr: Aguardo uma resposta num prazo razoável, caso contrário terei de reportar a situação.
items.en: I await a response within a reasonable time, otherwise I will have to report the situation.
items.note: polite but firm closing

items.hr: Venho por este meio reclamar.
items.en: I am writing to make a complaint.
items.note: Venho por este meio is the standard opening of a formal complaint.

items.hr: Aguardo a vossa resposta.
items.en: I await your reply.

activities.title: Writing a complaint
activities.intro: Practise the structure and polite demand phrases used in a formal complaint letter.

questions.prompt: What should a formal complaint letter present first?
options: a joke to soften the tone
questions.explanation: A formal complaint starts with a clear, ordered account of the facts before stating the problem.

questions.prompt: Which phrase makes a polite formal demand?
questions.explanation: 'Solicito que' + subjunctive is the standard polite formal way to demand a remedy.

questions.prompt: Solicito que me ___ o valor pago. (be refunded)
questions.explanation: 'Solicito que' + present subjunctive passive: seja devolvido.

questions.prompt: Passaram três semanas e a encomenda ainda não ___. (arrived)
questions.explanation: Pretérito perfeito to state a completed fact: chegou.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'When it finally arrived, the coat had a tear in the sleeve.'
questions.explanation: 'Vinha com' (imperfeito) describes the state the item arrived in.

questions.prompt: Listen and complete the sentence: 'Passaram três semanas e a ___ ainda não chegou.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Passaram três semanas e a encomenda ainda não chegou.', which means 'Three weeks passed and the order still hasn't arrived.'
questions.audioText: Passaram três semanas e a encomenda ainda não chegou.

activities.title: I am going to write a complaint
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Tell a friend about a problem with an order and how you plan to demand a remedy politely.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então, o que aconteceu com a tua encomenda?
lines.en: So, what happened with your order?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Encomendei um casaco no dia 10 e passaram três semanas sem chegar.
lines.en: I ordered a coat on the 10th and three weeks passed without it arriving.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: A sério? E quando chegou, estava tudo bem?
lines.en: Really? And when it arrived, was everything okay?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não, vinha com um rasgão na manga. Por isso vou escrever uma reclamação.
lines.en: No, it had a tear in the sleeve. So I'm going to write a complaint.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa. E o que vais pedir?
lines.en: Good. And what are you going to ask for?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vou solicitar que me devolvam o dinheiro ou enviem outro em bom estado.
lines.en: I'm going to request that they refund my money or send another one in good condition.

days.title: Summarising a text in your own words
days.objective: Reduce a short text to its essential points in your own words, without copying its sentences.
days.paretoFocus: Paraphrasing with synonyms and nominalisation is the core skill behind every summary, from exam tasks to everyday retelling.
drills: Read a short text and identify its two or three main points.
Rewrite one sentence from the text using a synonym for the key verb.
Summarise the text in two sentences of your own.

items: Recall two techniques for paraphrasing: synonyms and nominalisation.
Say a synonym for 'aumentar'.
Say a two-sentence summary of any short text you know.

activities.title: Summarising without copying
activities.intro: Summarising well means picking out the main points and rephrasing them with synonyms or nominalisation, not repeating the original sentences.

items.hr: Texto original: 'O número de pessoas que trabalha a partir de casa aumentou significativamente nos últimos anos.'
items.en: Original text: 'The number of people working from home has increased significantly in recent years.'
items.note: the source sentence to be paraphrased

items.hr: Resumo: 'O trabalho remoto cresceu muito recentemente.'
items.en: Summary: 'Remote work has grown a lot recently.'
items.note: nominalisation: 'pessoas que trabalha a partir de casa' becomes 'trabalho remoto'

items.hr: Em vez de repetir 'aumentou', podemos usar 'cresceu' ou 'subiu'.
items.en: Instead of repeating 'increased', we can use 'grew' or 'went up'.
items.note: synonym substitution keeps meaning without copying

items.hr: Um bom resumo mantém as ideias principais e deixa de fora os exemplos e os detalhes.
items.en: A good summary keeps the main ideas and leaves out the examples and details.
items.note: core rule of summarising

items.hr: Por outras palavras, o texto defende que trabalhar de casa trouxe mais liberdade, mas também mais isolamento.
items.en: In other words, the text argues that working from home brought more freedom, but also more isolation.
items.note: por outras palavras = in other words, useful summary connector

items.hr: Por outras palavras, cresceu muito.
items.en: In other words, it grew a lot.

items.hr: O essencial é manter as ideias principais.
items.en: The key is to keep the main ideas.

activities.title: Parafrasear e resumir
activities.intro: Practise choosing synonyms and rewording sentences without copying the original.

questions.prompt: What should a good summary avoid?
questions.explanation: A summary must reword the text, not copy its sentences.

questions.prompt: Which is a good synonym for 'aumentou' in a summary?
questions.explanation: 'Cresceu' means 'grew', a synonym for 'aumentou' (increased); the others mean the opposite or unrelated things.

questions.prompt: ___ palavras, o texto defende que o trabalho remoto trouxe mais liberdade. (In other)
questions.explanation: 'Por outras palavras' means 'in other words', a common summary connector.

questions.prompt: Um bom resumo mantém as ideias principais e deixa ___ os detalhes. (leaves out)
questions.explanation: 'Deixar de fora' means 'to leave out'.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'Remote work has grown a lot recently.'
questions.explanation: A concise, paraphrased summary sentence using 'cresceu' instead of repeating 'aumentou'.

questions.prompt: Listen, then type the missing word: 'Resumo: 'O trabalho remoto cresceu muito ___.''
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Resumo: 'O trabalho remoto cresceu muito recentemente.'', which means 'Summary: 'Remote work has grown a lot recently.''
questions.audioText: Resumo: 'O trabalho remoto cresceu muito recentemente.'

activities.title: Can you summarise this?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Help a friend summarise a short text in their own words instead of copying it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tenho de resumir este texto sobre o trabalho remoto, mas só copio as frases todas.
lines.en: I have to summarise this text about remote work, but I just copy all the sentences.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não podes copiar, tens de usar as tuas próprias palavras.
lines.en: You can't copy, you have to use your own words.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Mas como troco 'aumentou significativamente' sem mudar o sentido?
lines.en: But how do I change 'increased significantly' without changing the meaning?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Podes dizer 'cresceu muito', é um sinónimo mais simples.
lines.en: You can say 'grew a lot', it's a simpler synonym.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E os exemplos do texto, ponho todos no resumo?
lines.en: And the examples in the text, do I put them all in the summary?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Não, um bom resumo deixa os exemplos de fora e mantém só as ideias principais.
lines.en: No, a good summary leaves the examples out and keeps only the main ideas.

days.title: Writing an account: a memorable experience
days.objective: Write a structured past-tense narrative of a personal experience, organised into paragraphs with time connectors.
days.paretoFocus: Time connectors (primeiro, entretanto, por fim) turn a list of past events into a narrative a reader can actually follow.
drills: Tell a memorable experience in three sentences using primeiro, depois and por fim.
Add one sentence of background using the imperfeito.
Write a closing sentence saying what you learned or felt.

items: Recall three time connectors: primeiro, entretanto, por fim.
Say a sentence in the imperfeito describing background circumstances.
Say a closing sentence about a memorable experience.

activities.title: Telling a memorable experience
activities.intro: A structured narrative uses the pretérito perfeito for the main events, the imperfeito for background, and time connectors (primeiro, entretanto, por fim) to link paragraphs.

items.hr: Primeiro, era uma manhã de inverno e chovia muito quando saí de casa.
items.en: First, it was a winter morning and it was raining hard when I left home.
items.note: imperfeito (era, chovia) sets the background scene

items.hr: De repente, o autocarro travou a fundo e todos os passageiros caíram para a frente.
items.en: Suddenly, the bus braked hard and all the passengers fell forward.
items.note: pretérito perfeito for the sudden main event

items.hr: Entretanto, uma senhora ajudou-me a levantar e perguntou se eu estava bem.
items.en: Meanwhile, a lady helped me get up and asked if I was okay.
items.note: entretanto = meanwhile, links the next part of the story

items.hr: No fim, trocámos números de telefone e tornámo-nos amigas.
items.en: In the end, we exchanged phone numbers and became friends.
items.note: no fim = in the end, marks the conclusion

items.hr: Por fim, percebi que até os dias mais estranhos podem trazer coisas boas.
items.en: Finally, I realised that even the strangest days can bring good things.
items.note: por fim = finally, the closing reflection

activities.title: Linking the events
activities.intro: Practise the time connectors and past tenses used to structure a personal narrative.

questions.prompt: Which connector best introduces the background of a story?
questions.explanation: 'Primeiro' introduces the opening scene or background of a narrative.

questions.prompt: Which tense sets the background scene ('it was raining') in a narrative?
questions.explanation: The imperfeito describes ongoing background circumstances, like the weather.

questions.prompt: ___, uma senhora ajudou-me a levantar. (Meanwhile)
questions.explanation: 'Entretanto' means 'meanwhile', linking a new part of the story.

questions.prompt: De repente, o autocarro ___ a fundo. (braked)
questions.explanation: Pretérito perfeito for a sudden completed action: travou.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'Finally, I realised that even the strangest days can bring good things.'
questions.explanation: 'Por fim' closes the narrative with a reflection, using the pretérito perfeito (percebi) and present (podem) for a general truth.

questions.prompt: Listen and fill in the word you hear: 'No fim, ___ números de telefone e tornámo-nos amigas.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'No fim, trocámos números de telefone e tornámo-nos amigas.', which means 'In the end, we exchanged phone numbers and became friends.'
questions.audioText: No fim, trocámos números de telefone e tornámo-nos amigas.

activities.title: A different kind of morning
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Tell a friend about a memorable experience, using time connectors to structure the story.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Contas-me lá essa história do autocarro que mencionaste?
lines.en: Will you tell me that bus story you mentioned?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro. Primeiro, era uma manhã de inverno e chovia muito quando saí de casa.
lines.en: Sure. First, it was a winter morning and it was raining hard when I left home.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E depois? O que aconteceu?
lines.en: And then? What happened?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: De repente, o autocarro travou a fundo e caí quase ao chão.
lines.en: Suddenly, the bus braked hard and I nearly fell to the floor.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Que susto! Alguém te ajudou?
lines.en: What a fright! Did anyone help you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sim, entretanto uma senhora ajudou-me, e por fim ficámos amigas.
lines.en: Yes, meanwhile a lady helped me, and in the end we became friends.

days.title: Describing an image: what you see and what it looks like
days.objective: Describe a photo systematically using spatial expressions and speculate about it using parece que and talvez.
days.paretoFocus: Spatial markers (em primeiro plano, à esquerda) and speculation phrases (parece que, talvez seja) are exactly what oral exams and picture-description tasks require.
drills: Describe a photo you have using em primeiro plano and ao fundo.
Say what's on the left and on the right of an image.
Speculate about what's happening in the photo using talvez.

items: Recall three spatial expressions: em primeiro plano, à esquerda, ao fundo.
Say a speculation sentence starting with 'Parece que...'
Say a speculation sentence starting with 'Talvez...' with the subjunctive.

activities.title: Describing and speculating about an image
activities.intro: A systematic image description moves through spatial zones (foreground, sides, background) before speculating about the scene with parece que and talvez + subjunctive.

items.hr: Em primeiro plano, vê-se uma mulher a ler um livro num banco de jardim.
items.en: In the foreground, you can see a woman reading a book on a park bench.
items.note: em primeiro plano = in the foreground

items.hr: À esquerda, há uma criança a brincar com um cão.
items.en: On the left, there's a child playing with a dog.
items.note: à esquerda = on the left

items.hr: Ao fundo, distinguem-se algumas árvores e o que parece ser um lago.
items.en: In the background, some trees and what looks like a lake can be made out.
items.note: ao fundo = in the background; o que parece ser = what looks like

items.hr: Parece que é um dia de verão, porque toda a gente está com roupa leve.
items.en: It looks like it's a summer's day, because everyone is wearing light clothes.
items.note: parece que + indicative, when fairly confident

items.hr: Talvez seja um domingo, porque o parque está cheio de famílias.
items.en: It might be a Sunday, because the park is full of families.
items.note: talvez + present subjunctive (seja) expresses a guess

activities.title: What you see and what it seems
activities.intro: Practise spatial expressions for describing an image and phrases for speculating about it.

questions.prompt: Which expression means 'in the foreground'?
questions.explanation: 'Em primeiro plano' refers to the front part of an image.

questions.prompt: Which word requires the subjunctive when speculating?
questions.explanation: 'Talvez' before the verb triggers the subjunctive (seja); the others take the indicative.

questions.prompt: Ao fundo, ___ algumas árvores e um lago. (can be made out)
questions.explanation: Reflexive/passive construction, present tense agreeing with 'árvores' (plural): distinguem-se.

questions.prompt: Talvez ___ um domingo, porque o parque está cheio de famílias. (be)
questions.explanation: 'Talvez' + present subjunctive of ser: seja.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'On the left, there's a child playing with a dog.'
questions.explanation: 'À esquerda' + 'há' introduces what's on the left side of the image.

questions.prompt: Play the audio and complete: 'À ___, há uma criança a brincar com um cão.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'À esquerda, há uma criança a brincar com um cão.', which means 'On the left, there's a child playing with a dog.'
questions.audioText: À esquerda, há uma criança a brincar com um cão.

activities.title: What do you make of this photo?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Describe a photo systematically and speculate about what's happening in it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Olha esta foto que encontrei, o que se vê nela?
lines.en: Look at this photo I found, what can you see in it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Em primeiro plano, há uma mulher a ler um livro num banco de jardim.
lines.en: In the foreground, there's a woman reading a book on a park bench.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: E à volta dela, o que mais se vê?
lines.en: And around her, what else can be seen?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: À esquerda, uma criança brinca com um cão, e ao fundo há um lago.
lines.en: On the left, a child is playing with a dog, and in the background there's a lake.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Achas que é verão? Que dia parece ser?
lines.en: Do you think it's summer? What day does it seem to be?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Parece que sim, e talvez seja domingo, porque o parque está cheio de famílias.
lines.en: It looks like it, and it might be Sunday, because the park is full of families.

days.title: The weather forecast: understanding the bulletin
days.objective: Understand a weather forecast and pass on its key points, using the future tense.
days.paretoFocus: Weather-forecast vocabulary and the future tense let a learner both understand and relay one of the most common everyday broadcasts.
drills: Listen to or read a short forecast and identify tomorrow's temperature.
Relay one detail of a forecast to someone else, using the future tense.
Say a sentence recommending what to bring based on the forecast.

items: Recall the pt-PT words for 'aguaceiros' and 'vento'.
Say a sentence in the future tense about tomorrow's weather.
Say a sentence recommending what to take based on a forecast.

activities.title: The weather bulletin
activities.intro: Weather forecasts use the future tense (soprará, subirão, haverá) and specific vocabulary for wind, rain and temperature that's worth learning as a set.

items.hr: Amanhã de manhã, o céu estará muito nublado no litoral.
items.en: Tomorrow morning, the sky will be very cloudy on the coast.
items.note: estará = future of estar, common in forecasts

items.hr: O vento soprará forte a partir do meio-dia, sobretudo no norte.
items.en: The wind will blow strongly from midday, especially in the north.
items.note: soprar = to blow (wind)

items.hr: Haverá aguaceiros dispersos durante a tarde, com possibilidade de trovoada.
items.en: There will be scattered showers during the afternoon, with a chance of thunder.
items.note: o aguaceiro = shower; a trovoada = thunderstorm

items.hr: As temperaturas irão descer ligeiramente, não ultrapassando os dezoito graus.
items.en: Temperatures will drop slightly, not exceeding eighteen degrees.
items.note: ir + infinitive, an alternative future form

items.hr: Por isso, é melhor levar guarda-chuva e um casaco mais quente.
items.en: So, it's better to bring an umbrella and a warmer coat.
items.note: practical advice based on the forecast

activities.title: Understanding and passing on the forecast
activities.intro: Practise the future tense and vocabulary needed to understand and relay a weather forecast.

questions.prompt: Which verb means 'to blow' (of the wind)?
questions.explanation: 'Soprar' means 'to blow', used for wind in forecasts.

questions.prompt: What is 'um aguaceiro'?
questions.explanation: 'Um aguaceiro' is a shower, brief rain, common forecast vocabulary.

questions.prompt: O vento ___ forte a partir do meio-dia. (will blow)
questions.explanation: Futuro simples of soprar: soprará, typical of forecast language.

questions.prompt: As temperaturas ___ ligeiramente amanhã. (will drop)
questions.explanation: Either 'irão descer' (ir + infinitive) or the simple future 'descerão' works for forecasts.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'There will be scattered showers during the afternoon.'
questions.explanation: 'Haverá' (future of haver) is used impersonally to announce weather events.

questions.prompt: Listen closely and fill the gap: 'Amanhã de manhã, o céu estará muito ___ no litoral.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Amanhã de manhã, o céu estará muito nublado no litoral.', which means 'Tomorrow morning, the sky will be very cloudy on the coast.'
questions.audioText: Amanhã de manhã, o céu estará muito nublado no litoral.

activities.title: Do you think it will rain?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend asks about tomorrow's weather; relay the forecast using the future tense.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Viste a previsão para amanhã? Vamos fazer aquele passeio.
lines.en: Did you see the forecast for tomorrow? We're going on that walk.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vi, o céu estará muito nublado de manhã, e o vento soprará forte à tarde.
lines.en: I did, the sky will be very cloudy in the morning, and the wind will blow hard in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Achas que vai chover?
lines.en: Do you think it'll rain?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Haverá aguaceiros dispersos, com possibilidade de trovoada.
lines.en: There will be scattered showers, with a chance of thunder.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então talvez seja melhor adiar o passeio.
lines.en: So maybe it's better to postpone the walk.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Talvez, mas as temperaturas irão descer só um pouco, ainda dá para andar com casaco.
lines.en: Maybe, but temperatures will only drop a little, we can still go with a coat.

days.title: Hearing European Portuguese: the vowels that disappear
days.objective: Decode fast European Portuguese speech by expecting reduced vowels and swallowed syllables.
days.paretoFocus: European Portuguese drops unstressed vowels so consistently that recognising the pattern once unlocks understanding of natural spoken speech.
drills: Say three everyday phrases aloud with reduced vowels, the way natives actually speak.
Listen to yourself saying 'está' as 'tá' and 'para' as 'pra'.
Identify the full form behind three reduced spoken forms.

items: Recall the full form behind 'tá', 'pra' and 'ps'.
Say one sentence with reduced vowels the way it's actually pronounced.
Recall why unstressed vowels tend to disappear in European Portuguese.

activities.title: The vowels that disappear
activities.intro: In fast European Portuguese, unstressed vowels are often swallowed almost completely, so words shrink in speech even though they're spelled in full.

items.hr: Pois, está excelente.
items.en: Yes, that is excellent.
items.note: In fast speech this becomes Ps, tá xcelente: pois shrinks to ps, está to tá, and the unstressed initial e of excelente disappears.

items.hr: 'Para onde vais?' soa muitas vezes como 'Pr'onde vais?' na fala corrente.
items.en: 'Where are you going?' often sounds like 'Pr'onde vais?' in everyday speech.
items.note: para -> pr(a), the vowel merges with the next word

items.hr: 'Não sei' pode soar quase como 'nsei', muito rápido e ligado.
items.en: 'I don't know' can sound almost like 'nsei', very quick and run together.
items.note: unstressed 'ão' and 'e' compress in fast speech

items.hr: 'Se calhar', que significa 'talvez', costuma soar como 'skalhar'.
items.en: 'Se calhar', which means 'maybe', usually sounds like 'skalhar'.
items.note: se calhar = maybe, a very common spoken filler

items.hr: É por isso que ouvir português europeu exige esperar sílabas mais curtas do que na escrita.
items.en: That's why listening to European Portuguese requires expecting shorter syllables than in writing.
items.note: the key listening strategy for this lesson

activities.title: Decoding fast speech
activities.intro: Practise recognising reduced spoken forms and matching them to their full written forms.

questions.prompt: In fast European Portuguese speech, 'está' commonly sounds like:
questions.explanation: The unstressed initial syllable of 'está' is typically swallowed, leaving 'tá'.

questions.prompt: 'Se calhar' means:
questions.explanation: 'Se calhar' is a very common spoken way of saying 'maybe', even though it literally means 'if it happens'.

questions.prompt: The reduced spoken form 'ps' stands for the full written word ___.
questions.explanation: 'Pois' is often reduced to just 'ps' in fast speech.

questions.prompt: The full form behind the fast spoken 'pr'onde vais' is '___ onde vais'.
questions.explanation: 'Para' loses its final vowel and merges with the next word: 'pr'onde'.

questions.prompt: Build the full written Portuguese for the fast spoken 'skalhar inda nsei': 'Maybe I still don't know.'
questions.explanation: 'Skalhar inda nsei' expands to 'Se calhar ainda não sei' once the swallowed vowels are restored.

questions.prompt: Type the word you hear: 'Na escrita: 'Pois, está ___.' Na fala rápida: 'Ps, tá xcelente.''
questions.explanation: The audio says 'Na escrita: 'Pois, está excelente.' Na fala rápida: 'Ps, tá xcelente.'', which means 'In writing: 'Yes, it's excellent.' In fast speech: 'Ps, tá xcelente.''
questions.audioText: Na escrita: 'Pois, está excelente.' Na fala rápida: 'Ps, tá xcelente.'

questions.prompt: Write it in Portuguese: ''Se calhar', which means 'maybe', usually sounds like 'skalhar'.'
questions.answer: 'Se calhar', que significa 'talvez', costuma soar como 'skalhar'.
questions.explanation: ''Se calhar', which means 'maybe', usually sounds like 'skalhar'.' is ''Se calhar', que significa 'talvez', costuma soar como 'skalhar'.'

activities.title: I did not catch any of that!
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend who is a slower listener didn't catch a fast sentence; slow it down and explain the reduced forms.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ela disse 'ps, tá xcelente' e eu não percebi nada!
lines.en: She said 'ps, tá xcelente' and I didn't understand anything!

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Calma, é só a fala rápida. 'Ps' quer dizer 'pois' e 'tá' é 'está'.
lines.en: Relax, it's just fast speech. 'Ps' means 'pois' and 'tá' is 'está'.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ah! E aquele 'skalhar' que ouço sempre?
lines.en: Ah! And that 'skalhar' I always hear?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Isso é 'se calhar', que significa 'talvez'.
lines.en: That's 'se calhar', which means 'maybe'.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Então é por isso que nunca percebo os diálogos rápidos.
lines.en: So that's why I never understand fast dialogues.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sim, é só uma questão de hábito: as vogais desaparecem na fala rápida.
lines.en: Yes, it's just a matter of habit: the vowels disappear in fast speech.

days.title: Taking notes as you listen: names, numbers and dates
days.objective: Catch and note down spelled names, phone numbers, prices and dates from spoken messages, using the Portuguese spelling alphabet.
days.paretoFocus: The Portuguese spelling alphabet and quick note-taking for numbers and dates are essential for real phone calls, appointments and messages.
drills: Practise spelling your own name aloud, letter by letter, the way a native speaker would over the phone.
Note down a phone number and a date from a short recorded message.
Write down a price you hear spoken aloud in euros.

items: Recall the code words for three tricky letters, like the ones easily confused over a bad phone line.
Say a phone number aloud in pairs of digits, the natural pt-PT way.
Recall the order for saying a date aloud in Portuguese.

activities.title: Soletrar e anotar
activities.intro: To avoid mishearing names over the phone, Portuguese speakers often spell them out letter by letter using a word for each letter; numbers are usually said in pairs, and dates in day-month-year order.

items.hr: Chamo-me Bárbara, com B de Braga, A, R, B de Braga outra vez, A, R, A.
items.en: My name is Bárbara, with B for Braga, A, R, B for Braga again, A, R, A.
items.note: spelling a name using a city word per letter is a common pt-PT strategy

items.hr: O meu número é novecentos e doze, trinta e quatro, cinquenta e seis.
items.en: My number is nine hundred twelve, thirty-four, fifty-six.
items.note: phone numbers are usually said in pairs after the first three digits

items.hr: A consulta ficou marcada para o dia dois de março.
items.en: The appointment was set for the second of March.
items.note: dates are said day then month in Portuguese

items.hr: O total ficou em trinta e sete euros e cinquenta cêntimos.
items.en: The total came to thirty-seven euros and fifty cents.
items.note: prices: euros then cêntimos

items.hr: Pode repetir o número, se faz favor? Não apanhei bem o último algarismo.
items.en: Could you repeat the number, please? I didn't quite catch the last digit.
items.note: a useful clarification phrase when taking notes

activities.title: Noting down what you hear
activities.intro: Practise writing down exactly what you hear in a short recording, then compare your notes to the transcript to catch anything you missed.

questions.prompt: How are Portuguese phone numbers usually grouped when spoken aloud, after the first three digits?
questions.explanation: After the first three digits, Portuguese phone numbers are typically said two digits at a time.

questions.prompt: In pt-PT, a date like '2 de março' is said in which order?
questions.explanation: Portuguese dates are said day first, then month, unlike the English month-first order.

questions.prompt: Polite phrase to ask someone to repeat a number: 'Pode ___ o número, se faz favor?'
questions.explanation: 'Repetir' means to repeat, the key verb for asking someone to say a number again.

questions.prompt: 'O total ficou em trinta e sete euros e cinquenta ___.' (cents)
questions.explanation: 'Cêntimos' is the pt-PT word for cents.

questions.prompt: Build the Portuguese for: 'I didn't quite catch the last digit.'
questions.explanation: 'Apanhar' here means 'to catch' (understand), and 'o algarismo' means digit.

questions.prompt: Listen and complete the sentence: 'A ___ ficou marcada para o dia dois de março.'
questions.explanation: The audio says 'A consulta ficou marcada para o dia dois de março.', which means 'The appointment was set for the second of March.'
questions.audioText: A consulta ficou marcada para o dia dois de março.

activities.title: Pode soletrar, por favor?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Take down a caller's name, phone number and appointment date accurately.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Boa tarde, queria marcar uma consulta, o meu nome é Bárbara.
lines.en: Good afternoon, I'd like to book an appointment, my name is Bárbara.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pode soletrar o nome, se faz favor?
lines.en: Could you spell the name, please?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Claro, B de Braga, A, R, B de Braga outra vez, A, R, A.
lines.en: Sure, B for Braga, A, R, B for Braga again, A, R, A.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bárbara, anotado. E o seu número de telefone?
lines.en: Bárbara, noted. And your phone number?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Novecentos e doze, trinta e quatro, cinquenta e seis.
lines.en: Nine hundred twelve, thirty-four, fifty-six.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pode repetir o último algarismo? Não apanhei bem.
lines.en: Could you repeat the last digit? I didn't quite catch it.

lines.hr: Seis. E fico com a consulta marcada para quando?
